items.item: Review reference list: works on plasmon loss, lifetime and mobility (Cui, Wang, Sun 2021)
items.value: The review has 198 references. Those on this topic: Morozov 2008 [32], Du 2008 [19], Park 2008 [20], Levitov & Falkovich 2016 [34], Low & Avouris 2014 [38], Fei 2012 [52], Chen 2012 [53], Koppens 2011 [60], Tan 2007 [68], Jablan 2009 [76], Hwang & Das Sarma 2007 [78], Grigorenko 2012 [83], Ju 2011 [87], Ni 2018 [146], Song 2018 (News & Views) [147], Dai 2015 [148], Kumar 2015 [149], Woessner 2015 [150], Alcaraz Iranzo 2018 [151], Osborne 2017 (editor's summary of Lundeberg 2017) [152], Brar 2014 [153], Dean 2010 [161]. All date from 2007–2018. Every measured plasmon-damping figure among them is mid-IR. The one exception is Ju 2011: THz absorption peaks of CVD-graphene micro-ribbons at RT, with no Q given in the abstract. None reports a 1-THz damping time under a metal gate. Alonso-González 2017 and Lundeberg 2017 are not cited.
items.source_title: Crossref deposit for Cui, Wang, Sun, 'Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics', Rev. Phys. 6, 100054 (2021)
items.note: The review's full text sits behind a bot check and was not read. The reference list comes from Crossref. Ju 2011 abstract via PubMed 21892164.

items.item: Best exfoliated hBN/graphene/hBN device: room-temperature mobility vs density (Wang et al. 2013, Fig. 3B)
items.value: At 300 K, μ ≈ 90,500 cm²/Vs at n = 1.0×10¹² cm⁻² (95,500 at 0.9 and 85,600 at 1.1×10¹²). The 140,000 peak occurs only at n ≈ 0.1–0.3×10¹². The plotted acoustic-phonon model gives ≈121,000 at 10¹² (μ·n ≈ constant, so ρ_ph ≈ 52 Ω), and the device reaches that model only at n ≳ 2.5×10¹². The text says 'room-temperature mobility up to 140,000 cm2/Vs' and quotes ~40,000 cm²/Vs with ρ < ~40 Ω at 4.5×10¹². The figure shows ≈31,400 at 4.4×10¹².
items.source_title: L. Wang et al., 'One-dimensional electrical contact to a two-dimensional material', Science 342, 614–617 (2013) (Part I ref. [33])
items.note: Values digitized from Fig. 3B against detected axis ticks, about ±5%. Derived: τ = μE_F/(e v_F²) = 9.05 m²/Vs × 0.1167 V / 10¹² m²s⁻² = 1.06 ps, so Q = 2π×10¹²×1.06 ps = 6.6 and the λp/2 gate loss is 13.65/6.6 = 2.06 dB. Part I §4 reads the 140,000 as 'near the acoustic-phonon limit'. That pairs a low-density peak with a high-density behaviour.

items.item: Derived: lifetime vs density in the best room-temperature device, τ(n) = μ(n)E_F(n)/(e v_F²)
items.value: From Wang 2013 Fig. 3B: τ = 1.01 ps at 0.5×10¹², 1.04 at 0.8, 1.06 at 0.9–1.0, 1.05 at 1.1, 1.02 at 1.5, 0.98 at 2.0, 0.85 at 3.0, 0.80 at 4.0 and 0.77 ps at 4.4×10¹² cm⁻². n = 10¹² sits at the maximum of τ. Lowering n raises μ but does not lengthen τ, because E_F ∝ √n.
items.source_title: Derived from Wang et al., Science 342, 614 (2013), Fig. 3B
items.note: Arithmetic: E_F(n) = 116.7 meV × √(n/10¹²). Example at n = 0.5×10¹²: 12.25 m²/Vs × 0.0825 V / 10¹² = 1.01 ps. Assumes v_F = 10⁶ m/s at every density, with no renormalization.

items.item: Second best-device dataset: room-temperature mobility at n = ±10¹² (Purdie et al. 2018, Fig. 7b)
items.value: At 290 K, μ ≈ 80,000 cm²/Vs at n = +1×10¹² (electrons) and ≈103,000 at −1×10¹² (holes). The peak is ≈173,000 near −0.15×10¹². The abstract gives 'up to 180,000 cm2 V−1 s−1 at room temperature', and the text gives an average of ~160,000 across 15 Hall bars, both peak values.
items.source_title: D. G. Purdie et al., 'Cleaning interfaces in layered materials heterostructures', Nat. Commun. 9, 5387 (2018)
items.note: Digitized against the detected plot frame. Derived: τ = 8.0×0.1167/10¹² = 0.93 ps for electrons (Q 5.9, 2.32 dB per gate) and 10.3×0.1167/10¹² = 1.20 ps for holes (Q 7.5, 1.81 dB per gate).

items.item: Derived: DC-transport lifetime envelope at n = 10¹², 290–300 K (exfoliated hBN/G/hBN)
items.value: τ = 0.93–1.20 ps (Q 5.9–7.5; 2.3–1.8 dB per λp/2 gate) across the two best published datasets. Part I's row, τ = 1.0 ps (μ ≈ 86,000, Q 6.3, 2.17 dB), lies inside this envelope, in its lower half. Margin above it comes only from the hole branch of one device and from the phonon ceiling.
items.source_title: Derived from Wang et al. 2013 (Fig. 3B) and Purdie et al. 2018 (Fig. 7b)
items.note: These are DC transport times, not plasmon damping times. Neither device carried a metal gate 10 nm away.

items.item: Acoustic-phonon-limited mobility at room temperature (Hwang & Das Sarma 2008)
items.value: μ ≈ 3.7×10⁷/(D² ñ) cm²/Vs at 300 K, with D the deformation potential in eV and ñ = n/10¹². D = 19 eV gives ≈1.02×10⁵ at 10¹². Literature D spans 10–30 eV and μ scales as D⁻². The authors expect room-temperature intrinsic mobility 'surpassing 10^5'.
items.source_title: E. H. Hwang and S. Das Sarma, 'Acoustic phonon scattering limited carrier mobility in two-dimensional extrinsic graphene', Phys. Rev. B 77, 115449 (2008)
items.note: Derived: τ_ph(10¹², D = 19 eV) = 10.25×0.1167/10¹² = 1.20 ps, Q 7.5, 1.82 dB per gate. D = 25 eV would give 5.9×10⁴, i.e. 0.69 ps. That is below the measured 90,000, so D = 25 eV is inconsistent with Wang 2013.

items.item: Measured intrinsic room-temperature resistivity bound (Morozov et al. 2008)
items.value: The temperature-dependent resistivity ρ_S does not exceed 50 Ω at 300 K. That gives μ of 40,000–400,000 cm²/Vs for n = 3×10¹¹–3×10¹² cm⁻². The paper states that mobilities above 200,000 cm²/Vs are achievable once extrinsic disorder is removed.
items.source_title: S. V. Morozov et al., 'Giant intrinsic carrier mobilities in graphene and its bilayer', Phys. Rev. Lett. 100, 016602 (2008) (review ref. [32])
items.note: Measured on graphene on SiO2/PMMA. Derived at 10¹²: μ ≥ 1/(10¹⁶ m⁻² × e × 50 Ω) = 1.25×10⁵ cm²/Vs, so τ ≥ 1.46 ps, Q ≥ 9.2 and the gate loss ≤ 1.49 dB.

items.item: Derived: acoustic-phonon lifetime ceiling at n = 10¹², 300 K
items.value: τ_ph ≈ 1.2–1.8 ps (Q 7.5–11.3; 1.8–1.2 dB per λp/2 gate). The span comes from four estimates: 1.20 ps (Hwang–Das Sarma, D = 19 eV), 1.41 ps (Wang's plotted model, 121,000), ≥1.46 ps (Morozov, ρ_S ≤ 50 Ω) and ≥1.61–1.82 ps (Wang's high-density data).
items.source_title: Derived from Hwang & Das Sarma 2008; Morozov 2008; Wang et al. 2013 Fig. 3B
items.note: High-density bound: the measured ρ at 4.4–4.5×10¹² is 35–45 Ω (text <~40 Ω; figure ≈45 Ω). Acoustic-phonon resistivity is density-independent (Sohier 2014; Hwang–Das Sarma), so μ_ph(10¹²) ≥ 1/(10¹⁶·e·45 Ω) = 1.39×10⁵ to 1/(10¹⁶·e·40 Ω) = 1.56×10⁵, i.e. τ ≥ 1.61–1.82 ps. The ceiling is ×1.2–1.8 the design row.

items.item: First-principles phonon-limited resistivity (Sohier et al. 2014)
items.value: In the equipartition regime the acoustic-phonon resistivity is doping- and substrate-independent and is governed by the unscreened gauge field. Even at the GW level the calculation underestimates it by 30%. Above ~270 K, optical phonons (A1' at 0.15 eV) add a steep rise, which the calculation underestimates against experiment (graphene on SiO2).
items.source_title: T. Sohier et al., 'Phonon-limited resistivity of graphene by first-principle calculations', Phys. Rev. B 90, 125414 (2014)
items.note: No absolute 300-K resistivity was extracted: the figures add fictitious residual resistivities for clarity. The density-independence is what the Wang high-density bound relies on.

items.item: Remote (surface-optical) hBN phonons: energies and mobility limit (Perebeinos & Avouris 2010)
items.value: The hBN surface-optical phonon energies are 101.7 and 195.7 meV. Their model at n = 10¹² and 300 K gives low-field μ ≈ 1×10⁵ cm²/Vs for graphene on BN, with remote-phonon scattering, against ≈7×10⁵ intrinsic (their D_ac = 3.7 eV).
items.source_title: V. Perebeinos and Ph. Avouris, 'Inelastic scattering and current saturation in graphene', Phys. Rev. B 81, 195442 (2010)
items.note: Read from the log-scale Fig. 1a; model-dependent, with the graphene–substrate distance a fitted input. Measured hBN/G/hBN devices (Wang 2013) sit at or above acoustic-only models at high n, so the measured remote-phonon penalty at RT appears smaller than this model implies.

items.item: Plasmon damping vs DC transport time in hBN/G/hBN (Principi et al. 2014)
items.value: At RT, graphene's acoustic phonons dominate mid-IR plasmon damping in hBN/G/hBN, with theoretical γ⁻¹ ≈ 50–60. The plasmon lifetime 'is not directly correlated with the mobility: in fact, it can be anti-correlated'. hBN optical phonons contribute nothing to DC transport but can damp at finite (q, ω). In the limit q → 0, ω → 0 the damping reproduces the DC transport time.
items.source_title: A. Principi et al., 'Plasmon losses due to electron-phonon scattering: the case of graphene encapsulated in hexagonal Boron Nitride', Phys. Rev. B 90, 165408 (2014)
items.note: Derived for Fable: at 1 THz, ħω = 4.1 meV ≪ k_BT = 25.9 meV ≪ hBN optical phonons (≥95 meV), and q = 2.7×10⁶ m⁻¹ ≪ k_F = 1.77×10⁸ m⁻¹. The DC transport τ is therefore the right proxy for phonon damping at 1 THz. The mid-IR anti-correlation does not transfer.

items.item: Room-temperature mid-IR plasmon damping in hBN/G/hBN, and lifetime definitions (Woessner et al. 2015)
items.value: At ħω ≈ 116 meV and n = 7.4×10¹², RT: γp⁻¹ = Re q/Im q ≈ 25. The lifetime τp = (Im q)⁻¹/v_g ≈ 500 fs is an amplitude decay time (v_g ≈ 10⁶ m/s). Graphene thermal phonons cause about half of the damping and hBN dielectric loss the rest; the intrinsic limit is γp⁻¹ ≈ 40–70. The hBN loss model ('Cai damaged') uses ħγ = 6.5 meV in-plane and 1.9 meV out-of-plane.
items.source_title: A. Woessner et al., 'Highly confined low-loss plasmons in graphene–boron nitride heterostructures', Nat. Mater. 14, 421 (2015) (review ref. [150]; Part I ref. [41])
items.note: Mid-IR only; there is no metal gate (ERRATA I-43 already records that [41] does not support the gate-loss sentence). For any Drude mode the amplitude decay time is 2τ: acoustic Im q·v_g = 1/(2τ), and √q mode Im q·v_g = 1/(2τ) too.

items.item: Cryogenic mid-IR plasmon limits (Ni et al. 2018), abstract
items.value: Nano-imaging of encapsulated graphene at cryogenic temperatures. Propagation is 'primarily restricted by the dielectric losses of the encapsulated layers, with a minor contribution from electron–phonon interactions'. At liquid-nitrogen temperature the intrinsic propagation length exceeds 10 µm, or 50 plasmon wavelengths. A ≈1.6 ps lifetime or Q ≈ 130 was not found in any accessible primary text.
items.source_title: G. X. Ni et al., 'Fundamental limits to graphene plasmonics', Nature 557, 530–533 (2018) (review ref. [146]; Part I [42]; Part II [14])
items.note: The full text is paywalled and was not read. If its lifetime is the Woessner-type amplitude decay time, the Drude-equivalent of 1.6 ps is 0.8 ps. That is unverified.

items.item: Room-temperature acoustic THz plasmon decay time (Alonso-González et al. 2017)
items.value: RT, 2.52 THz; hBN(13 nm)/graphene/hBN(42 nm) on 15-nm AuPd split gates. The 'acoustic plasmon amplitude decay time' τp ≈ L_PC/v_g rises from about 380 fs at n = 1.9×10¹¹ to about 600 fs at 7.7×10¹¹ (electrons) and is about 500 fs for holes. Damping is dominated by Coulomb impurities (n_imp = 7×10¹⁰ cm⁻²). The authors say L_PC gives 'only qualitative estimates' of the propagation length.
items.source_title: P. Alonso-González et al., 'Acoustic terahertz graphene plasmons revealed by photocurrent nanoscopy', Nat. Nanotechnol. 12, 31 (2017) (Part I ref. [39])
items.note: Derived: for ω(ω+i/τ) = s²q² the amplitude decay time is 2τ, so the Drude τ is 0.19–0.30 ps, Q(1 THz) is 1.19–1.88, and the gate loss is 13.65/Q = 11.4–7.2 dB (9.9–6.8 dB exact). Measured at n ≤ 7.7×10¹¹, below the design density.

items.item: Derived record issue: Part I §4 baseline 'τ ≈ 0.4–0.6 ps, Q ≈ 2.5–3.8 [39, 40]' uses the wrong lifetime convention
items.value: Part I's Q 2.5–3.8 equals 2π × 1 THz × (0.4–0.6 ps). That takes [39]'s amplitude decay time as the Drude τ of Eq. (2), whose amplitude damping is −1/(2τ). In Part I's own convention the [39] baseline is τ = 0.19–0.30 ps and Q = 1.2–1.9. [40] (Lundeberg 2017) gives no lifetime in its main text. Part I's own ref. [10] (Barcons Ruiz 2023) gives momentum τ = 0.18–0.48 ps at 295 K. Re-running Part I's own τ⁻³ thermal arithmetic: continuous-drive duty at the baseline falls from 8–28% to 0.9–3.5%.
items.source_title: Derived from Alonso-González 2017 (amplitude decay time) and Fable Part I v6.1 §4 / Part III v1.1 limitation 1 and §2.2
items.note: Duty = 55 K/(42.234 K × (1 ps/τ)³): 0.19 ps gives 0.9% and 0.30 ps gives 3.5%. Part I's 8.3–28.1% reproduces at 0.4–0.6 ps. No ERRATA row covers this; I-41 to I-43 concern other citations. The caveat that L_PC is qualitative cuts both ways, but Barcons's explicit Γ = 1/(2τ) decomposition is independent of it.

items.item: Lundeberg et al. 2017: what it supplies
items.value: Photocurrent nanoscopy at 3.11 THz of hBN-encapsulated graphene on AuPd, with phase velocities down to ~c/250 near v_F. It covers dispersion and three nonlocal quantum effects. No plasmon lifetime or Q value was found in the main text.
items.source_title: M. B. Lundeberg et al., 'Tuning quantum nonlocal effects in graphene plasmonics', Science 357, 187 (2017) (Part I ref. [40])
items.note: The supplement was not checked. As cited, [40] supports the dispersion, Eq. (1), but not the lifetime baseline.

items.item: Room-temperature THz acoustic-plasmon damping and momentum time under Pd gates (Barcons Ruiz et al. 2023)
items.value: 295 K, 1.84–4.25 THz, n ≈ 10¹². Gates are 2 nm Ti/15 nm Pd; the hBN spacer is 2.0 nm (device 1) or 11.8 nm (device 2), with air gaps. The text reports 'plasmon lifetimes of about 0.5 to 1 ps' as 1/Γ, with Γ = ωIm(q²)/(2Re(q²)), which reduces to Γ = 1/(2τ) at low screening (Eq. S8). Fig. S6 at 4.25 THz: Γ = 1.40–2.11×10¹² s⁻¹ (device 1) and 1.56–2.89×10¹² s⁻¹ (device 2). Fig. S7 momentum-relaxing τ: 0.32–0.48 ps (device 1; S8 lower bound 0.24–0.36 ps) and 0.18–0.34 ps (device 2).
items.source_title: D. Barcons Ruiz et al., 'Experimental signatures of the transition from acoustic plasmon to electronic sound in graphene', Sci. Adv. 9, eadi0415 (2023), main text and supplementary notes S5–S7 (Part I ref. [10])
items.note: Figure values digitized from the supplement (S6: 32 and 30 points; S7: 20 and 21 markers). The authors note Im q has a larger uncertainty than Re q. These are the only RT THz momentum times in hBN/G/hBN under a metal gate found; device 2 is the closest to Fable's 10-nm spacer.

items.item: Derived: Q and gate loss at 1 THz from the Barcons Ruiz momentum times
items.value: Device 2 (11.8 nm): Q = 2π×10¹²×(0.18–0.34 ps) = 1.13–2.14, and the λp/2 gate loss 13.65/Q = 12.1–6.4 dB (exact for q² ∝ 1+i/Q: 10.3–6.1 dB). Device 1 (2 nm): Q = 1.51–3.0 and 9.0–4.6 dB (exact 8.2–4.5 dB). Both compare with Q 6.3 and 2.17 dB at the design row.
items.source_title: Derived from Barcons Ruiz et al. 2023, Fig. S7
items.note: Exact form: loss = 20log10(e)·π·tan(φ/2) with φ = arctan(1/Q). This assumes the 4.25-THz damping time also applies at 1 THz (ħω < k_BT in both cases).

items.item: Room-temperature resonant THz detection in hBN-encapsulated graphene under a metal top gate (Caridad et al. 2024)
items.value: Exfoliated monolayer graphene, 6-µm channel, 4.8-µm metal top gate, bow-tie antenna. Average μ > 70,000 cm²/Vs at 10 K and > 60,000 at RT. Momentum-relaxing τ is 0.29 ps at 10 K and 0.23 ps at RT. A plasmon lifetime of ≈0.6 ps comes from resonance half-widths (10-K data at 2.5–4.7 THz). Resonances at 4.7 THz persist up to 300 K.
items.source_title: J. M. Caridad et al., 'Room-Temperature Plasmon-Assisted Resonant THz Detection in Single-Layer Graphene Transistors', Nano Lett. 24, 935 (2024)
items.note: Derived: with μ = 60,000, τ = 0.23 ps corresponds to n ≈ 1×10¹¹ cm⁻² (from τ = μħ√(πn)/(e v_F)), so the quoted τ is not at 10¹². At 1 THz, 0.23 ps would give Q = 1.45. This is a 2021–2026 work superseding the review.

items.item: Plasmon lifetime vs transport time in a gated THz detector (Bandurin et al. 2018)
items.value: Bilayer graphene, hBN-encapsulated, 10 K. The plasmon lifetime from resonance widths is 0.3–0.9 ps, against a transport time τ_tr ≈ 2 ps. Q = 2πfτp is 4–11 at 2 THz and 0.2–0.7 at 0.13 THz. μ(10¹²) exceeds 10 m²/Vs at 10 K and 2 m²/Vs at 300 K.
items.source_title: D. A. Bandurin et al., 'Resonant terahertz detection using graphene plasmons', Nat. Commun. 9, 5392 (2018)
items.note: Cryogenic, bilayer. Here the THz plasmon lifetime is 2.2–6.7× shorter than the DC transport time. De Fazio 2026 notes that these resonances were 'visible only under cryogenic conditions (10 K)'.

items.item: Cryogenic THz plasmon lifetimes in DS photodetectors (Delgado-Notario et al. 2025)
items.value: Mono- and bilayer graphene TeraFETs at 1.7 K, average μ > 70,000 cm²/Vs. Transport τ exceeds 0.4 ps. Plasmon lifetimes from Lorentzian fits are typically above 1 ps and 'slightly exceed' the transport times ('momentum scattering alone does not set the linewidth').
items.source_title: J. A. Delgado-Notario et al., 'Resonant Dyakonov–Shur Magnetoplasmons in Graphene Terahertz Photodetectors', arXiv:2512.00180
items.note: Cryogenic only; preprint. Together with Bandurin 2018 and Caridad 2024, the ratio of THz plasmon to DC lifetime ranges from ×0.15 to ×2 across devices. The sign of the DC-vs-THz gap is device-dependent.

items.item: On-chip THz spectroscopy of graphene plasmon modes (Kipp et al. 2024)
items.value: hBN-encapsulated graphene in an on-chip THz circuit on sapphire, at 20 K. The s = 2 mode at n = 2.85×10¹² has Q = ω/Γ ≈ 5.7 ± 0.1 and a mean free path of 9.1 ± 0.2 µm. The authors say the Q is 'limited by device dimensions'.
items.source_title: G. Kipp et al., 'Cavity electrodynamics of van der Waals heterostructures', arXiv:2403.19745
items.note: Cryogenic. A 9.1-µm mean free path implies τ ≈ 9 ps (ωτ ≫ 5.7), so geometry, not scattering, set Q. Fable's 576-nm cell is far smaller.

items.item: Hydrodynamic THz plasmons in ultraclean graphene (Zhao et al. 2023)
items.value: On-chip THz spectroscopy of a graphene micro-ribbon close to charge neutrality (Dirac fluid). It shows a hydrodynamic bipolar-plasmon resonance and an energy wave. No damping or Q value at n ≈ 10¹² or at RT appears in the abstract.
items.source_title: W. Zhao et al., 'Observation of hydrodynamic plasmons and energy waves in graphene', Nature 614, 688 (2023)
items.note: The full text was blocked (403) and not read. Not applicable to the n = 10¹² Fermi-liquid regime.

items.item: CVD graphene with exfoliated hBN, room temperature (Banszerus et al. 2016)
items.value: hBN/CVD-graphene/hBN, dry-transferred from reusable Cu. The 300 K mean free path is ≈0.49 µm at n = −1×10¹² and ≈0.57 µm at +1×10¹² (Fig. 2d, log axis). The text states that electron-phonon scattering 'limits the room temperature mobility of graphene to values around 130,000 cm2/(Vs) at carrier densities around 10^12 cm-2'; that limit is cited from Chen 2008 and Hwang & Das Sarma 2008, not measured here.
items.source_title: L. Banszerus et al., 'Ballistic Transport Exceeding 28 µm in CVD Grown Graphene', Nano Lett. 16, 1387 (2016)
items.note: Digitized. Derived: τ = ℓ/v_F = 0.49–0.57 ps; μ = 2eℓ√π/(h√n) = 42,000–49,000 cm²/Vs; Q 3.1–3.6; gate loss 4.4–3.8 dB. Lab-scale: CVD graphene with exfoliated hBN.

items.item: CVD graphene on reusable copper (Banszerus et al. 2015): room-temperature value
items.value: The abstract reports mobilities up to 350,000 cm²/Vs; the temperature is not stated in the abstract and is low-T in context. A room-temperature mobility at 10¹² was not found, because the full text was not read.
items.source_title: L. Banszerus et al., 'Ultrahigh-mobility graphene devices from chemical vapor deposition on reusable copper', Sci. Adv. 1, e1500222 (2015)
items.note: The publisher PDF request returned an HTML page, which was not pursued. The 2016 follow-up (preceding item) supplies the RT mean free path.

items.item: Wet-transferred CVD graphene encapsulated in hBN, room temperature (De Fazio et al. 2019)
items.value: At 290 K, μ_H reaches 70,000 cm²/Vs close to the CNP and stays above 30,000 for |n| up to 1.5×10¹². Field-effect μ is 49,000 (electrons) and 54,000 (holes) at 290 K. Polycrystalline graphene after annealing reaches ≈30,000 at RT. Single-crystal domains are ~500 µm.
items.source_title: D. De Fazio et al., 'High-mobility, wet-transferred graphene grown by chemical vapor deposition', ACS Nano 13, 8926 (2019)
items.note: Derived at 10¹², assuming μ = 30,000–45,000 (bounded by '>30,000 up to 1.5×10¹²'): τ = 0.35–0.53 ps, Q 2.2–3.3, gate loss 6.2–4.1 dB.

items.item: Wafer-scale CVD-hBN/CVD-graphene stacks, room temperature (Fukamachi et al. 2023)
items.value: cm-scale CVD multilayer hBN grown on Fe–Ni foil, with CVD graphene grown on Cu(111)/sapphire, measured at RT in vacuum, two-terminal field-effect mobility. hBN/G/hBN: maximum 10,219 (holes) and 9,571 (electrons) cm²/Vs; averages 5,477 and 5,551 (more than 60 channels). G/hBN maximum 7,284; G/SiO2 maximum 5,384.
items.source_title: S. Fukamachi et al., 'Large-area synthesis and transfer of multilayer hexagonal boron nitride for enhanced graphene device arrays', Nat. Electron. 6, 126–136 (2023) (Part III ref. [42])
items.note: Derived at 10¹²: τ = 0.064–0.12 ps, Q = 0.40–0.75 (overdamped), exact λp/2 loss 18.4–13.7 dB. The authors note that two-terminal field-effect mobility underestimates μ.

items.item: Decoupled CVD graphene on Cu(111)/sapphire (Gebeyehu et al. 2024)
items.value: The abstract reports room-temperature carrier mobility 'exceeding 10^4 cm2 V−1 s−1 on SiO2/Si and 10^5 cm2 V−1 s−1 upon encapsulation in hexagonal boron nitride'. Growth is non-reducing LPCVD with an oxidized Cu2O interface, which enables dry pick-up.
items.source_title: Z. M. Gebeyehu et al., 'Decoupled High-Mobility Graphene on Cu(111)/Sapphire via Chemical Vapor Deposition', Adv. Mater. 36, 2404590 (2024)
items.note: Abstract only: the full text sits behind a bot check and was not read. The density and the hBN source are not stated. Derived, if μ > 10⁵ holds at 10¹²: τ > 1.17 ps and Q > 7.3. De Fazio 2026 cites this as a route to RT acoustic-plasmon resonances.

items.item: Acoustic-plasmon cavity resonances in scalable CVD graphene (De Fazio et al. 2026)
items.value: CVD graphene on SiO2 with ~40-nm AlOx and no hBN. Acoustic-plasmon Fabry–Pérot resonances at 1.83–2.52 THz are pronounced from 6 to 90 K and vanish by 130 K. At 6 K, τp ≈ 0.13 ps (Q ≈ 2.0) and 0.05 ps (Q ≈ 0.8), from μ_e ≈ 1.2–1.3×10⁴ and μ_h ≈ 2.7–3.7×10⁴ cm²/Vs. The authors report 'a reduction of carrier mobility by nearly two orders of magnitude between T = 6 and 130 K'.
items.source_title: D. De Fazio et al., 'Enhanced Terahertz Photoresponse via Acoustic Plasmon Cavity Resonances in Scalable Graphene', ACS Photonics 13, 4505 (2026) (Part III ref. [43])
items.note: Derived Q at 1 THz from the 6-K values: 2π×10¹²×(0.05–0.13 ps) = 0.31–0.82. At RT the damping is higher still.

items.item: CVD acoustic plasmons at room temperature, mid-IR (Menabde et al. 2021)
items.value: Near-field imaging of mid-IR acoustic plasmons in large-area CVD graphene under gold with an alumina spacer, at RT. Fitted E_F ≈ 0.5 eV and μ ≈ 2,000 cm²/Vs. The acoustic mode is up to 2.3× more confined than the unscreened mode and has 1.4× lower damping.
items.source_title: S. G. Menabde et al., 'Real-space imaging of acoustic plasmons in large-area CVD graphene', Nat. Commun. 12, 938 (2021)
items.note: Mid-IR, at high E_F. Not transferable to 1 THz: μ = 2,000 at E_F = 0.117 eV gives τ = 0.023 ps and Q = 0.15.

items.item: Derived: gate-metal ohmic damping at 1 THz, n = 10¹²
items.value: The extra rate is 1/τ_gate = R_s·n e²v_F²/E_F = R_s × 1.373×10¹⁰ s⁻¹ per Ω, because the image current equals the graphene sheet current at qd = 0.027. Bulk Au (ρ = 2.44×10⁻⁸ Ω m, skin depth 78.6 nm): R_s = 0.31 Ω, adding 0.43% of 1/τ at τ = 1 ps (Q 6.26; 2.18 dB per gate). 30-nm Au: 1.17 Ω, +1.6%. 15-nm Pd: 10–17 Ω, +14–23% (Q 5.1–5.5; 2.47–2.67 dB). 15-nm AuPd: 20 Ω, +27% (Q 4.9; 2.77 dB). At τ = 0.3 ps each share is ×0.3.
items.source_title: Derived; gate stacks from Barcons Ruiz 2023 (2 nm Ti/15 nm Pd) and Alonso-González 2017 (15-nm AuPd); Au resistivity is the handbook value
items.note: Assumed thin-film resistivities: Au 30 nm, 3.5×10⁻⁸ Ω m; Pd 15 nm, 1.5–2.5×10⁻⁷; AuPd, 3×10⁻⁷. Cross-check: ωL_k/R_s = 458 Ω/0.31 Ω gives Q_metal ≈ 1.5×10³. A 5-nm Ti adhesion layer under thick Au adds ~0.3% of the Au loss. Drive power at a fixed bias ratio scales as (1+x)², so ×1.009 for thick Au and ×1.29–1.63 for 15-nm Pd/AuPd. ERRATA I-43 records this loss as unquantified.

items.item: hBN dielectric loss at 1 THz: no crystalline-hBN measurement found; derived phonon-tail estimate
items.value: Derived from the Lorentz parameters in Woessner 2015 Table S1 ('Cai damaged': z: ε∞ 2.95, s 0.61, ħω_TO 92.5 meV, ħγ 1.9 meV; in-plane ħγ 6.5 meV). At 1 THz: ε_z = 3.56 and tan δ_z ≈ 1.6×10⁻⁴ (0.4×10⁻⁴ with a clean ħγ_z ≈ 0.5 meV); tan δ_x ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁴. The added 1/Q ≤ 2.5×10⁻⁴ against 1/Q = 0.159 at Q 6.3, i.e. ≤0.16% of the damping and ≤ +0.003 dB per gate.
items.source_title: Derived from Woessner et al. 2015 supplement Table S1. Ceramic BN THz-TDS: Naftaly, Leist, Dudley, J. Eur. Ceram. Soc. 30, 2691 (2010); Naftaly & Leist, Appl. Opt. 52, B20 (2013)
items.note: No measured tan δ at 1 THz for exfoliated or CVD hBN was found. The NPL ceramic-BN papers report THz loss coefficients (linear in porosity; pyrolytic BN suited as a THz optical material), but their numbers were not accessible. In the mid-IR, hBN loss is about half the damping (Woessner); at 1 THz it is negligible.

items.item: Derived: DS threshold vs lifetime (Part I Eq. 3, M_th = 1/(8 f0 τ), s = 2.33×10⁶ m/s)
items.value: The threshold drift is v0,th = s/(8f0τ). It is 0.29×10⁶ m/s at τ = 1 ps. It reaches v_F at τ = 0.29 ps (0.33–0.34 ps with the closure's ×1.12–1.16). It exceeds the Landau ceiling s − v_F = 1.33×10⁶ m/s, where no threshold exists, for τ < 0.22 ps (0.25 ps with the shift). At the RT THz-plasmon τ measured under metal gates (0.18–0.48 ps): M_th = 0.26–0.69 and v0,th = 0.61–1.62×10⁶ m/s.
items.source_title: Derived from Fable Part I v6.1 Eq. (3) and §5, with Barcons Ruiz 2023 Fig. S7
items.note: In-model, from the hydrodynamic threshold. Arithmetic: 1/(8 × 10¹² × 0.571) = 0.219 ps, with 0.571 = 1.33/2.33.

items.item: Derived: per-cell drive power and duty vs lifetime (Part I §4: dissipation ∝ τ⁻³ at the tracked bias)
items.value: Scaling Part III's 7.78–10.22 µW per cell and 29–39 fJ/MAC (τ = 1 ps, 300 K). At τ = 1.2–1.8 ps (phonon ceiling): ×0.58–0.17, i.e. 1.3–5.9 µW and 5–23 fJ/MAC. At τ = 0.93–1.20 ps (best DC devices): ×1.24–0.58. At τ = 0.48/0.34/0.18 ps (RT THz plasmon): ×9.0/25/171, i.e. 70–92 µW, 198–260 µW and 1.33–1.75 mW per cell, or 0.26–0.35, 0.74–0.99 and 5.0–6.7 pJ/MAC. Continuous-drive duty under the 55-K budget is 14%, 5.1% and 0.8% at those three τ.
items.source_title: Derived from Fable Part I v6.1 §4 (τ⁻³ scaling, ΔT = 42.234 K at τ = 1 ps) and Part III v1.1 per-cell power
items.note: Duty = 55/(42.234 × (1 ps/τ)³). Below ≈0.25–0.33 ps no reachable threshold exists (previous item), so those power figures describe a cell that cannot be biased to 0.7 M_th.

items.item: Derived summary: defensible Q at 1 THz and λp/2 gate loss (13.65/Q) at 300 K, n = 10¹²
items.value: (i) DC transport, best exfoliated devices: τ 0.93–1.20 ps, Q 5.9–7.5, 2.3–1.8 dB. (ii) Acoustic-phonon ceiling: 1.2–1.8 ps, Q 7.5–11.3, 1.8–1.2 dB. (iii) THz plasmon under metal gates at RT: 0.18–0.48 ps, Q 1.1–3.0, 12.1–4.6 dB (exact 10.3–4.5). (iv) Lab-scale CVD graphene with exfoliated hBN (DC): 0.35–0.57 ps, Q 2.2–3.6, 6.2–3.8 dB. (v) Wafer-scale CVD stack (DC): 0.064–0.12 ps, Q 0.40–0.75, overdamped, exact 18.4–13.7 dB. (vi) Design row: 1.0 ps, Q 6.3, 2.17 dB.
items.source_title: Derived from the items above (Wang 2013; Purdie 2018; Hwang & Das Sarma 2008; Morozov 2008; Barcons Ruiz 2023; Alonso-González 2017; Banszerus 2016; De Fazio 2019; Fukamachi 2023)
items.note: Only (iii) is a THz plasmon damping measurement in a metal-gated stack. Rows (i), (ii), (iv) and (v) are DC proxies, valid for phonon damping at 1 THz by Principi 2014's ω→0 limit but not tested under a gate. The 13.65/Q formula is a large-Q expansion, so the exact form is given wherever Q < 3.

items.item: Electron–electron intrinsic plasmon damping (Principi et al. 2013)
items.value: A T = 0 theory of electron–electron damping beyond RPA, which is intrinsic and operates without disorder or phonons. Graphene's pseudospin suppresses these losses relative to ordinary 2D electron liquids. The paper targets plasmons below the single-particle threshold in the mid-IR.
items.source_title: A. Principi, G. Vignale, M. Carrega, M. Polini, 'Intrinsic lifetime of Dirac plasmons in graphene', Phys. Rev. B 88, 195405 (2013)
items.note: At 1 THz (ħω/E_F = 0.035) this T = 0 channel is small. The RT electron–electron channel that matters, hydrodynamic and viscous, is already carried in Part I §7.5 and was measured as a velocity crossover by Barcons Ruiz 2023.

mapping.fable_problem: Lifetime row τ = 1.0 ps at 300 K (Part I Table 3/§4; Q 6.3; issue #140): 'mobility ≈ 86,000 … inside the demonstrated envelope (~140,000 near the acoustic-phonon limit [33])'
mapping.reason: Part I already flags the row as best-case premium material. The primary data sharpen it. The best exfoliated devices give DC τ(10¹², 290–300 K) = 0.93–1.20 ps (Wang 2013 ≈90,500; Purdie 2018 ≈80,000 for electrons and ≈103,000 for holes), so the row sits inside the measured DC envelope, in its lower half. The ~140,000 in [33] is that device's peak at n ≈ 0.1–0.3×10¹², where τ is shorter. The device reaches the phonon model only at n ≳ 2.5×10¹². The acoustic-phonon ceiling is ≈1.2–1.8 ps.
mapping.what_must_be_true: For the row to hold in a cell, the THz plasmon damping time under the metal gate must equal the best devices' DC transport time. No RT THz plasmon measurement under a metal gate has shown τ above 0.48 ps.
mapping.quantified_effect: Design 1.0 ps (Q 6.3) against: DC envelope 0.93–1.20 ps (Q 5.9–7.5); phonon ceiling 1.2–1.8 ps (Q 7.5–11.3); RT THz plasmon under metal gates 0.18–0.48 ps (Q 1.1–3.0).

mapping.fable_problem: Measured room-temperature baseline 'τ ≈ 0.4–0.6 ps, Q ≈ 2.5–3.8 [39, 40]' (Part I §4; repeated in Part III §2.2 and limitation 1; Part I's duty arithmetic 8–28%)
mapping.reason: The baseline is in the record but uses the wrong lifetime convention. [39] (Alonso-González 2017) reports an amplitude decay time (L_PC/v_g = 380–600 fs). Under the record's own dispersion ω(ω+i/τ) = s²q², with Eq. (2) damping −1/(2τ), that equals 2τ. [40] gives no lifetime in its main text. Part I's own ref. [10] (Barcons Ruiz 2023, Fig. S7) gives momentum τ directly: 0.18–0.34 ps at 11.8 nm and 0.32–0.48 ps at 2 nm, at 295 K and n ≈ 10¹². No ERRATA row covers this; I-41 to I-43 concern other citations.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The factor 2 on [39] holds if L_PC tracks the amplitude decay length; the authors call L_PC a qualitative estimate. The Barcons Ruiz values do not depend on that caveat.
mapping.quantified_effect: Baseline τ 0.4–0.6 ps becomes 0.19–0.30 ps (Q 2.5–3.8 becomes 1.2–1.9). Part I's continuous-drive duty at the baseline falls from 8–28% to 0.9–3.5%. The λp/2 gate loss at the baseline rises from 5.2–3.6 dB to 9.9–6.8 dB (exact).

mapping.fable_problem: Passive loss budget: 27.3/Q dB per λp, i.e. 2.17 dB per λp/2 gate at Q 6.3 (300 K) and 2.56 dB at Q 5.3 (353 K) (Part I §4, Part II Table Q1)
mapping.reason: The formula is the record's own. No measurement at 1 THz under a metal gate settles which Q applies. DC-transport proxies support 2.3–1.8 dB (best devices) and 1.8–1.2 dB (phonon ceiling). The only RT THz plasmon damping data under metal gates give 12.1–4.6 dB by 13.65/Q (10.3–4.5 dB exact). The review's cited works are mid-IR and do not bear on this. hBN dielectric loss adds ≤0.003 dB per gate.
mapping.what_must_be_true: 2.17 dB needs a plasmon τ of at least 1 ps in the gated cell. Reaching 1.2–1.8 dB needs τ at the acoustic-phonon ceiling, i.e. disorder-free graphene at 10¹² with no extra damping from the gate.
mapping.quantified_effect: λp/2 gate loss ranges from 1.2 dB (ceiling) through 2.17 dB (design) to 4.5–10.3 dB (measured RT THz plasmon, exact).

mapping.fable_problem: Gate-metal ohmic loss, unquantified (Part I §4; ERRATA I-43; the gate is specified only as a 'segmented Au gate lattice', with no thickness)
mapping.reason: Derived quantification: 1/τ_gate = R_s·n e²v_F²/E_F = R_s × 1.37×10¹⁰ s⁻¹ per Ω, since the image current equals the sheet current at qd = 0.027. A thick Au gate (δ = 79 nm at 1 THz) adds 0.43% of the damping at τ = 1 ps. The 15-nm Pd or AuPd gates used in every RT acoustic-THz experiment cited ([10], [39], [40]) would add 14–27%. A gate-thickness specification closes an open line of the record.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The local surface-impedance picture must hold: for Au at 1 THz, ωτ ≈ 0.2 and the mean free path is below δ. The gate must be at least about 1–2 skin depths thick (≈80–160 nm), smooth under 10-nm hBN, with an adhesion layer of 5 nm or less (≈ +0.3% of the Au loss). The thin-film resistivities used for comparison are assumed: 1.5–3×10⁻⁷ Ω·m for 15-nm Pd/AuPd.
mapping.quantified_effect: Thick Au: Q 6.26, 2.18 dB per gate, drive power ×1.009. 15-nm Pd/AuPd: Q 4.9–5.5, 2.47–2.77 dB per gate, drive power ×1.29–1.63 at a fixed bias ratio, since P ∝ (1+x)².

mapping.fable_problem: hBN dielectric loss at 1 THz (not quantified in the record; Part I §1 says the hBN Reststrahlen bands play no role)
mapping.reason: The record's qualitative statement holds. Derived from Woessner 2015's hBN Lorentz parameters: tan δ ≈ 0.4–2.5×10⁻⁴ at 1 THz, which adds ≤0.16% of the damping at Q 6.3. In the mid-IR, the review's Woessner 2015 and Ni 2018 found hBN dielectric loss to be half or most of the damping; that lesson does not transfer to 1 THz.
mapping.what_must_be_true: No defect or impurity absorption in thin hBN at 1 THz beyond the phonon tail. This is unmeasured on crystalline hBN: only ceramic BN THz-TDS exists, and its values were not accessed.
mapping.quantified_effect: Added 1/Q ≤ 2.5×10⁻⁴ against 0.159; ≤ +0.003 dB per gate.

mapping.fable_problem: 'Phonon-set ceiling on plasmon lifetime in this stack is mapped in [42]' (Part I §4), and Part II Table Q1's cold-side saturation τ = 2 ps (Q 12.6), 'slightly above' ≈1.6 ps [14]
mapping.reason: [42] and [14] are both Ni 2018: a cryogenic mid-IR measurement limited mainly by dielectric losses, per its abstract. At 1 THz and 300 K the phonon ceiling is the DC acoustic-phonon limit (Principi 2014's q, ω → 0 limit; Hwang & Das Sarma 2008; Morozov 2008), ≈1.2–1.8 ps at 10¹². The 1.6-ps figure is not in Ni's accessible text; if it is an amplitude lifetime, its Drude-equivalent is 0.8 ps. Cryogenic THz plasmon lifetimes from resonance widths (Q = ωτ convention) are 0.3–0.9 ps (bilayer, 10 K), ≈0.6 ps (monolayer, 10 K) and >1 ps (1.7 K). Revision-history item 6 already flags the band crossing in Part II.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: 300-K ceiling τ 1.2–1.8 ps (Q 7.5–11), set by DC phonon scattering, not by [42]. Part II's cold 2 ps (1.09 dB per gate) is about 2× or more the measured cryogenic THz plasmon τ.

mapping.fable_problem: G1: single-cell per-pulse net gain ≥ +2.6 dB at ≤ 80 °C (Part I Table 7); the threshold M_th = 1/(8 f0 τ) and whether a 353 K threshold exists
mapping.reason: Derived in Part I's own equations. At the RT THz plasmon τ measured under metal gates (0.18–0.48 ps), M_th = 0.26–0.69 and the threshold drift is 0.61–1.62×10⁶ m/s. That drift exceeds v_F for τ < 0.29 ps (0.33–0.34 ps with the closure's ×1.12–1.16) and exceeds the Landau ceiling s − v_F = 1.33×10⁶ m/s for τ < 0.22–0.25 ps, where no threshold exists. Continuous drive closes the 55-K budget only for τ ≳ 0.92 ps (Part I). At 353 K, phonon-limited τ scales by about ×0.85.
mapping.what_must_be_true: For G1 to be reachable in continuous drive, the gated cell's plasmon τ must be at least about 0.92 ps at 300 K. That is about 1.9× the best RT THz plasmon value measured (0.48 ps) and at the DC envelope of the best devices.
mapping.quantified_effect: Threshold drift at the measured τ: 0.61–1.62×10⁶ m/s against 0.29×10⁶ m/s at the design row. Duty ceiling 0.8–14% against 100%.

mapping.fable_problem: Drive power and energy per MAC (Part III: 7.78–10.22 µW per cell and 29–39 fJ/MAC at 300 K, τ = 1 ps; Part I: dissipation ∝ τ⁻³)
mapping.reason: Derived τ⁻³ scaling. At the phonon ceiling (1.2–1.8 ps): ×0.58–0.17, i.e. 1.3–5.9 µW per cell and 5–23 fJ/MAC. At the best DC devices (0.93–1.20 ps): ×1.24–0.58. At the RT THz plasmon values (0.18–0.48 ps): ×9–171, i.e. 70 µW–1.75 mW per cell and 0.26–6.7 pJ/MAC. The improvement branch needs a device result that no source shows.
mapping.what_must_be_true: An improvement needs a THz plasmon τ above 1 ps under the gate (5–23 fJ/MAC at 1.2–1.8 ps). Holding the record needs at least 1 ps.

mapping.fable_problem: Material gap for scalable stacks (issue #140; Part III limitation 1; refs [42] Fukamachi 2023 and [43] De Fazio 2026)
mapping.reason: The record cites both works and keeps the gap open. New numbers: the wafer-scale CVD-hBN/CVD-graphene stack (Fukamachi) gives RT field-effect μ ≤ 10,219, i.e. τ ≤ 0.12 ps and Q ≤ 0.75 (overdamped). De Fazio 2026 (no hBN) shows resonances only at or below 90 K, with Q(1 THz) ≤ 0.82 from its 6-K values. Lab-scale CVD graphene with exfoliated hBN (Banszerus 2016; De Fazio 2019) gives DC τ ≈ 0.35–0.57 ps and Q 2.2–3.6 at RT.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: Q(1 THz): scalable 0.40–0.75 and lab-scale CVD 2.2–3.6, against 6.3. Exact λp/2 loss for scalable stacks is 13.7–18.4 dB.

mapping.fable_problem: A route to τ ≥ 1 ps in CVD graphene (issue #140)
mapping.reason: Gebeyehu et al. 2024 report RT μ > 10⁵ cm²/Vs for decoupled CVD graphene on Cu(111)/sapphire once encapsulated in hBN. De Fazio 2026 names this growth route as the way to RT acoustic-plasmon resonances. Only the abstract was read; the density and the hBN source are not verified because the full text sits behind a bot check.
mapping.what_must_be_true: μ > 10⁵ must hold at n = 10¹², not only near neutrality. The encapsulating hBN must be scalable (CVD-grown, as in Fukamachi) rather than exfoliated. The THz plasmon τ under a metal gate must track the DC τ, which the RT data so far do not show.
mapping.quantified_effect: If all hold: τ ≥ 1.17 ps, Q ≥ 7.3, λp/2 loss ≤ 1.87 dB, and drive power ≤ ×0.62 of the design row.

mapping.fable_problem: Electron–electron and viscous damping beyond Drude at 1 THz, 300 K (Part I §7.5 kinetic band; A-band 0.5–3)
mapping.reason: Part I §7.5 carries νq² ≈ 20% of 1/τ at 300 K (≈0.10 after the collisionless reduction) and the kinetic operator's 0.387 of 1/(2τ) at 353 K. It also cites [10] for the crossover. Barcons Ruiz's damping fit splits the measured Γ: about 25% is electron–electron (τ_ee-dependent) at the 2-nm spacer (S8 bound 0.24–0.36 ps against full fit 0.32–0.48 ps), and it is negligible at 11.8 nm. The T = 0 theory of Principi 2013 is small at 1 THz.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: Measured electron–electron share of Γ: ≈0 at 11.8 nm and ≈25% at 2 nm, against 0.10–0.39 in-model in the record.

mapping.fable_problem: Interband, Landau and radiation damping channels at 1 THz (Part I §5 and §7.5)
mapping.reason: Pauli blocking (ħω = 4.1 meV ≪ 2E_F = 233 meV) and s > v_F (×2.3) exclude the first two; the record gives interband < 0.001 dB. The review's Jablan 2009 places these losses above ≈0.2 eV. A bound acoustic mode (λ0/λp = 129) does not radiate in a uniform section.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: None; no change.

mapping.fable_problem: The review's mid-IR loss results as a route to lower loss at 1 THz (Woessner 2015 γ⁻¹ ≈ 25 at RT; Ni 2018 cryogenic; Iranzo 2018; Brar 2014; Dai 2015; Kumar 2015; Fei/Chen 2012; Menabde 2021)
mapping.reason: In the mid-IR (ħω ≈ 0.1 eV ≫ k_BT), damping is set by hBN dielectric loss, phonon emission and plasmon–phonon hybridization; Principi 2014 shows the lifetime can even anti-correlate with mobility there. At 1 THz those channels vanish (hBN ≤ 0.16%) and phonon damping reduces to the DC transport rate. Mid-IR Q values of 25–130 do not translate into a 1-THz Q.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

mapping.fable_problem: Density row n = 10¹² cm⁻² (Part I §4)
mapping.reason: The record chooses this density on saturation-velocity, heating and puddle grounds. New, derived from Wang 2013 Fig. 3B: the best RT device's τ(n) = μE_F/(ev_F²) is flat at 1.01–1.06 ps over n = 0.5–1.5×10¹² and falls to 0.77 ps at 4.4×10¹². So 10¹² also sits at the lifetime maximum. Lowering n raises μ (to 140,000 near 0.2×10¹²) without lengthening τ.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: τ = 1.01 ps (0.5×10¹²), 1.06 ps (1×10¹²), 0.98 ps (2×10¹²) and 0.77 ps (4.4×10¹²). No gain is available from moving n.

mapping.fable_problem: Downstream in-model figures resting on τ = 1 ps (fan-out 2 at ≈69 GHz; DG1 with 99–277 quanta delivered against ≥406 needed; 2.207 TMAC/s per lane)
mapping.reason: Part III limitation 1 states that every gain and power figure rests on the lifetime row. At the measured RT THz plasmon τ, per-cell passive loss rises ×2–5 and the threshold becomes unreachable below about 0.25–0.33 ps. These quantities were not re-run here.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A solver re-run at τ = 0.2–0.5 ps would be needed to state the effect.
mapping.quantified_effect: Not quantified here. Per-cell passive loss at λp/4 is 1.09 dB at the design row and 2.2–5.2 dB (exact) at the measured RT THz plasmon τ.

mapping.fable_problem: Launch coupling, readout and THz I/O (Part I §9.5, DG4, Part III limitation 12)
mapping.reason: The lifetime topic touches these only through propagation loss in plasmonic lines, already assessed elsewhere (≈1,860 dB/mm at Q 6.3). No cited loss or lifetime work bears on transducer efficiency, launch jitter or readout.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

items.item: Which topic works the review actually cites (its Crossref reference list, 198 refs)
items.value: It cites Alcaraz Iranzo 2018 (#151); Osborne 2017, a Science editor's highlight of Lundeberg 2017 (#152, not the paper itself); Woessner 2015 (#150); Ni 2018 (#146) and the Song 2018 News & Views (#147); de Vega & García de Abajo 2019 on plasmon generation by tunnelling in metal–insulator–graphene (#126); La 2015 (#110, not found online); and double-layer/RPA theory (#72, #78, #99, #104, #106, #109). It does NOT cite Lundeberg 2017 itself, Alonso-González 2017, Epstein 2020 or Principi 2011.
items.source_title: Crossref record for Cui, Wang, Sun, 'Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics', Reviews in Physics 6, 100054 (2021), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
items.note: Taken from the deposited reference list. The full text sits behind a bot check and was not read.

items.item: Principi 2011: speed of the gated acoustic plasmon (RPA)
items.value: c_s = v·sqrt(Λ/(Λ−1)), with Λ = [1 + 1/(2 g_s g_v α_ee d k_F)]². Within RPA, c_s > v for every value of α_ee d k_F. The paper's examples are at n = 5×10^13 cm^-2 and d = 3–5 Å.
items.source_title: Principi, Asgari, Polini, Solid State Commun. 151, 1627 (2011); arXiv:1104.2707
items.note: DERIVED: this is algebraically the same as Part I Eq. (1). Set g = 8 α k_F d/ε_z and u = 1/g; then Λ/(Λ−1) = (1+u)²/(u(2+u)) = (1+g)²/(1+2g). Part I Eq. (1) cites [39, 40], not Principi 2011.

items.item: Alonso-González 2017: acoustic THz plasmon under a metal gate
items.value: Room temperature, 2.52 THz (also 3.11 and 4.25 THz). Stack: hBN 13 nm / graphene / hBN 42 nm on AuPd split gates. λ_p ≈ λ0/66 (journal abstract); v_g ≈ 0.014c; vertical confinement ≈ λ0/2800. Decay time L_PC/v_g ≈ 380–600 fs at n = 0.19–0.77×10^12 cm^-2, impurity-limited.
items.source_title: Alonso-González et al., Nat. Nanotechnol. 12, 31–35 (2017), doi:10.1038/nnano.2016.185
items.note: [THz, 300 K] Already in the record as Part I ref. [39]: it is the source of Eq. (1) and of the τ 0.4–0.6 ps baseline. DERIVED check: Eq. (1) at d = 42 nm, n ≈ 1.1e12, ε 3.56 gives λ0/λ_p ≈ 67.

items.item: Lundeberg 2017: measured plasmon speed vs gate distance at n = 1e12 cm^-2, 3.11 THz
items.value: v_p ≈ 3.7×10^6 m/s at d = 27 nm, ≈2.75×10^6 at 14.5 nm, ≈1.83×10^6 at 5.5 nm (AuPd bottom gate). The local (Drude) curve at 5.5 nm is ≈1.5×10^6.
items.source_title: Lundeberg et al., Science 357, 187 (2017); arXiv:1704.05518 Fig. 3
items.note: [THz] Values read off Fig. 3 (about ±0.1e6). The temperature is not stated; the paper says 'ambient conditions'. Already in the record as Part I ref. [40].

items.item: Lundeberg 2017: the nonlocal corrections
items.value: The local approximation is off by more than 10% once v_p/v_F < 2. The nonlocal plasmon never drops below v_F; the local one does at 5.5 nm. Plasmons were slowed to ≈c/250. Three quantum layers are needed: RPA Fermi-surface deformation, Fermi-velocity renormalization (from 0.85×10^6 bare up to 3×10^6 m/s at very low density), and a compressibility correction δ = 1 − κ0/κ. The full theory matches the data with no fitted parameters.
items.source_title: Lundeberg et al., Science 357, 187 (2017); arXiv:1704.05518
items.note: DERIVED: s = 2v_F is reached at g = 6.464, i.e. d = 7.3 nm (ε_z 3.5) or 6.9 nm (ε_z 3.32) at n = 1e12. Below that, a Drude estimate errs by more than 10%.

items.item: Eq. (1) against Lundeberg's data at n = 1e12
items.value: With ε_z = 3.32, Eq. (1) gives 1.83, 2.75 and 3.66 ×10^6 m/s at 5.5, 14.5 and 27 nm: −0.1%, −0.2% and −1.2% from the read values. With ε_z = 3.5 the gaps are −2.1%, −2.5% and −3.6%.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I Eq. (1) and Lundeberg 2017 Fig. 3
items.note: Eq. (1) holds down to d = 5.5 nm within about 4% at 3.11 THz, close to collisionless. At 1 THz the first-sound shift (separate item) comes on top.

items.item: Part I calls Eq. (1) 'gated local-RPA'; it is actually the nonlocal RPA result
items.value: The local (Drude) speed is v_F·sqrt(g/2) = 2.16×10^6 m/s at 10 nm (ε_z 3.32), so Eq. (1) at 2.33×10^6 sits +7.9% above it (+8.3% at ε 3.5). The gap grows to +16% at 5 nm, +26% at 3 nm, +38% at 2 nm and +70% at 1 nm.
items.source_title: DERIVED (algebra on Part I Eq. (1); terminology as in Lundeberg 2017)
items.note: A labelling point only; no number moves. The many-body layers (velocity renormalization, compressibility) are not in Eq. (1).

items.item: Mode speed and plasmon wavelength vs gate distance (Eq. (1), ε_z 3.5, n = 1e12, v_F = 1e6, 1 THz)
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I Eq. (1) = Principi 2011
items.note: α_g = 2.1877 and k_F = 1.7725e8 m^-1. As d → 0, s → v_F, so λ_p never falls below v_F/f = 1.0 µm at 1 THz.

items.item: In-plane compression λ0/λ_p vs d
items.value: 131.5 at 10 nm, 173.3 at 5, 205.9 at 3, 230.5 at 2, 264.6 at 1 nm (ε 3.5). The ceiling is c/v_F ≈ 300, i.e. at most ×2.3 beyond the design's λ0/129.
items.source_title: DERIVED; ceiling as stated by Epstein et al. 2020 ('maximal wavelength confinement of λ0/300')
items.note: The mid-IR records do not lift this floor. Epstein's slowest measured AGP was ≈1.42×10^6 m/s (mid-IR).

items.item: Cell length vs d: L = (s/4f0)(1−M²) at the 353 K bias (M = 0.103)
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I Eq. (1) and (4); record parameters in fable-model-chain/constants.py
items.note: ε_z 3.32 reproduces the record's 582.8 nm zero-drift and 576.6 nm operating lengths exactly.

items.item: The d = 5 nm die already in the record
items.value: g = 4.672, s = 1.7635 v_F, cell 441 nm (zero drift). Part I §10 scores it as a '+2.6 dB-class gain lever at the hydrodynamic tier'. In the single-rate kinetic operator at 353 K (A = 1, drift heat shed) it restores no threshold: best Im ω −0.190, base stable.
items.source_title: notes/2026-10-15-graphene-fluid-threshold-turns-on-current-channel.md; Part I §10; ERRATA I-40
items.note: In-model. The record books no footprint or energy consequences for this die.

items.item: Propagation loss vs d at Q = ωτ = 6.28
items.value: Per wavelength it stays 27.3/Q = 4.35 dB, so per cell and per gate it is unchanged. Per µm: 1.91 (10 nm), 2.21 (7), 2.51 (5), 2.72 (4), 2.99 (3), 3.34 (2), 3.84 (1) dB/µm.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I §4 (27.3/Q dB per λ_p)
items.note: Loss per mm roughly doubles at 1 nm (∝ 1/s), but layout distances shrink by the same factor.

items.item: Viscous damping term vs d (the record's own hydrodynamic estimate)
items.source_title: DERIVED by scaling Part I §7 ('νq² ≈ 20% of 1/τ … ≈0.10 of 1/τ at the cap'), q = ω/s
items.note: Reproduces the record's 0.21 and 0.13/0.10 at 10 nm. Scales ∝ 1/s². This is a hydrodynamic-tier estimate.

items.item: Barcons Ruiz 2023: room-temperature THz acoustic plasmons with a thin spacer
items.value: 295 K, 1.84/2.52/3.11/4.25 THz, hBN on 2/15-nm Ti/Pd split gates. Device 1: 2.0 nm hBN plus a fitted 1.46-nm air gap, C = 4.37 mF/m², Λ = 0.178, momentum τ = 0.44 ps. Device 2: 11.8 nm hBN plus 6.24-nm air gap, C = 0.93 mF/m², Λ = 0.038, τ = 0.30 ps. Plasmon lifetimes 0.5–1 ps; v_F(1e12) = 1.1×10^6 m/s; F0^s = −0.061 / −0.067.
items.source_title: Barcons Ruiz et al., Sci. Adv. 9, eadi0415 (2023); arXiv:2301.07399 (Table S1, Supp. Note 5)
items.note: [THz, 300 K] This is Part I ref. [10], cited there for the crossover only, not for τ or the air gap. DERIVED: hBN-equivalent d_eq = 3.5·ε0/C = 7.1 nm (device 1) and 33 nm (device 2). The thinnest room-temperature THz device to date therefore behaved electrostatically like ≈7 nm. The thinner device showed no τ penalty (2 devices).

items.item: Barcons Ruiz 2023: collisionless-to-hydrodynamic (first-sound) speed
items.value: Measured: ≈5% slow-down from 4.25 to 1.84 THz in device 1, none in device 2. Theory (their Eq. 2): v_h = sqrt((v_c² + v_c·sqrt(v_c² − v_F²))/2), with |v_h − v_c|/v_c ≲ 29%. For Λ ≫ 1, v_c → v_F and v_h → v_F/√2. Calculated τ_ee = 0.16/0.17 ps; the data fit better with about half that.
items.source_title: Barcons Ruiz et al., Sci. Adv. 9, eadi0415 (2023); theory from Torre et al., PRB 99, 144307 (2019), arXiv:1812.09889
items.note: [THz, 300 K] Eq. (2) is a T → 0 Fermi-liquid result with F1^s neglected.

items.item: First-sound speed deficit vs d (Barcons Eq. 2 with v_c from Eq. (1), v_F = 1e6)
items.source_title: DERIVED from Barcons Ruiz 2023 Eq. (2) and Part I Eq. (1)
items.note: The 1-THz cell sits at ωτ_ee ≈ 0.52–0.72 (record), so the real shift lies between 0 and this limit.

items.item: Cross-check of the record's kinetic speed deficit
items.value: The external first-sound bound at d = 10 nm is ≈2.6–2.8%, i.e. a ≈+10–12% density trim. The record's in-closure figure is −1.8% (+7% trim). Its single-rate kinetic operator gives ≈11% (9.6–13.4%, 353 K; +48% trim), which is 4–5× the crossover bound.
items.source_title: DERIVED: Barcons Ruiz 2023 Eq. (2) vs Part I §5/§7.5/§10
items.note: So the record's larger deficit must come from something other than the zero-to-first-sound crossover (finite temperature, or the operator's form). THz nanoscopy at 1.84–4.25 THz, as Barcons did, could tell which on the bench.

items.item: Trim authority vs d (how far a density change moves the speed)
items.value: ∂ln s/∂ln n = ½g²/((1+g)(1+2g)): 0.213 at 10 nm, 0.199 at 7, 0.183 at 5, 0.171 at 4, 0.153 at 3, 0.125 at 2, 0.075 at 1. Density trim needed to cancel the first-sound limit (linearized): +12%, +26%, +33%, +46%, +76%, +190% respectively (10, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 nm).
items.source_title: DERIVED from Eq. (1) (g ∝ k_F ∝ n^1/2)
items.note: The record's trim range is +7% to +48%. If the record's ≈11% kinetic deficit were d-independent, d = 5 nm alone would need ≈+60%.

items.item: Speed error from a ±1 hBN layer (0.333 nm) vs d
items.value: ±1.43% at 10 nm (record: 'under 2%'), ±2.47% at 5, ±2.88% at 4, ±3.45% at 3, ±4.21% at 2, ±5.01% at 1 nm. For comparison the active half-width is 2.76% of f0. Density trim to cancel it: 6.7%, 13.5%, 16.9%, 22.5%, 33.8%, 66.7%.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Eq. (1); comparison numbers from Part I §9.7
items.note: Adding first-sound trim and layer trim: 39% at 5 nm (inside +48%) but 50% at 4 nm. The trimmable window ends at d ≈ 4.5–5 nm.

items.item: Landau ceiling vs d, and the smallest workable gate distance
items.value: Ceiling M_L = 1 − v_F/s (Galilean legs of Eq. 2): 0.561 at 10 nm, 0.422 at 5, 0.313 at 3, 0.231 at 2, 0.117 at 1 nm, against M_th 0.125 (300 K) / 0.147 (353 K). The threshold reaches the ceiling at d = 1.06–1.23 nm (v_F 1e6); 1.17–1.36 nm (v_F 1.1e6); 0.95–1.06 nm with the record's Dirac-fluid drift law (drag ½, M 0.2201/0.2497); 1.57–1.68 nm with the viscous term; 1.82–1.97 nm in the first-sound limit; 2.21–2.32 nm with both.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I Eq. (1)–(3) and §5 ceiling definition, Barcons Eq. (2)
items.note: The ceiling-to-threshold ratio at 300 K falls from 4.5 (10 nm) to 3.4 (5 nm), 2.5 (3 nm), 1.85 (2 nm) and 0.94 (1 nm).

items.item: Effect of a renormalized Fermi velocity (v_F = 1.1e6 at 1e12, as computed by Barcons Ruiz)
items.value: s rises +5.7% at 10 nm, +6.3% at 5, +7.5% at 2, +8.5% at 1 nm. The ceiling still falls: 0.561 → 0.543 at 10 nm and 0.117 → 0.105 at 1 nm.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Eq. (1) with v_F from Barcons Ruiz 2023 Table S1
items.note: Lundeberg's 5.5–27 nm data agree with the bare-v_F Eq. (1) within ~1–4%, so in practice velocity renormalization and the compressibility correction largely cancel, or are absorbed into the fitted ε_z.

items.item: Alcaraz Iranzo 2018: the 'ultimate confinement' result (mid-IR)
items.value: λ0 ≈ 8 µm, E_F up to 0.54 eV, CVD graphene. Spacers: CVD monolayer hBN (0.7 nm) or 2-nm Al2O3 under metal rods (w = 33 nm, gap 37 nm). Vertical mode length ≈0.3 nm = λ0/26000. The calculated resonance width does not grow as the spacer thins. Metal nonlocal field penetration becomes significant below 3 nm. Damping from metal electron-hole pairs is weak because Im(Feibelman d) → 0 for ω ≪ ω_p. Projected single resonator: λ_p = λ0/170, V_p = 664 nm³ (~1e-9 λ0³).
items.source_title: Alcaraz Iranzo et al., Science 360, 291 (2018); arXiv:1804.01061
items.note: [mid-IR, room temperature] This is the only ultimate-confinement paper the review cites (#151).

items.item: Alcaraz Iranzo 2018: effective spacer is thicker than the 0.7-nm hBN
items.value: The data fit a uniform dielectric 3 nm thick (perfect-conductor model). The local-metal dispersion overlaps the full nonlocal one at s = 1.5 nm, against the nominal 0.7 nm.
items.source_title: Alcaraz Iranzo et al., arXiv:1804.01061
items.note: [mid-IR] At the sub-nm limit the effective electrostatic d is ×2–4 the nominal value.

items.item: Epstein 2020: single AGP cavities under metal nanocubes (mid-IR)
items.value: Ag nanocubes of 50/75/110 nm on a ~2-nm dielectric spacer over CVD graphene on SiO2. Mode volume ≈5×10^-10 λ0³ (QNM calculation 4.7×10^-10). Slowest measured AGP ≈1.42×10^6 m/s. A 3–13% nanocube fill gives a response comparable to gratings at 50–85% fill. Below 1 nm, nonlocal effects in both metal and graphene dominate. Model inputs: E_F 0.47 eV, τ = 10 fs, 300 K.
items.source_title: Epstein et al., Science 368, 1219 (2020); arXiv:2002.00366
items.note: [mid-IR, room temperature] The nanocube acts as a metal patch antenna over a graphene acoustic-plasmon cavity. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Gonçalves 2021: quantum surface response of the gate metal
items.value: Re d⊥ ≈ −0.4 nm is used as a reasonable value for Au. Effects matter for t ≲ 5 nm (framework valid for t ≳ 1 nm). Wavevector change approaches ~5% at a few nm and reaches up to ~10% at t ≈ 0.7 nm (λ0 = 11.28 µm, E_F 0.3 eV). Q is essentially unchanged. Surface-enabled Landau damping is negligible because Im d⊥ ∝ ω.
items.source_title: Gonçalves et al., Nat. Commun. 12, 3271 (2021)
items.note: [mid-IR theory] The −0.4 nm is an illustrative value, not a measurement. DERIVED: an effective d = d + 0.4 nm raises s by +1.7% at 10 nm, +2.9% at 5, +4.9% at 2, +6.0% at 1 nm. At 1 THz, ω/ω_p ~ 1e-4, so the shift remains but the extra loss does not.

items.item: Principi 2018: Landau damping in the metal gate
items.value: Landau damping from particle-hole pairs in the metal gate, including metal nonlocality, is 'surprisingly weak': Q > 10².
items.source_title: Principi, van Loon, Polini, Katsnelson, 'Confining graphene plasmons to the ultimate limit', PRB 98, 035427 (2018); arXiv:1802.06797
items.note: Already in the record: ERRATA I-43 (2026-11-03) cites it.

items.item: Gate-metal ohmic loss does not depend on d (for qd ≪ 1)
items.value: The image current in the gate equals the channel current, so the ohmic share of damping is R_s·τ/L_k = 0.287 Ω × 1 ps / 7.28e-11 H ≈ 0.4% for bulk Au at τ = 1 ps, with no d in it.
items.source_title: DERIVED (R_s and L_k from this session's earlier SPP assessment, spp_findings.txt)
items.note: Part I §4's 'adds to the budget at small d' therefore has no ohmic d-trend at 1 THz. Any d-dependence enters through metal nonlocality, which shifts s but costs little loss (Iranzo 2018; Gonçalves 2021).

items.item: Menabde 2021: acoustic plasmons in large-area CVD graphene (mid-IR)
items.value: Au / Al2O3 (8, 18, 21 nm) / CVD graphene at 1150 cm^-1, room temperature, μ ≈ 2000 cm²/Vs. λ_AGP ≈ 222 nm at 18 nm and 156 nm at 8 nm. Figure of merit 2.12 for both spacers, ×1.4 the unscreened plasmon. No cutoff as the spacer thins.
items.source_title: Menabde et al., Nat. Commun. 12, 938 (2021)
items.note: [mid-IR, room temperature] Loss per wavelength did not grow from 18 to 8 nm.

items.item: Kipp 2025: graphite gates have their own THz plasmon modes (cryogenic)
items.value: 10–17-nm graphite gates host 2D plasmon self-cavity modes at 0.25–2.5 THz. They couple ultrastrongly to the graphene plasmon: g = 50 ± 5 GHz at 0.43 THz, η = 0.12 ± 0.01. Graphene mode Q ≈ 5.7 at n = 2.85e12. Measured on-chip at 0.05–1 THz, 7–20 K.
items.note: [THz, 7–20 K] Relevant to Part I's graphite-gated disorder de-risk die.

items.item: Drive heat is tied to quanta per logic level, independent of d
items.value: P_cell / N(ε) = 4M²ħω0/(ε²τ) = 50.7 nW per quantum at a 2% swing (M = 0.0875, τ = 1 ps, 300 K). 153 quanta give 7.78 µW, reproducing Part III. Holding 406 quanta at the same 2% swing would take 20.6 µW per cell, ×2.65.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I §8.1 (P = n m* v0²/τ · A) and Part II Eq. (Q1)–(Q2) (E = ¼ n m* s² ε² A)
items.note: n, m*, s and A all cancel in the ratio. Any d (or width) change that cuts drive heat cuts the quanta at each fractional logic level by the same factor.

items.item: Drive heat and fabric energy per MAC vs d (fixed cell width, same τ, bias ratio and fractional swing)
items.value: Scale factor (s/s10)³: 0.643 at 7 nm, 0.437 at 5, 0.345 at 4, 0.261 at 3, 0.186 at 2, 0.123 at 1. At 5 nm: 3.40–4.47 µW per cell, 12.7–17.0 fJ/MAC, lane 28–38 mW. At 3 nm: 2.03–2.66 µW, 7.6–10.2 fJ/MAC. At 1 nm: 0.96–1.25 µW, 3.6–4.8 fJ/MAC. Including the viscous rise in threshold (P ∝ M_th², ×1.19 at 5 nm, ×1.40 at 3, ×1.91 at 1): 15.1–20.3, 10.6–14.2 and 6.8–9.2 fJ/MAC.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part III (7.78–10.22 µW per cell; 29–39 fJ/MAC; 64–86 mW per lane at 300 K)
items.note: Assumes the knee and fixed point stay at the same fractional swing. 1 nm is excluded by the floors below; the row is shown only for scaling.

items.item: Quanta per logic level vs d (fixed width)
items.value: Loaded fan-out-2 fixed point 99–277 → 43–121 at 5 nm, 34–95 at 4, 26–72 at 3, 18–51 at 2, 12–34 at 1 nm (DG1 needs ≥406). Fan-out-1 level 628–955 → 274–417 at 5 nm. Knee 38 → 16.6 at 5 nm. Single-plasmon swing ε1 0.16% → 0.24% at 5 nm, 0.31% at 3, 0.46% at 1 nm.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part II Eq. (Q2) (N ∝ s²A ∝ s³) and Part III DG1 numbers
items.note: The thermal 5.76 quanta at 300 K do not change with d, so decision SNR falls with confinement.

items.item: Footprint vs d
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part III (27.4 µm² per cell, lane 0.224–0.232 mm²) and Part I §3.1 (lattice pitch follows L)
items.note: The range runs from scaling one lattice axis (∝ s) to both (∝ s²). Wiring and the 384–704 launch lines are excluded, as they are in Part III.

items.item: Threshold drift velocity and current vs d (M_th = 0.125 at 300 K, d-independent)
items.value: v0,th = 2.85×10^5 m/s at 10 nm, 2.16×10^5 at 5, 1.42×10^5 at 1 nm. j_th = 0.456, 0.346, 0.227 mA/µm. The tracked 353 K bias current 0.38 mA/µm becomes ≈0.29 mA/µm at 5 nm.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I Eq. (3) and §9.2
items.note: The threshold Mach number does not improve; only the current at threshold falls.

items.item: DC field in the gate hBN vs d
items.value: E = n e/(ε0 ε) = 0.052 V/nm (ε 3.5) to 0.060 V/nm (ε 3.0) at any d; 0.077–0.089 V/nm with a +48% density trim. That is ×13–23 below breakdown (×9–16 with the trim). Gate voltage 0.634 V at 10 nm and 0.168 V at 1 nm (geometric part plus E_F/e = 0.117 V).
items.source_title: DERIVED (charge-set field) against Lee 2011 and Hattori 2015 breakdown fields
items.note: Breakdown never binds at any d. The field is fixed by the carrier density, not by the thickness.

items.item: Lee 2011: hBN breakdown and tunnelling barrier
items.value: Fowler–Nordheim analysis gives a barrier of 3.07 eV and a dielectric strength of 7.94 MV/cm (0.79 V/nm). Direct tunnelling is measurable in mono-, bi- and tri-layer hBN on Au.
items.source_title: G.-H. Lee et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 99, 243114 (2011)
items.note: Conductive-AFM measurement on Au/mica.

items.item: Hattori 2015: hBN breakdown field
items.value: ≈12 MV/cm (1.2 V/nm) out of plane, comparable to SiO2. Breakdown proceeds layer by layer.
items.source_title: Hattori, Taniguchi, Watanabe, Nagashio, ACS Nano 9, 916 (2015); arXiv:1510.01930
items.note: A 2016 follow-up reports ≈3 MV/cm in plane (APS abstract).

items.item: Britnell 2012: zero-bias tunnel conductance through thin hBN
items.value: About 1 kΩ^-1 µm^-2 for one layer, falling to about 0.1 GΩ^-1 µm^-2 for four layers (graphite electrodes, 1–4 layers = 0.3–1.3 nm). The I–V turns exponential above ≈0.5 V. Au contacts were less reproducible because hBN can delaminate from rough metal.
items.source_title: Britnell et al., Nano Lett. 12, 1707 (2012); arXiv:1202.0735
items.note: The conductance drops ≈215× per layer (derived: (10^7)^(1/3)).

items.item: Gate leakage and gate-charge retention vs hBN layer count (derived from Britnell 2012)
items.value: At the n = 1e12 gate bias of 0.13–0.19 V: 1 layer 1.3×10^4 A/cm²; 2 layers 70 A/cm² (0.1 µW/µm²); 3 layers (1.0 nm) 0.36 A/cm², 0.6 nW/µm², retention C/G ≈ 0.7 µs; 4 layers (1.33 nm) 1.9×10^-3 A/cm², ≈0.13 ms. Extrapolated: 5 layers (1.67 nm) ≈1e-5 A/cm², ≈24 ms; 6 layers (2.0 nm) ≈5e-8 A/cm², ≈5 s.
items.source_title: DERIVED from Britnell 2012 conductances; C = series of ε0·3.5/d and C_Q = 2.75 µF/cm²
items.note: Values beyond 4 layers are extrapolated (low confidence). For the gate-charge memory of Part I §6.4 this sets a floor of d ≳ 1.3–1.7 nm. At d = 5 nm (15 layers) tunnelling is negligible.

items.item: Knobloch 2021: hBN as a scaled gate insulator
items.value: Requirements: leakage < 10^-2 A/cm² at gate voltages up to 0.7 V, breakdown > 10 MV/cm. EOT 0.8 nm needs ≤0.99 nm of hBN (3 layers). Available hBN exceeds the leakage limit through trap-assisted tunnelling; even ideal hBN is mostly above it.
items.source_title: Knobloch et al., Nat. Electron. 4, 98–108 (2021), doi:10.1038/s41928-020-00529-x (numbers from the TU Wien IUE Annual Review 2021 summary)
items.note: Numbers come from the authors' institutional summary, not the paper text. That page uses ε(hBN) ≈ 5. It is consistent with the 0.36 A/cm² derived above at 3 layers.

items.item: Electrical write (issue #141): gate swing and capacitance vs d
items.value: Swing for a −0.2n depletion: 116 mV at 10 nm, 64 at 5, 33 at 2, 23 mV at 1 nm (geometric part ∝ d plus a fixed 12.3 mV quantum part). Series gate capacitance: 0.28, 0.51, 0.75 (3 nm), 0.99, 1.46 µF/cm² (quantum capacitance 2.75 µF/cm²).
items.source_title: DERIVED (record: −0.17…−0.28 n write; gate RC unmodelled)
items.note: The record prices neither write energy nor RC.

items.item: Plasmon generation by tunnelling (review ref. #126) and its predecessor
items.value: de Vega & García de Abajo 2019: in metal–insulator–graphene the inelastic-tunnelling efficiency is several orders of magnitude below double-layer graphene; a 4° twist keeps ~20% of the aligned maximum. de Vega 2017: graphene–hBN–graphene gives a unity-order yield per tunnelled electron, about 10^12–10^14 plasmons/s per λ_p².
items.source_title: de Vega & García de Abajo, PRB 99, 115438 (2019), arXiv:1812.10109; ACS Photonics (2017), arXiv:1706.09674
items.note: Theory, aimed at IR. The generation is spontaneous and incoherent.

items.item: Svintsov 2016: plasmon gain from stimulated tunnelling
items.value: Predicts plasmon amplification by stimulated tunnelling in graphene–insulator–graphene; with a suitable barrier the gain can match or exceed Drude and interband loss. The abstract gives no numbers.
items.source_title: Svintsov, Devizorova, Otsuji, Ryzhii, PRB 94, 115301 (2016); arXiv:1509.03776
items.note: Theory only. Not found quantified at 1 THz and 300 K.

items.item: Part II blockade limit compared with what d-scaling offers
items.value: Record: χ/κ ≈ 8.2×10^-6 at 4 K; blockade would need ≈3-nm cells (χ ∝ 1/A). DERIVED: shrinking d at fixed width raises per-quantum nonlinearity by at most 1/r³: ×2.3 at 5 nm, ×8 at 1 nm, against the ≈1.2×10^5 needed.
items.source_title: Fable Computer Part II v2.1 §3–4, plus derived scaling
items.note: Already in the record.

items.item: Carrier-frequency floor if d is reduced
items.value: At 0.5 THz the quarter wave is 650 nm with d = 2 nm, vs 1,140 nm at 10 nm. But M_th = 1/(8f0τ) rises to 0.25 (τ 1 ps), and n̄ at 300 K rises to 12.0 (vs 5.76 at 1 THz).
items.source_title: DERIVED from Part I §1, Eq. (1) and Eq. (3)
items.note: A smaller d would relax Part I §1's footprint floor but costs gain and decision quanta.

items.item: Launch mitigations already named in the record
items.value: Part I §9.5 lists, in order of maturity: photoconductive launch (4 K); tapered-gate impedance transformers; a resonant antenna-coupled gate segment. A graphene patch antenna (Haque [8], simulation only, 3.75–6.46 THz) is the free-space option.
items.source_title: Fable Computer Part I v6.1 §9.5 and §3.3
items.note: Epstein 2020's nanocube is a measured mid-IR case of a metal patch over an acoustic-plasmon cavity. No 1-THz coupling efficiency was found.

items.item: Record's ε_z band vs its design speed
items.value: Part I gives ε_z ≈ 3.4–3.8 and s ≈ 2.2–2.3×10^6; computed, that band gives 2.20–2.31×10^6. The design 2.33×10^6 needs ε_z = 3.32, the value in constants.py (band 3.3–3.8).
items.source_title: DERIVED; Part I Table 3 and §5 vs fable-model-chain/constants.py
items.note: A minor labelling inconsistency of about 1%; no number moves.

items.item: Process note: privacy slip in this run
items.value: One curl request to arxiv.org (the arXiv:1804.01061 PDF) carried the user's email address in its User-Agent header by mistake. No other request did, and the repository was only read, never modified.
items.source_title: This assessment run
items.note: Disclosed for transparency.

mapping.fable_problem: Cell length L ≈ 576 nm and the gate-lattice pitch (footprint; Part I Table 3, §3.1)
mapping.reason: L = (s/4f0)(1−M²) is proportional to s, and Eq. (1) lowers s as d shrinks. The record's own d = 5 nm die is 441 nm at zero drift. Measured speeds (Lundeberg 2017, 5.5–27 nm) agree with Eq. (1) within about 4%.
mapping.what_must_be_true: (1) The electrostatic d must really be reached. Barcons Ruiz 2023's 2.0-nm hBN on a pre-patterned Pd gate behaved like ≈7.1 nm because of a fitted 1.46-nm air gap, so evaporated top gates or flat gates are needed. (2) The ±1-layer speed error (±2.5% at 5 nm, against a 2.76% active half-width) plus the first-sound shift (up to −4.7% at 5 nm) must stay inside the record's +48% density-trim range; linearized, that holds only down to d ≈ 4.5–5 nm. (3) The lattice pitch must keep following L.
mapping.quantified_effect: 576.6 → 436 nm at d = 5 nm (−24%) and 403 nm at 4 nm (−30%), with ε_z 3.32 at the 353 K bias; 366 nm at 3 nm is outside the trim window.

mapping.fable_problem: Area per cell 27.4 µm² (1 µm² active, 3.6% fill) and lane area 0.224–0.232 mm² (Part III)
mapping.reason: The lattice sites scale with the plasmon wavelength, so area falls as s (one axis) to s² (both axes).
mapping.what_must_be_true: The conditions of the cell-length row. The gain does not touch the binding area items: wiring and the 384–704 launch lines, which Part III does not model (limitations 3 and 12).
mapping.quantified_effect: 15.8–20.8 µm² per cell and 0.129–0.176 mm² per lane at d = 5 nm (×0.58–0.76).

mapping.fable_problem: Drive heat 7.78–10.22 µW per cell and fabric energy 29–39 fJ/MAC at 300 K (Part III)
mapping.reason: The bias Mach number 0.7·M_th does not depend on d, so drift velocity v0 = M·s falls with s, Joule density n m* v0²/τ falls as s², and active area falls as s at fixed width; per-cell heat goes as s³. Cells per MAC and slot rate do not change.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Same τ under the closer gate (Barcons 2023 saw no penalty: τ 0.44 ps at d_eq ≈ 7 nm vs 0.30 ps at ≈33 nm, two devices) and the same fractional logic swing. Critically, it also requires that DG1 does not need the quanta it removes. P_cell = 4M²·N·ħω0/(ε²τ), so at fixed decision quanta the energy gain is zero; d trades energy for quanta one-for-one.
mapping.quantified_effect: ×0.437 at 5 nm: 3.40–4.47 µW per cell, 12.7–17.0 fJ/MAC, 28–38 mW per lane. With the viscous rise in threshold (×1.19), 15.1–20.3 fJ/MAC. At 3 nm, 7.6–14.2 fJ/MAC, but 3 nm is outside the trim window.

mapping.fable_problem: DG1 decision quanta: ≥406 needed at 300 K vs 99–277 sustained by a loaded fan-out-2 cascade (Part III)
mapping.reason: This gets WORSE; the schema has no 'worsens' value. Mode energy at a fixed fractional swing is ¼ n m* s² ε² A, proportional to s³ at fixed width, so the knee, the fixed point and the rail all lose quanta as d shrinks, while the 5.76 thermal quanta do not change. Confinement trades decision quanta one-for-one against drive energy.
mapping.what_must_be_true: No d makes this better, unless decisions are taken on a re-launched, larger swing. Restoring the quanta needs width ∝ 1/s³, which brings P_cell back to 7.78–10.22 µW and grows active area ∝ 1/s².
mapping.quantified_effect: Fan-out-2 fixed point 99–277 → 43–121 quanta at 5 nm, 26–72 at 3 nm, 12–34 at 1 nm. Fan-out-1 level 628–955 → 274–417 at 5 nm.

mapping.fable_problem: DS threshold M_th = L/(2sτ) ≈ 1/(8f0τ) = 0.125 at 300 K (Part I Eq. (3))
mapping.reason: Part I already states M_th is independent of s and d once the cell is tuned to f0. Confinement only lowers the threshold drift and current. It also lowers the Landau ceiling M_L = 1 − v_F/s toward the threshold, which hurts.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Any use of d < 5 nm needs the ceiling to stay well above the threshold. Collisionless, it stays ≥2.5× down to 3 nm.
mapping.quantified_effect: j_th falls 0.456 → 0.346 (5 nm) → 0.227 mA/µm (1 nm). M_L falls 0.561 → 0.422 → 0.313 (3 nm) → 0.117 (1 nm). The threshold meets the ceiling at d ≈ 1.06–1.23 nm (collisionless), 1.57–1.68 nm with the viscous term, 1.82–1.97 nm in the first-sound limit, 2.2–2.3 nm with both.

mapping.fable_problem: G1: single-cell per-pulse net gain ≥ +2.6 dB at ≤ 80 °C, and whether a 353 K threshold exists
mapping.reason: Part I §10's die plan already carries a d = 5 nm variant, scored as a '+2.6 dB-class' lever at the hydrodynamic tier. ERRATA I-40 and note 2026-10-15 record that the single-rate kinetic operator at 353 K finds no threshold for it (best Im ω −0.190). Below 5 nm the side effects of confinement only add damping, detuning and ceiling pressure.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A d-based gain lever would need the kinetic tier, or the bench, to confirm the hydrodynamic +2.6 dB.
mapping.quantified_effect: Relative to 10 nm at 300 K, damping rises ×1.09 (5 nm), ×1.18 (3 nm), ×1.38 (1 nm) (viscous estimate). The first-sound speed deficit grows from −2.6% to −4.7% (5 nm) and −14.3% (1 nm).

mapping.fable_problem: Gate dielectric below 5 nm: breakdown, leakage, and the gate-charge memory (Part I §6.4: 'the bit's persistent home is the charge on a cell's gate'; §9.3 kHz–MHz programming)
mapping.reason: This is a constraint, not an improvement, and the record does not cover it. Breakdown never binds, because the field is set by the carrier density: 0.052–0.060 V/nm at any d, 0.077–0.089 V/nm with a +48% trim, ×9–23 below 0.79–1.2 V/nm (Lee 2011; Hattori 2015). Direct tunnelling does bind: from Britnell 2012, 3 layers (1.0 nm) leak 0.36 A/cm² (×36 the 1e-2 A/cm² low-power limit cited by Knobloch 2021) and hold gate charge for only ≈0.7 µs; 4 layers (1.33 nm) leak 1.9e-3 A/cm² and hold ≈0.13 ms.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.
mapping.quantified_effect: Floor of d ≳ 1.3–1.7 nm (4–5 layers) for ms-class gate-charge retention. Leakage power is negligible down to 3 layers (0.6 nW/µm² against ~1 µW per cell), but reaches 0.1 µW/µm² at 2 layers and 18 µW/µm² at 1 layer. Tunnelling is negligible at the d = 5 nm die (15 layers).

mapping.fable_problem: Passive loss budget: 27.3/Q dB per λ_p (4.3 dB at Q 6.3) and 2.17 dB per λ_p/2 gate at 300 K
mapping.reason: To first order, loss per wavelength (and so per cell and per gate) does not change, because Q = ωτ is fixed. Measurements agree: Menabde 2021 (mid-IR) figure of merit 2.12 at both 18 and 8 nm; Iranzo 2018 calculated widths do not grow down to 0.7 nm; Barcons 2023 τ 0.44 ps at d_eq ≈ 7 nm vs 0.30 ps at ≈33 nm. Loss per mm rises as 1/s, and the record's own hydrodynamic viscous term rises as 1/s². The net is neutral to adverse; neither improves it.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.
mapping.quantified_effect: 1.91 → 2.51 (5 nm) → 3.84 dB/µm (1 nm) at Q 6.3. Per-gate loss including viscous damping: 2.48 dB (10 nm) → 2.71 (5 nm) → 3.43 dB (1 nm), 300 K, derived.

mapping.fable_problem: Gate-metal ohmic loss 'adds to the budget at small d' (Part I §4)
mapping.reason: ERRATA I-43 (2026-11-03) already corrected the citation and cites Principi 2018 (metal-gate Landau damping weak, Q > 10²) and Dias 2018. Derived refinement: for qd ≪ 1 the gate's image current equals the channel current, so the ohmic share R_s·τ/L_k ≈ 0.4% (bulk Au, τ = 1 ps) has no d in it. Metal nonlocality (Re d⊥ ≈ −0.4 nm for Au, illustrative) shifts the effective d, but its loss vanishes as ω/ω_p → 0 (Iranzo 2018; Gonçalves 2021).
mapping.what_must_be_true: The gate stays thick and bulk-like. A thin Pd gate raises R_s; this session's earlier SPP assessment estimated ≈23% of the damping for a 15-nm Pd gate, against ≈0.4% for bulk Au.
mapping.quantified_effect: No d-trend in ohmic metal loss at 1 THz. Speed shift from d⊥: +1.7% at 10 nm to +6.0% at 1 nm.

mapping.fable_problem: Mode speed below Eq. (1) and the density trim it demands (+7% in-closure to +48% kinetic; Part I §5, §7.5, §10)
mapping.reason: Part I already cites [10] (Barcons Ruiz 2023) for the zero-to-first-sound crossover at 1 THz (ωτ_ee ≈ 0.7). New cross-check from that paper's Eq. (2): at d = 10 nm the full first-sound limit is only −2.6 to −2.8% (≈+10–12% trim), and the measured shift was ≈5% at d_eq ≈ 7 nm. The record's ≈11% (9.6–13.4%) kinetic deficit at 353 K is 4–5× this bound, so it must come from something other than the crossover — a question the bench can answer. Below 5 nm the deficit grows while trim authority shrinks.
mapping.what_must_be_true: For use as a bench discriminant: THz nanoscopy or cavity-line measurements at about 1–4 THz on the d = 10 nm stack.

mapping.fable_problem: Validity and labelling of Eq. (1) (Part I §5, citing [39, 40])
mapping.reason: Eq. (1) is algebraically Principi 2011's RPA c_s, and it reproduces Lundeberg 2017's n = 1e12 speeds at 5.5, 14.5 and 27 nm within 0.1–1.2% (ε_z 3.32) or 2–4% (ε_z 3.5), read off the figure. Two minor record points. First, Part I calls Eq. (1) 'gated local-RPA', but it is the nonlocal RPA; the local (Drude) speed is 7.9% lower at 10 nm and 70% lower at 1 nm. Second, the design s = 2.33e6 needs ε_z = 3.32, just below the 3.4–3.8 band Part I quotes.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.
mapping.quantified_effect: No number moves.

mapping.fable_problem: Launch and read-out coupling into the acoustic mode (unquantified at 300 K; Part I §3.3, §9.5)
mapping.reason: Part I §9.5 already names tapered-gate impedance transformers and a resonant antenna-coupled gate segment. Epstein 2020 is the first measured case of a metal patch over an acoustic-plasmon cavity excited from free space (mid-IR, Ag nanocubes; a 3–13% fill matches gratings at 50–85%). That supports the antenna-segment idea, but no THz or stripline-coupling efficiency was found. A thinner d widens the mismatch the transducer must bridge (record, ERRATA I-42: ≈3% coupling under the Au gate vs 30–35% under ZnO, at 4 K).
mapping.what_must_be_true: An antenna or taper with a demonstrated 1-THz coupling efficiency at 300 K.
mapping.quantified_effect: Not found at 1 THz.

mapping.fable_problem: Electrical write by gate depletion and read by rectification (issue #141; gate RC unmodelled)
mapping.reason: A thinner d lowers the write voltage, since the geometric part scales with d and only a fixed 12.3 mV quantum part remains. But gate capacitance per area climbs toward the 2.75 µF/cm² quantum capacitance, so RC per cell rises. The record prices neither the write energy nor the RC.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A priced #141 write and read with its gate RC modelled.
mapping.quantified_effect: −0.2n write swing: 116 mV (10 nm) → 64 (5) → 33 (2) → 23 mV (1). Series gate capacitance: 0.28 → 0.51 → 0.99 → 1.46 µF/cm².

mapping.fable_problem: Part II quantum regime: single-plasmon Kerr χ/κ ≈ 8.2e-6; blockade would need ≈3-nm cells
mapping.reason: Part II already states the confinement requirement (χ ∝ 1/A) and excludes gate-model quantum logic. Shrinking d at fixed width raises per-quantum nonlinearity by at most 1/r³.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.
mapping.quantified_effect: ×2.3 at 5 nm, ≤×8 at 1 nm, against the ≈1.2×10^5 needed.

mapping.fable_problem: Carrier frequency set near 1 THz (Part I §1: below ~0.5 THz the cell outgrows the ~500-nm pitch)
mapping.reason: A smaller d would let 0.5 THz keep a ~650-nm cell (d = 2 nm) instead of 1,140 nm. But M_th = 1/(8f0τ) doubles to 0.25 and thermal occupancy doubles to 12 quanta at 300 K, so the move costs gain and decision quanta.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.
mapping.quantified_effect: Not an improvement.

mapping.fable_problem: Clock and slot rate (69-GHz fan-out-2 frontier) and per-bit speed
mapping.reason: To first order, f0 and Q = ωτ do not depend on d. The only d-dependent change is the viscous term, which lowers the effective Q by 9% (5 nm) to 38% (1 nm); the frontier would need a re-run, and that change can only slow it.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.
mapping.quantified_effect: No speed gain.

mapping.fable_problem: Alternative launch or gain using tunnelling through thin hBN (double-layer graphene instead of a metal gate)
mapping.reason: Review ref. #126 (de Vega & García de Abajo 2019): plasmon generation by inelastic tunnelling is several orders of magnitude weaker in metal–insulator–graphene than in graphene–hBN–graphene, where de Vega 2017 predicts a unity-order yield (10^12–10^14 plasmons/s per λ_p²). Svintsov 2016 predicts stimulated-tunnelling gain that can exceed Drude loss. All of this is theory and mostly infrared. Spontaneous emission is incoherent, so it is noise unless stimulated.
