A graphene 'gate' also gives up the metal gate's AC short at the DS source boundary (ERRATA I-41).
mapping.what_must_be_true: Coherent, stimulated tunnelling gain at 1 THz and 300 K, phase-locked to the clock, plus some substitute for the gate-referenced source short.
mapping.quantified_effect: Not quantified at 1 THz.

mapping.fable_problem: Graphite-gated disorder de-risk die (Part I §10)
mapping.reason: Kipp 2025 (7–20 K): 10–17-nm graphite gates host their own 2D plasmon modes at 0.25–2.5 THz, which couple ultrastrongly (η = 0.12) to the graphene plasmon. At 1 THz a graphite gate is a resonator, not a passive ground; its mode would have to be placed away from f0 or damped. Cryogenic data only.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The graphite gate's self-mode is designed off 1 THz, or the die uses a bulk metal gate.
mapping.quantified_effect: η = 0.12 ± 0.01 (g = 50 GHz at 0.43 THz), measured at 7–20 K.

mapping.fable_problem: The review's headline 'ultimate confinement' results (vertical mode length 0.3 nm = λ0/26000; mode volume ≈5e-10 λ0³)
mapping.reason: These are mid-IR results (λ0 ≈ 8–11 µm, CVD graphene, τ ≈ 10 fs in the model). Alcaraz Iranzo 2018 is cited by the review as ref. 151; Epstein 2020 is not. At 1 THz in-plane compression saturates at c/v_F ≈ λ0/300, only ×2.3 beyond the design's λ0/129, and vertical confinement and mode volume enter no Fable number. What does carry over: at sub-3-nm spacers the effective d is ×2–4 the nominal value (Iranzo's fit, Barcons' air gap).
mapping.what_must_be_true: Not applicable.

items.item: Electrical-pulse-to-plasmon conversion efficiency, headline (Yoshioka et al., Part I ref [4])
items.value: ≈30% (arXiv abstract) and 'up to 35%' (journal abstract). Wave packets are 1.2 ps long, confined to 2.1×10⁻¹⁸ m³ in 3D, and injected through an ohmic contact from a coplanar waveguide fed by an LT-GaAs photoconductive switch. The authors credit the efficiency to the absence of a momentum mismatch.
items.source_title: Yoshioka et al., 'On-chip transfer of ultrashort graphene plasmon wave packets using terahertz electronics', Nat. Electron. 7, 537–544 (2024), arXiv:2311.02821
items.note: On-chip galvanic launch: no antenna, grating or metasurface. This is the only measured launch efficiency into any gated graphene plasmon that I found. Access limits: the arXiv PDFs (12.6 and 13.8 MB) exceed the fetch limit; nature.com redirected to a sign-in/cookie flow; ResearchGate returned 403; IA Scholar showed a bot check. None of these was bypassed.

items.item: Per-device split: unscreened (ZnO gate) vs acoustic (Au gate) launch efficiency, Yoshioka et al.
items.value: η ≈ 0.35 for the unscreened mode (THz-transparent ZnO top gate, 72-nm top hBN, v ~10⁷ m/s). η ≈ 0.03 for the acoustic mode (Au top gate, 35-nm top hBN, v ~10⁶ m/s). The authors attribute the Au-gate shortfall to impedance mismatch from the large velocity difference to the CPW pulse, plus the metal gate. η is defined as transmittance (squared plasmon/input amplitude ratio), which they state is a lower bound.
items.source_title: Yoshioka et al., arXiv:2311.02821 v2, conclusions and Fig. 5 (search-indexed text)
items.note: I did not read these values in the PDF; they come from search-engine indexing of the arXiv full text, which matches the prior session's finding. The ordering Au < ZnO is medium confidence: NTT's release says the ZnO gate raises the efficiency and the Au gate gives confinement. Laser Focus World printed '3% maximum', likely the Au-gate value. Fable's d = 10 nm makes the CPW-to-plasmon velocity mismatch larger than at 35 nm (s ∝ √d), so by the authors' own explanation the Au-gate value should not improve at Fable's spacing. That is a qualitative inference, not a measurement.

items.item: Measurement temperature of Yoshioka et al.
items.value: 4 K, in vacuum, for all measurements
items.source_title: Yoshioka et al., arXiv:2311.02821 (search-indexed Methods); also Fable Part I §3.1 and Table 2
items.note: Already in the record: Part I §3.1 says the demonstration was at 4 K. No 300-K launch efficiency exists for any gated graphene plasmon (searched to 2026-11-03).

items.item: Light-to-propagating-plasmon launch efficiency quoted in the NTT press release
items.value: ≈0.005% (conventional optical excitation), against 'maximum 35%' for the electrical launch after gate-material optimization; 0–2 THz bandwidth
items.source_title: NTT press release 'Electrical generation, propagation control, and detection of the ultrashort graphene plasmon wave packets' (EN), and the Japanese release
items.note: Press, not primary. The Japanese release (https://digitalpr.jp/r/92021) cites Nat. Photonics 12, 22 (2018) for the 0.005% figure. That paper is a UCLA study (Yao B. et al., next item), not NTT's own, which corrects the prior session's 'NTT optical launch 0.005%'. Derived: 10 aJ × 5×10⁻⁵ = 0.5 zJ = 0.75 quanta at 1 THz (hf = 0.6626 zJ).

items.item: All-optical (difference-frequency) generation of THz graphene plasmons on a SiN waveguide (source of the 0.005%)
items.value: Gate-tunable plasmons at 4.7–9.4 THz. On-chip plasmon power is 'order of single nW' at ≤32 mW pump and 1.4 W signal. Normalized efficiency η = I_SP/(I_s·I_p) peaks at ≈6×10⁻⁵ W⁻¹ and approaches 10⁻⁴ W⁻¹ at E_F ≈ 0.13 eV. Earlier free-space nonlinear schemes reached up to 10⁻⁵.
items.source_title: Yao B. et al., 'Broadband gate-tunable terahertz plasmons in graphene heterostructures', Nat. Photon. 12, 22 (2018), arXiv:1710.01940
items.note: Unscreened, mid-THz modes. Temperature not stated. This is not a THz-to-acoustic-mode launch.

items.item: Acoustic THz plasmons imaged by photocurrent nanoscopy (Alonso-González et al., Part I ref [39])
items.value: At 2.52 THz (λ0 = 118.8 µm) and room temperature: λp ≈ λ0/66, group velocity ≈ 0.014c, lifetime ≈ 0.5 ps. Plasmons are launched by the s-SNOM tip near field and detected thermoelectrically at the split-gate pn junction. No launch efficiency is reported.
items.source_title: Alonso-González et al., 'Acoustic terahertz graphene plasmons revealed by photocurrent nanoscopy', Nat. Nanotechnol. 12, 31–35 (2017), arXiv:1601.05753
items.note: The split gate here is the detector (pn junction), not a far-field antenna. Already in the record (Part I §4, τ 0.4–0.6 ps baseline).

items.item: Status of tip, grating and metal-taper launch at mid-IR/THz
items.value: Tip-launch efficiency is unknown and expected to be low. Grating couplers on waveguides need a coupling length of order the incident wavelength. At mid-IR and THz, metal tapers compress the mode diameter but do not provide the needed wavelength reduction.
items.source_title: Nikitin, Alonso-González, Hillenbrand, 'Efficient coupling of light to graphene plasmons by compressing surface polaritons with tapered bulk materials', Nano Lett. 14, 2896 (2014), arXiv:1805.01362
items.note: Applied to Fable: a metal stripline taper alone cannot reach λp = 2.33 µm (λ0/129). The compression must happen in the 2D sheet itself, by grading the gate distance or density.

items.item: Taper-compression coupler efficiency (simulation)
items.value: >25% photon-to-graphene-plasmon conversion at 877 cm⁻¹ (≈26.3 THz). A SiC phonon-polariton slab tapers 400→50 nm (optimum angle 11.5–15°, ~1.3 µm long). The untapered 50-nm-slab-to-graphene step alone gives ≈70%, so taper loss dominates. Graphene assumed at E_F 0.44 eV, τ 0.5 ps, 150 nm above the slab.
items.source_title: Nikitin et al., Nano Lett. 14, 2896 (2014), arXiv:1805.01362
items.note: Simulation, mid-IR. The only quantified taper coupler into graphene plasmons I found. No measured THz or acoustic-mode taper/transformer efficiency was found (searched to 2026-11-03).

items.item: Dipole-antenna split gates launching acoustic plasmons in CVD graphene (De Fazio et al., Part III ref [43])
items.value: Antenna lobes are the split gates: 40-µm dipole, 200-nm gap, ~40-nm AlOx, L ≈ 2 µm. Acoustic resonances at 1.83–2.52 THz appear from 6 to 90 K (abstract) and are gone by ≈130 K. Q ≈ 0.8–2.0 (τp 0.05–0.13 ps). At 6 K and 2.5 THz: ~12 V/W, NEP ≈ 100 pW/√Hz, ~40% photoresponse modulation. No coupling efficiency, antenna efficiency or absorbed fraction is reported.
items.source_title: De Fazio et al., 'Enhanced Terahertz Photoresponse via Acoustic Plasmon Cavity Resonances in Scalable Graphene', arXiv:2601.16604
items.note: Cryogenic only. The authors call the antenna an 'efficient launcher and receiver' qualitatively. Already in the record (Part III limitation 1).

items.item: Room-temperature resonant gated-plasmon THz detection with a bow-tie antenna between top gate and source (Caridad et al.)
items.value: At 4.7 THz, resonant gate-voltage oscillations persist up to 300 K. Device: L_TG 4.8 µm, top hBN 28 nm, μ > 60,000 cm²/Vs at 300 K, transport τ ≈ 0.23 ps (Q > 6 at 4.7 THz), plasmon τp ≈ 0.6 ps from linewidths. λp is 0.6–2.1 µm over 2.5–4.7 THz (compression up to 110). Responsivity is 0.29 A/W at 0.3 THz and 1.8 mA/W at 4.7 THz (spot-area-normalized). No coupling efficiency is reported.
items.source_title: Caridad et al., 'Room-Temperature Plasmon-Assisted Resonant THz Detection in Single-Layer Graphene Transistors', Nano Lett. 24, 935–942 (2024), arXiv:2401.04005
items.note: Derived: at 1 THz the same RT τ gives Q = 2π×10¹²×0.23×10⁻¹² = 1.45 (3.77 at τp 0.6 ps). The resonance this paper shows at 300 K would be near-overdamped at Fable's carrier.

items.item: Antenna-coupled resonant THz detection with gated bilayer-graphene plasmons (Bandurin et al.)
items.value: 0.13–2 THz, broadband bow-tie/spiral antennas with Si lens. Resonances clear at 10 K, persisting to ~77 K, none at room temperature. Q 4–11 at 2 THz (0.2–0.7 at 0.13 THz), τp 0.3–0.9 ps, λp/λ0 = 1/50–1/150, top hBN ~80 nm, L 3–6 µm. Power reaching the antenna ≈ P/3.5 (lens and window losses). Fitted antenna impedance ≈ 74 Ω. NEP ≈ 0.2 pW/√Hz (Johnson-noise estimate).
items.source_title: Bandurin et al., 'Resonant terahertz detection using graphene plasmons', Nat. Commun. 9, 5392 (2018)
items.note: Derived: P/3.5 = 5.4 dB of free-space optics loss before any antenna-to-plasmon step. No antenna-to-plasmon efficiency is given.

items.item: Antenna-driven plasma waves in a graphene FET channel imaged at room temperature (Soltani et al.)
items.value: At 2 THz and room temperature, plasma waves are overdamped: decay time 25–70 fs, decay length 0.3–0.5 µm, speed 3.5–7×10⁶ m/s (THz s-SNOM, free-electron-laser source)
items.source_title: Soltani et al., 'Direct nanoscopic observation of plasma waves in the channel of a graphene field-effect transistor', Light Sci. Appl. 9, 97 (2020)
items.note: Antenna coupling into a gated channel works at RT, but in scalable (non-premium) graphene the wave decays within ~0.5 µm. No efficiency reported.

items.item: On-chip stripline coupling to graphene plasmons in a graphite-gate cavity (Kipp et al.)
items.value: On-chip THz spectroscopy (0.1–1 THz) at 20 K on a ~10×10 µm² hBN/graphene/graphite cavity. Stripline modes couple to graphene plasmons through unscreened currents in the gaps between metal strips, with strength set by the strip-to-gap width ratio. Ultrastrong coupling: g/ν0 = 0.12 ± 0.01 (2g = 50 ± 5 GHz at 0.43 THz). The s = 2 mode has Q ≈ 5.7 at 2.85×10¹² cm⁻². No coupling efficiency or transmission percentage is reported.
items.source_title: Kipp et al., 'Cavity electrodynamics of van der Waals heterostructures', Nat. Phys. 21, 1926 (2025), arXiv:2403.19745
items.note: Same group as Fable's launcher precedent (Kusyak [7]). Gives the mechanism behind Part I §9.4's 'ungated sliver' coupling, cryogenic, without a loss number.

items.item: Antenna-coupled graphene TeraFET magnetoplasmons (Delgado-Notario et al.)
items.value: Same geometry as Caridad (L_ch 6 µm, L_TG 4.8 µm, bow-tie between source and top gate). At 1.7 K: resonant at 2.5–3.8 THz (QCL 2.5–16 mW), non-resonant at 0.22–0.33 THz. No efficiency reported.
items.source_title: Delgado-Notario et al., 'Resonant Dyakonov–Shur Magnetoplasmons in Graphene Terahertz Photodetectors', arXiv:2512.00180
items.note: Cryogenic.

items.item: Split-gate dipole-antenna graphene pn-junction THz detector (non-plasmonic) (Castilla et al.)
items.value: Room temperature, 1.8–4.2 THz, ~100-nm antenna gap, photothermoelectric detection. NEP ≈ 80 pW/√Hz; response <30 ns (setup-limited).
items.source_title: Castilla et al., 'Fast and Sensitive Terahertz Detection Using an Antenna-Integrated Graphene pn Junction', Nano Lett. 19, 2765 (2019), arXiv:1905.01881
items.note: Abstract-level via search. Room-temperature precedent for the split-gate-as-antenna geometry, as a detector.

items.item: Total/complete light absorption in patterned graphene (Thongrattanasiri, Koppens, García de Abajo) — theory
items.value: A thin layer in a symmetric environment absorbs at most 50%. 100% is reached under total internal reflection or over a dielectric-coated metal, at critical coupling, when the particle extinction cross-section (σ_max ≈ (3λ²/2π)·κr/κ) is comparable to the unit-cell area. Example: 60-nm disks, E_F 0.4 eV, μ = 10⁴ cm²/Vs, 1.12-µm dielectric on Au, infrared.
items.source_title: Thongrattanasiri, Koppens, García de Abajo, 'Complete optical absorption in periodically patterned graphene', PRL 108, 047401 (2012), arXiv:1106.4460
items.note: Theory, IR. Absorption is into localized, dissipative disk modes, not into a propagating mode. Low & Avouris (ACS Nano 8, 1086, 2014; arXiv:1403.2799) still listed complete absorption as an undemonstrated proposal in 2014.

items.item: Field enhancement in graphene nanostructure dimers — theory (Thongrattanasiri & García de Abajo)
items.value: Field enhancement beyond noble metals of similar size; armchair edges >10× stronger than zigzag; ~200-nm dimers predicted to give IR-absorption enhancement ~10⁸
items.source_title: Thongrattanasiri & García de Abajo, 'Optical field enhancement by strong plasmon interaction in graphene nanostructures', PRL 110, 187401 (2013)
items.note: Abstract via Europe PMC. IR, theory; no bearing on a 1-THz launch.

items.item: Gate-tunable metasurface perfect absorber / modulator (Yao, Shankar, Kats et al.)
items.value: Antennas on graphene in a sub-λ0/10 cavity. Gate switching in and out of critical coupling gives modulation depth 'up to 100%' (stated as achievable). Modulators demonstrated up to 20 GHz over 5–7 µm. The authors claim scalability from near-IR to THz.
items.source_title: Yao et al., 'Electrically Tunable Metasurface Perfect Absorbers for Ultrathin Mid-Infrared Optical Modulators', Nano Lett. 14, 6526 (2014)
items.note: Abstract via Europe PMC. Mid-IR, free-space, localized absorption. 20 GHz is below Fable's 69-Gb/s lines.

items.item: Antenna-enhanced mid-IR graphene photodetector (Yao et al.)
items.value: ≈0.4 V/W at λ0 = 4.45 µm at room temperature, >200× devices without antennas (<2 mV/W)
items.source_title: Yao et al., 'High-responsivity mid-infrared graphene detectors with antenna-enhanced photocarrier generation and collection', Nano Lett. 14, 3749 (2014)
items.note: Mid-IR; not plasmon launch.

items.item: Electrically tunable damping of plasmonic resonances with graphene (Emani et al.)
items.value: Large-area graphene electrically tunes the width of a metal plasmonic resonance at IR; effect stronger at mid-IR. No numerical depth, wavelength or speed in the abstract.
items.source_title: Emani et al., Nano Lett. 12, 5202 (2012)
items.note: Abstract only; no numbers found.

items.item: Graphene on plasmonic Fano-resonant metasurfaces (Dabidian et al. 2015)
items.value: Reflectivity modulation of nearly an order of magnitude (journal); modulation depth up to 90% (arXiv:1405.0991 preprint); mid-IR
items.source_title: Dabidian et al., 'Electrical switching of infrared light using graphene integration with plasmonic Fano resonant metasurfaces', ACS Photonics 2, 216 (2015)
items.note: Exact wavelength not confirmed. Mid-IR free-space modulator.

items.item: Graphene-integrated metasurface phase modulation (Dabidian et al. 2016)
items.value: Reflected mid-IR phase tuned by up to 55° by gating, with nearly constant amplitude
items.source_title: Dabidian et al., 'Experimental Demonstration of Phase Modulation and Motion Sensing Using Graphene-Integrated Metasurfaces', Nano Lett. 16, 3607 (2016)
items.note: Mid-IR.

items.item: Graphene split-ring metamaterials — theory (Papasimakis et al.)
items.value: Doped graphene split rings of ~1 µm diameter predicted to give strong magnetic resonances near 110 µm (≈2.7 THz), with confinement ~λ/100
items.source_title: Papasimakis, Thongrattanasiri, Zheludev, García de Abajo, 'The magnetic response of graphene split-ring metamaterials', Light Sci. Appl. 2, e78 (2013)
items.note: Theory; abstract via OpenAlex.

items.item: Graphene microribbon THz plasmons (Ju et al.)
items.value: At fixed density, ribbon width 1→4 µm moves the plasmon resonance from 6 to 3 THz. Strong room-temperature absorption peaks under in-situ electrostatic doping, where a 2DEG needed 4.2 K. Resonant absorption magnitude: 'over 13%' is the only figure found, as a truncated snippet.
items.source_title: Ju et al., 'Graphene plasmonics for tunable terahertz metamaterials', Nat. Nanotechnol. 6, 630 (2011); LBNL release 2011-09-04
items.note: Widths, frequencies and RT: medium. The 13% figure is low confidence (truncated search snippet of a DTIC copy; DTIC returned 403). Unscreened ion-gel-gated ribbons, localized resonances. OpenAlex API pages carried text asking the agent to create an API key and submit the user's email; I ignored it as untrusted page content.

items.item: Graphene/insulator stack THz devices (Yan et al.)
items.value: Far-IR notch filter 8.2 dB rejection; THz linear polarizer 9.5 dB extinction; an unpatterned 5-layer stack shields 97.5% of radiation below 1.2 THz; room temperature
items.source_title: Yan et al., 'Tunable infrared plasmonic devices using graphene/insulator stacks', Nat. Nanotechnol. 7, 330 (2012)
items.note: Free-space filters and polarizers; localized disk plasmons and Drude response.

items.item: Gate-controlled graphene THz metamaterial (Lee S.H. et al.)
items.value: Transmitted THz amplitude modulated by up to 47% and phase by 32.2° at room temperature, with hysteresis
items.source_title: Lee S.H. et al., 'Switching terahertz waves with gate-controlled active graphene metamaterials', Nat. Mater. 11, 936 (2012)
items.note: Abstract via Europe PMC. Free-space modulator; no ≥69-Gb/s graphene THz modulator was found.

items.item: Gate-tunable THz critical coupling in graphene (Kakenov et al.)
items.value: 99% absorption at 2.8 THz at critical coupling (graphene / electrolyte / metal reflector, ionic gating to E_F ≈ 1 eV). 99/76/42% at 2.83/8.24/13.23 THz.
items.source_title: Kakenov et al., 'Observation of gate-tunable coherent perfect absorption of terahertz radiation in graphene', ACS Photonics 3, 1531 (2016); arXiv:1801.04640
items.note: Drude (non-plasmonic) dissipation in a Salisbury-type cavity. Temperature not confirmed. Shows the THz critical-coupling rule, not a launch.

items.item: Edge and waveguide THz plasmon modes in graphene microribbons — theory (Nikitin et al.)
items.value: Waveguide and edge modes are separated by a wavenumber gap; the even hybridized edge mode is the fundamental, lowest-loss mode. Every mode has an optimum low-loss frequency. No numbers in the abstract.
items.source_title: Nikitin, Guinea, García-Vidal, Martín-Moreno, PRB 84, 161407(R) (2011)
items.note: Unscreened ribbons; no launch efficiency.

items.item: Far-field coupling into screened (acoustic) plasmons by metal-rod gratings over graphene (Alcaraz Iranzo et al.)
items.value: Metal rods over graphene with 0.7–2 nm spacers. Far-field light launches screened plasmons at rod edges, through edge dipoles that supply the momentum. Fabry–Pérot resonances up to 7th order; λ0 ≈ 8 µm; 'high' extinction (number not extracted).
items.source_title: Alcaraz Iranzo et al., 'Probing the ultimate plasmon confinement limits with a van der Waals heterostructure', Science 360, 291 (2018)
items.note: Mid-IR. Here the metal is both gate and coupler, the closest structural analog to a Fable gate lattice, but the resonances are localized standing waves.

items.item: Graphene acoustic plasmon resonator with near-perfect absorption (Lee I.-H. et al.)
items.value: 94% absorption of incident mid-IR light (8-nm alumina gap case, near 1,170 cm⁻¹ ≈ 8.5 µm ≈ 35 THz). Two-stage coupling (free space → conventional plasmon → acoustic plasmon) on ultraflat Au ribbons with an integrated spacer and reflector.
items.source_title: Lee, Yoo, Avouris, Low, Oh, 'Graphene acoustic plasmon resonator for ultrasensitive infrared spectroscopy', Nat. Nanotechnol. 14, 313 (2019)
items.note: Best measured metasurface coupling into an acoustic graphene mode, but mid-IR and into a localized, dissipative resonance. Ambient operation not explicitly confirmed in the text read.

items.item: Single nanocube acoustic-plasmon cavities excited from the far field (Epstein et al.)
items.value: Mode-volume confinement ~5×10⁻¹⁰. Nanocube fill factors of 3–13% give a response comparable to grating couplers with 50–85% fill. Extinction is of order a few percent to ~15% on the plotted axes. Mid-IR.
items.source_title: Epstein et al., 'Far-field excitation of single graphene plasmon cavities with ultracompressed mode volumes', Science 368, 1219 (2020)
items.note: Mid-IR; localized.

items.item: Acoustic plasmons in large-area CVD graphene at ambient (Menabde et al.)
items.value: Mid-IR acoustic mode twice as confined and 1.4× less damped than the graphene surface plasmon under similar conditions. A resonant Bloch state in an Au-nanoribbon array is credited with the high far-field coupling efficiency (no number).
items.source_title: Menabde et al., 'Real-space imaging of acoustic plasmons in large-area CVD graphene', Nat. Commun. 12, 938 (2021), arXiv:2010.01958
items.note: Mid-IR; no efficiency number.

items.item: THz plasmons under sub-wavelength metal gratings in CVD graphene (Bylinkin et al.)
items.value: 5–10 THz FTIR. Plasmon resonance visible above the Drude background at μ ~10³ cm²/Vs; field tightly bound below the stripes (500-nm period); frequency set by stripe width, not period.
items.source_title: Bylinkin et al., 'Tight-binding terahertz plasmons in chemical vapor deposited graphene', arXiv:1812.04028
items.note: Grating-gate coupling at THz in scalable graphene; absorption magnitude and efficiency not extracted.

items.item: UTC-PD photomixer conversion law used for the per-line pump
items.value: 24 µW at 0.914 THz from 100 mW optical; P_THz/P_opt² = 2.4×10⁻³ W⁻¹. Near 1 THz, CW UTC-PD output is 2.9–10.9 µW (Part I §3.2).
items.source_title: Rouvalis, Renaud & Seeds, 'Ultra-Fast Photodiodes for Terahertz Generation', UCL LCS 2010 (device of Opt. Express 18, 11105 (2010))
items.note: Carried over from the prior session's sourced item. Derived: 24 µW × 4 ps = 96 aJ; 10.9 µW → 43.6 aJ; 2.9 µW → 11.6 aJ per 4-ps slot.

items.item: Fable in-fabric targets used for the coupling arithmetic (record values)
items.value: ~10 aJ per 4-ps slot at ~3 µW (Part I §3.2); ~10 aJ/bit intrinsic field energy (§8.1); launch budget 576–737 quanta and homodyne decision floor ≥406 quanta at 300 K / 477 at 353 K (§9.5); knee ≈38 quanta at the launch plane, rail ≈3,833, default N_op 400, REF N_op 2,600 = 1.72 aJ, loaded F = 2 fixed point 99–277 (Part III §2.3, §5); 384–704 launch lines at 69 Gb/s (Part III)
items.source_title: Fable Computer Part I v6.1 and Part III v1.1, repository copies
items.note: Read from the scratchpad text extracts of the repo papers; nothing in the repo was modified.

items.item: Required launch-transducer efficiency from a 10-aJ, 4-ps slot (derived)
items.value: hf at 1 THz = 0.6626 zJ, so 10 aJ = 15,092 quanta. Required η = N × 0.6626 zJ / 10 aJ: N_op 400 → 2.65%; decision 406 → 2.69% (300 K), 477 → 3.16% (353 K); launch budget 576–737 → 3.82–4.88%; REF N_op 2,600 → 17.2%; rail 3,833 → 25.4%; Part I §8.1's ~10 aJ/bit in the mode → 100%
items.source_title: Derived here from Part I §3.2/§8.1/§9.5 and Part III §2.3/§5 values
items.note: Arithmetic on record numbers; the two readings (budget in quanta vs ~10 aJ field energy) differ ×20–26 in the requirement. Which applies is a record question.

items.item: Energy reaching the mode from a 10-aJ, 4-ps slot at measured efficiencies (derived)
items.value: η 0.35 → 3.5 aJ = 5,282 quanta; η 0.30 → 4,528; η 0.03 (acoustic, Au gate) → 0.30 aJ = 453 quanta; η 5×10⁻⁵ (optical) → 0.75 quanta. At η = 0.03 the UTC-PD range 2.9–24 µW gives 525–4,346 quanta per 4 ps.
items.source_title: Derived from Yoshioka 2024 and NTT 2024 efficiencies, hf = 6.626×10⁻²² J
items.note: Inherits the low-confidence 0.03 and the 4-K condition. At 0.03, 453 quanta clears the 406-quanta decision floor but not the 576–737 launch budget; the weakest UTC-PD class (2.9 µW) misses the budget (525) and the best (24 µW at 0.914 THz) clears it.

items.item: Optical pump per launch line vs coupling efficiency (derived)
items.value: P_opt = sqrt(P_THz / 2.4×10⁻³ W⁻¹), with P_THz = E_mode/(η·4 ps). Launch-budget reading (576–737 quanta): 6.3–7.1 mW at η = 1; 10.7–12.1 mW at 0.35; 12.0–17.0 mW at 0.175–0.278 (taper route); 36.4–41.2 mW at 0.03. 10-aJ-in-mode reading: 32.3 mW at η = 1; 54.6 mW at 0.35; 61–77 mW on the taper route; 186 mW at 0.03 (needs 83 µW THz, above every UTC-PD ≤24 µW). Totals over 384–704 lines (launch-budget reading): 2.4–5.0 W (η = 1), 4.1–8.5 W (0.35), 4.6–12 W (taper), 14–29 W (0.03).
items.source_title: Derived from Rouvalis 2010 FOM, Part I/III targets and Yoshioka efficiencies
items.note: The prior session's 32–39 mW per line equals the η = 1 case of the 10-aJ reading, and lands on the η ≈ 3% case of the launch-budget reading. P_opt ∝ η^(−1/2), so going from 0.03 to 0.35 cuts pump ×0.293 (−5.3 dB optical). Excludes comb amplification, modulator loss and wall-plug efficiency.

items.item: Upper bound for a resonant (antenna-coupled) gate segment built from the lossy plasmon (derived, coupled-mode theory)
items.value: With an impedance-matched input (γ_in = γ_out + γ_i), transfer at resonance is η_max = γ_out/(γ_out + γ_i) = 1 − 2Q_L/Q_i, with Q_i = ωτ. At Q_i = 6.3: Q_L 1 → 68%, 1.5 → 52%, 2 → 37%, 2.5 → 21%, 3 → 5%. At Q_i = 5.3 (353 K): Q_L 2 → 25%. At the measured RT Q_i = 2.5–3.8: Q_L 1 → 20–47%; no segment with Q_L ≥ 1.25–1.9 exists. Passing a pulse needs Q_L ≲ 3 (3-cycle burst), ≲4 (4-ps slot) or ≲12 (Part III's 12-ps gated burst). For η ≥ 50%: Q_i ≥ 4Q_L, i.e. τ ≥ 0.64/1.27/1.91 ps for Q_L = 1/2/3.
items.source_title: Derived here (standard three-port coupled-mode result) using Part I Q = ωτ (6.3 at 300 K, 5.3 at 353 K; measured 2.5–3.8)
items.note: Ignores extra metal or radiative loss in the segment, which would lower Q_i further. The metasurface 'critical coupling' rule (γ_ext = γ_i) maximizes dissipation in the resonator, which is the wrong target for a transducer.

items.item: Acoustic-channel line impedance and contact-limited galvanic injection (derived, lumped transmission line)
items.value: L_k = πħ²/(e²E_F) = 7.28×10⁻¹¹ H/sq at E_F 116.7 meV. Z·W = L_k·s = 7.28×10⁻¹¹ × 2.33×10⁶ = 170 Ω·µm (156–164 Ω·µm from C_g with quantum capacitance at ε_z 3.4–3.8), so ≈98 Ω at the cell width W = 1 µm²/0.576 µm = 1.74 µm. A series contact ρ_c caps power transfer at η = 1/(1 + ρ_c/(2·Z·W))², independent of width: 0.76 (−1.2 dB) at 50 Ω·µm, 0.60 (−2.2 dB) at 100 Ω·µm, 0.40 (−4.0 dB) at 200 Ω·µm.
items.source_title: Derived here from Part I Eq. (1) design s = 2.33×10⁶ m/s, the 100 Ω·µm-class edge contact (Part I §9.1) and Part III's 1 µm² active cell area
items.note: The lumped model ignores field shape and return path. Yoshioka's measured 0.03 for the Au gate is far below what this impedance level would allow, which suggests that the field-shape and return-path mismatch dominates, not the impedance level (inference).

items.item: Length budget for any coupler inside the screened mode (derived)
items.value: 27.3/Q dB per λp gives 1.86 dB/µm at Q 6.3 (2.21 at 5.3; 3.08–4.69 at the measured 3.8–2.5). The 1/e intensity length λp·Q/2π is 2.34 µm at Q 6.3 (1.97 µm at 5.3; 0.93–1.41 µm at 3.8–2.5).
items.source_title: Derived from Part I §4 (27.3/Q dB per λp, λp = 2.33 µm)
items.note: Grating or phased-array couplers need coupling lengths ≫ λp (Nikitin 2014), so in the screened mode they lose more than they collect. Compression and coupling must happen in a weakly screened section (0.25–0.46 dB/µm, prior session) or within ≲1 µm of the cell.

items.item: Taper-route estimate: unscreened launch plus graded-gate transition into the Au-gated cell (derived)
items.value: η ≈ 0.35 × 10^(−0.1…−0.3) = 17.5–27.8%, i.e. 2,640–4,200 quanta per 10-aJ slot: 5.8–9.3× the ≈0.03 direct acoustic launch, clearing the 576–737-quanta launch budget
items.source_title: Derived from Yoshioka 2024 (0.35, 4 K) and Part I §9.4's −1 to −3 dB junction budget
items.note: Hypothetical. No measured THz taper exists; the 0.35 is a 4-K, 72-nm-hBN, ZnO-gate value. Part I §3.1 keeps ZnO only as a 'THz-transparent global window' option.

items.item: Launcher-jitter (DG4) sensitivity to coupling (derived)
items.value: A static, linear η leaves σ_rel unchanged. Under the additive-noise reading of Part I §9.5, launch SNR scales with η: 0.35 → 0.03 costs 10.7 dB. A resonant coupler's amplitude falls by (2Q_L·δ)²/2 off-centre: 2.3% (4.0%) loss at detuning δ = 3.6% (4.7%) of f0 for Q_L = 3, 5.4% (7.1%) for Q_L = 2, 10.7% (14.1%) for Q_L = 1.
items.source_title: Derived from Part III Table T10 (DG4: σ_rel ≤ 2.3–4.0%, SNR ≥ 28–33 dB) and the Lorentzian response
items.note: The coupler's detuning tolerance is looser than the cell's own ±1% of f0 (Part I §3.2), so a centred resonant coupler would not be the binding DG4 term.

items.item: Size of a resonant free-space port at 1 THz (derived)
items.value: Half-wave dipole on a sapphire interface: ε_eff = (9.4+1)/2 = 5.2, so L ≈ 300 µm/√5.2/2 ≈ 66 µm per port (~115 cell lengths of 576 nm). De Fazio's 40-µm dipole was sized for ~2.5 THz.
items.source_title: Derived from λ0 = 300 µm and sapphire ε_r ≈ 9.4 (Part I §3.1)
items.note: Quasi-static interface estimate; sapphire anisotropy ignored.

items.item: Measured coupling of free-space or stripline THz into a propagating gate-screened graphene mode at 300 K
items.value: not found
items.source_title: Search of arXiv, Europe PMC, Crossref, OpenAlex and publisher abstracts, 2007–2026
items.note: The only measured propagating-mode launch is Yoshioka 2024 at 4 K. RT antenna-coupled gated plasmons are shown only as detector resonances (Caridad 2024 at 4.7 THz) or overdamped waves (Soltani 2020 at 2 THz), without efficiencies.

mapping.fable_problem: Launch and read-out coupling efficiency into the acoustic mode: 'unquantified by any cited work' (Part I §3.2, §3.3, §9.5, Table 6; Part III limitations 11–12)
mapping.reason: The only measured electrical-to-gated-graphene-plasmon efficiency in the literature is in Part I's own ref [4] (Yoshioka 2024): ≈0.30–0.35 for the unscreened ZnO-gated mode and ≈0.03 for the Au-gated acoustic mode (35-nm hBN), both at 4 K. The record cites [4] for the launch but says no cited work quantifies the efficiency, which is a misstatement. None of the review's metasurface, antenna or grating works (2011–2016, mostly mid-IR) and none of the 2018–2026 THz antenna or stripline works (Bandurin 2018, Caridad 2024, Kipp 2025, Delgado-Notario 2025, De Fazio 2026) reports an efficiency into a propagating gate-screened mode. No 300-K value exists.
mapping.what_must_be_true: For [4]'s 0.03 to stand for the design, it must carry from 4 K, 35-nm hBN and ~10⁶ m/s to 300 K, 10-nm hBN and 2.33×10⁶ m/s. By the authors' own velocity-mismatch explanation it should not improve at 10 nm. The 0.03 itself is search-indexed, not read from the PDF.
mapping.quantified_effect: From a 10-aJ/4-ps slot (15,092 quanta), η ≈ 0.03 delivers ≈453 quanta. That clears the 406-quanta 300-K decision floor but not the 576–737-quanta launch budget, which needs η ≥ 3.8–4.9%, and is far from Part I §8.1's ~10 aJ/bit (η ≈ 1). The 0.30–0.35 unscreened value delivers 4,530–5,280 quanta.

mapping.fable_problem: Resonant antenna-coupled gate segment (Part I §9.5, third and least mature mitigation)
mapping.reason: The metasurface literature reaches 94–100% absorption only by critical coupling into localized, dissipative resonances: Thongrattanasiri 2012 (theory, IR); Yao 2014 (5–7 µm, ≤20 GHz); Lee 2019 (94% at ≈8.5 µm, acoustic); Kakenov 2016 (99% at 2.8 THz, Drude). That maximizes loss in the resonator, the wrong target for a transducer. THz antenna-coupled gated cavities report responsivity only. A resonant segment made of the plasmon itself obeys η ≤ 1 − 2Q_L/Q_i (derived, coupled-mode theory), so it trades bandwidth against the plasmon's own Q = ωτ.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Q_i ≥ 2Q_L/(1 − η). For ≥50% at Q_L = 2, which a 4-ps slot tolerates (Q_L ≲ 3–4), Q_i ≥ 8, i.e. τ ≥ 1.27 ps at 1 THz: beyond the 1-ps best case and ×2–3 the measured 0.4–0.6 ps. A measured antenna-to-propagating-mode efficiency at 1 THz is also needed; none exists.
mapping.quantified_effect: Upper bounds at Q_i = 6.3: ≤68% (Q_L 1), ≤37% (Q_L 2), ≤5% (Q_L 3). At 353 K (Q_i 5.3), Q_L 2 gives ≤25%. At the measured RT Q_i 2.5–3.8: ≤20–47% at Q_L 1, impossible above Q_L 1.25–1.9. It cannot beat a broadband galvanic launch (0.30–0.35 measured, unscreened) unless τ ≳ 1.3 ps.

mapping.fable_problem: Tapered-gate impedance transformers (Part I §9.5, second mitigation)
mapping.reason: The only quantified taper coupler is a mid-IR simulation (Nikitin 2014: >25% overall, ≈70% for the coupling step, loss dominated by the taper). It states that metal tapers at mid-IR/THz compress the field but not the wavelength, so the compression must happen in the graphene (grading gate distance or density). A derived lumped transmission-line estimate puts the acoustic line at L_k·s/W ≈ 170 Ω·µm/W, ≈98 Ω at the 1.74-µm cell width, within 2× of stripline impedances. The impedance level is therefore set by channel width, and [4]'s low Au-gate value points to field-shape and return-path mismatch, which is what a taper must fix.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Do the compression mostly in a weakly screened or ZnO-gated section (0.25–0.46 dB/µm) and keep the final step into the 10-nm-gated cell ≲1 µm. The acoustic 1/e intensity length is 2.34 µm at Q 6.3 and 0.93–1.41 µm at the measured Q. Contact resistivity must be ≲50 Ω·µm: a 100-Ω·µm edge contact alone caps galvanic injection at ≈60% (−2.2 dB). The transition must fit Part I §9.4's −1 to −3 dB, a Boltzmann–Maxwell-tier and bench question.
mapping.quantified_effect: If a 35% unscreened launch feeds a −1 to −3 dB taper: η ≈ 17.5–27.8%, 2,640–4,200 quanta per 10-aJ slot, 5.8–9.3× the ≈0.03 direct acoustic launch, clearing the 576–737-quanta launch budget. Hypothetical: no THz taper has been measured.

mapping.fable_problem: I/O energy: 32–39 mW optical pump per launch line (prior session), 384–704 lines for 2–7 lanes (Part III limitation 12)
mapping.reason: With P_THz = 2.4×10⁻³ W⁻¹·P_opt², the pump per line scales as η^(−1/2) at fixed in-mode energy. The 32–39-mW figure assumed the launcher's 10–44 aJ is delivered as is (η = 1, 10-aJ reading). The coupling literature fixes η only at 4 K: ≈0.35 unscreened, ≈0.03 acoustic. The improvement comes from changing the launch architecture (unscreened galvanic launch plus taper), not from metasurfaces.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The 576–737-quanta launch budget, not the ~10 aJ/bit field energy, must set the in-mode requirement. The 4-K unscreened efficiency must hold at 300 K, the transition must cost ≤3 dB, and the UTC-PD must stay in its P² regime. Per-line amplification and lasers are still needed as before.
mapping.quantified_effect: Launch-budget reading: 36.4–41.2 mW per line at η 0.03 (≈ the quoted 32–39 mW; 14–29 W optical over 384–704 lines); 12.0–17.0 mW on the taper route (4.6–12 W); 10.7–12.1 mW at 0.35 (4.1–8.5 W); floor 6.3–7.1 mW at η = 1. Going from 0.03 to 0.35 cuts pump ×0.29 (−5.3 dB optical). 10-aJ-in-mode reading: 54.6 mW at 0.35, 61–77 mW on the taper route, 186 mW at 0.03 (needs 83 µW THz, above every UTC-PD ≤24 µW), i.e. ×1.7–5.8 above the quoted 32–39 mW.

mapping.fable_problem: DG4: launcher amplitude jitter σ_rel ≤ 2.3–4.0% (launch SNR ≥ 28–33 dB) at the post-coupling launch plane, 384–704 lines
mapping.reason: A static, linear coupling leaves σ_rel, a ratio, unchanged. η enters only through Part I §9.5's open question (additive vs proportional launcher noise) and through resonant couplers that convert detuning or drift into amplitude. No coupling paper measures jitter.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Launcher noise must be proportional (a launcher self-noise spec). If a resonant coupler is used, Q_L ≤ 3 and centred within a few percent of f0.
mapping.quantified_effect: Additive reading: η 0.35 → 0.03 costs 10.7 dB of launch SNR. A Q_L = 3 coupler holds amplitude within 2.3% (4.0%) only for detuning ≤3.6% (4.7%) of f0, which is looser than the cell's own ±1% (Part I §3.2), so it would not be the binding DG4 term.

mapping.fable_problem: Free-space THz or optical port (Part I §3.3: graphene patch antenna option, Haque [8]; far-field launch)
mapping.reason: Far-field or optical launch into propagating graphene plasmons is 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴-class: Yao B. 2018 DFG gives ≤6×10⁻⁵ W⁻¹ and single-nW plasmons, NTT quotes ≈0.005%. Lens and window optics lose ≈5.4 dB before the antenna (Bandurin 2018). A resonant 1-THz dipole on sapphire is ≈66 µm per port (derived). Room-temperature antenna-coupled gated-plasmon resonances are shown only at 4.7 THz (Caridad 2024); at 1–2.5 THz they are cryogenic (Bandurin, De Fazio, Delgado-Notario). Momentum-matching optics solve a problem the on-chip galvanic launch does not have.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Only a few calibration or reference ports could use it, given mW-class free-space 1-THz sources, which the photomixer chain does not provide.
mapping.quantified_effect: 10 aJ × 5×10⁻⁵ ≈ 0.5 zJ ≈ 0.75 quanta per slot.

mapping.fable_problem: Read-out: photoconductive sampling at fabric edges, Part III #141 electrical read, and DG1's input-referred swing
mapping.reason: Antenna-coupled graphene THz detectors detect free-space power. Caridad 2024 is resonant at 300 K only at 4.7 THz; Bandurin 2018 ≤77 K; De Fazio 2026 ≤90–130 K; Castilla 2019 is RT and non-resonant (NEP 80 pW/√Hz, <30 ns). None raises the input-referred swing that DG1 needs (Part I §9.5), and Fable reads on-chip.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: At 1 THz, Caridad's RT transport τ = 0.23 ps gives Q = 1.45 (3.77 at τp 0.6 ps), short of the resonant regime they use at 4.7 THz.

mapping.fable_problem: Junction or transition loss: −1 to −3 dB per junction, including mode mismatch through the ungated sliver (Part I §9.4), owned by the unrun Boltzmann–Maxwell tier
mapping.reason: Kipp 2025 (Nat. Phys., 20 K) shows on-chip stripline modes couple to graphene plasmons through unscreened currents in the gaps between metal strips, with strength set by the strip-to-gap width ratio (ultrastrong, g/ν0 = 0.12 at 0.43 THz). This is a mechanism and design knob for the sliver, but no loss or efficiency number is given, and the data are cryogenic.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A 300-K measurement of transmission through gated, ungated and gated transitions at ~1 THz (bench junction variants, Part I §9.4).
mapping.quantified_effect: none quantified

mapping.fable_problem: Area: 27.4 µm² per cell (1 µm² active), 0.224–0.232 mm² per lane
mapping.reason: Metasurface, grating and antenna couplers need λ0-scale apertures or many periods. At 1 THz a resonant dipole is ≈66 µm and a grating's coupling length (~λ0) far exceeds the screened mode's 2.3-µm decay length. Such couplers suit a few free-space ports, not 384–704 data lines; the galvanic launch needs no such aperture.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: ≈66 µm per resonant port ≈ 115 cell lengths (derived).

mapping.fable_problem: Per-line modulation at 69 Gb/s (IQ-modulated DFB lines; Part III limitation 12)
mapping.reason: Graphene metasurface modulators modulate free-space light: up to 20 GHz at 5–7 µm (Yao 2014); 47% amplitude and 32.2° phase at THz with no speed figure (Lee S.H. 2012); mid-IR Fano and phase devices (Dabidian 2015/2016, Emani 2012). No graphene THz modulator at ≥69 Gb/s was found, and a shared-carrier scheme would need mW-class 1-THz sources.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: none

mapping.fable_problem: Gain and loss budget: G1 (≥ +2.6 dB per pulse at ≤80 °C), 27.3/Q dB per λp, DG1 decision error
mapping.reason: Coupling structures do not change τ, Q or drift gain. The antenna-gated devices show the same room-temperature damping limits: overdamped 25–70-fs plasma waves in Soltani 2020, τ 0.23 ps transport in Caridad 2024, Q 0.8–2.0 in CVD De Fazio 2026.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: none

items.item: Review scope on detection (Cui, Wang and Sun, 'Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics', Sec. 3.2)
items.value: Sec. 3.2 cites refs [181]-[186] (plus [175] in Sec. 3.1). All are metal-plasmon-enhanced or photogating graphene photodetectors working from the visible to the mid-IR. Quoted figures: 1e9 A/W and 1e13 Jones (UV-NIR) and 45 A/W at 1e5 Jones (mid-IR) for [184]; >20 GHz at 70 mA/W (2 um) and >40 GHz at 400 mA/W (1.55 um) for [186]. The section has no THz detector, no electrical readout of graphene plasmons, no Dyakonov-Shur (DS) rectification and no THz response-time data. It does not cite Bandurin 2018, Castilla 2019, Guo 2018, Lundeberg 2017 (Nat. Mater.), Alonso-Gonzalez 2017, Viti or Delgado-Notario.
items.source_title: L. Cui, J. Wang, M. Sun, Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics, Reviews in Physics 6, 100054 (2021); user-supplied PDF, text read
items.note: Read from the PDF Ryoji saved (C:/Users/Ryoji/Documents/Claude/Fablecomputer/1-s2.0-S2405428321000034-main.pdf); the publisher's bot check was not touched.

items.item: Guo et al. 2020, Light Sci. Appl. 9, 29 (review ref [186]): what it is
items.value: A silicon-graphene hybrid METAL-plasmonic waveguide photodetector, not a graphene-plasmon detector. At 2 um: ~70 mA/W (Vb -0.3 V, 0.28 mW) with a setup-limited 3-dB bandwidth >20 GHz. At 1.55 um: 396 mA/W (Vb -0.3 V, 0.16 mW), 3-dB bandwidth >40 GHz (VNA-limited) and a 30 Gbit/s eye. NEP at 2 um: 61.7-72.7 pW/rtHz in photoconductive mode and 668-992 pW/rtHz in bolometric mode. Dark current ~3 mA. PTE at zero bias, bolometric/photoconductive under bias. Room temperature.
items.source_title: J. Guo et al., High-performance silicon-graphene hybrid plasmonic waveguide photodetectors beyond 1.55 um, Light Sci. Appl. 9, 29 (2020)
items.note: Optical carrier (1.55-2 um). Not applicable to a 1-THz plasmon readout.

items.item: Liu et al. 2011, Nat. Commun. 2, 579 (review ref [181])
items.value: Metallic plasmonic nanostructures on graphene raise photocurrent and external quantum efficiency by up to 1,500%, with colour selectivity (visible).
items.source_title: Y. Liu et al., Plasmon resonance enhanced multicolour photodetection by graphene, Nat. Commun. 2, 579 (2011)
items.note: Abstract only. Responsivity and speed: not found. Metal plasmons at visible wavelengths.

items.item: Yao et al. 2014, Nano Lett. 14, 3749 (review ref [175])
items.value: ~0.4 V/W at 4.45 um, room temperature: >200x over antenna-free devices (<2 mV/W). Mechanism: antenna-enhanced absorption plus photoconductive gain.
items.source_title: Y. Yao et al., High-responsivity mid-infrared graphene detectors with antenna-enhanced photocarrier generation and collection, Nano Lett. 14, 3749 (2014)
items.note: Mid-IR, metal antennas. Abstract via Europe PMC.

items.item: Yu et al. 2016, Adv. Mater. 28, 4912 (review ref [183])
items.value: Graphene/Si-quantum-dot/bulk-Si Schottky-junction photodetector. The abstract gives no responsivity or speed (not found).
items.source_title: T. Yu et al., Graphene coupled with silicon quantum dots for high-performance bulk-silicon-based Schottky-junction photodetectors, Adv. Mater. 28, 4912 (2016)
items.note: Visible-NIR. Not a plasmon-readout device.

items.item: Ni et al. 2017, ACS Nano 11, 9854 (review ref [184])
items.value: B-doped Si quantum dots (LSPR) on graphene, hybrid phototransistor, UV to MIR: responsivity up to ~1e9 A/W, gain up to ~1e12, D* up to ~1e13 Jones. Mid-IR 45 A/W at 1e5 Jones (per the review).
items.source_title: Z. Ni et al., Plasmonic silicon quantum dots enabled high-sensitivity ultrabroadband photodetection of graphene-based hybrid phototransistors, ACS Nano 11, 9854 (2017)
items.note: The photogating gain implies long trap lifetimes. Response time is not in the abstract (not found).

items.item: Chen et al. 2017, ACS Nano 11, 430 (review ref [185])
items.value: 83 A/W at 1.55 um with a rise time <600 ns (Au-nanoparticle plasmonics plus electron trapping).
items.source_title: Z. Chen et al., Synergistic effects of plasmonics and electron trapping in graphene short-wave infrared photodetectors with ultrahigh responsivity, ACS Nano 11, 430 (2017)
items.note: SWIR at room temperature. The response is ~40x slower than a 14.5-ps slot (600 ns / 14.5 ps).

items.item: Nikitin et al. 2011, PRB 84, 161407(R) (review ref [182], cited in the photodetector section)
items.value: Theory only: edge and waveguide THz plasmon modes in graphene microribbons. The even-parity edge mode is the fundamental and lowest-loss mode, and each mode has an optimum frequency for minimum loss. No detector figures.
items.source_title: A. Y. Nikitin et al., Edge and waveguide terahertz surface plasmon modes in graphene microribbons, PRB 84, 161407 (2011)
items.note: Unscreened ribbon modes. Not a readout result.

items.item: H. Yan et al. 2012, Nat. Nanotechnol. 7, 330 (review ref [180])
items.value: Not a detector. Graphene/insulator stack devices: tunable far-IR notch filters with 8.2 dB rejection and THz linear polarizers with 9.5 dB extinction; an unpatterned 5-layer stack shields 97.5% of radiation below 1.2 THz.
items.source_title: H. Yan et al., Tunable infrared plasmonic devices using graphene/insulator stacks, Nat. Nanotechnol. 7, 330 (2012)
items.note: The review cites it in its metamaterials section (3.1), not its detector section.

items.item: J. Yan et al. 2012, Nat. Nanotechnol. 7, 472 (the 'Yan 2012' graphene detector, if a detector was meant)
items.value: Dual-gated bilayer-graphene hot-electron bolometer: NEP 33 fW/rtHz at 5 K; intrinsic speed >1 GHz at 10 K.
items.source_title: J. Yan et al., Dual-gated bilayer graphene hot-electron bolometer, Nat. Nanotechnol. 7, 472 (2012)
items.note: Cryogenic. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Guo et al. 2018, Nat. Mater. 17, 986: electrical detection of mid-IR graphene plasmons
items.value: At 12.2 um (mid-IR), room temperature: external responsivity 16 mA/W; measured NEP 1.3 nW/rtHz, against a theoretical limit of 460 pW/rtHz (dark-noise plateau 21 pA/rtHz at 1-5 kHz, Vb = 1 V, I0 = 175 uA). Footprint 5x5 um2. Response flat from 10 Hz to 5 kHz (chopper-limited); >1 GHz only in simulation. Mechanism: plasmon decay heats carriers, which thermally activate transport over disorder barriers in quasi-1D CVD nanoribbons (bolometric-type; conductance rises with Te; >20x over unpatterned graphene).
items.source_title: Q. Guo et al., Efficient electrical detection of mid-infrared graphene plasmons at room temperature, Nat. Mater. 17, 986 (2018); arXiv:1805.06105
items.note: Mid-IR, not THz. Mobility 475 cm2/Vs. Speed above 5 kHz is not measured.

items.item: Lundeberg et al. 2017, Nat. Mater. 16, 204: thermoelectric detection of propagating plasmons
items.value: All-graphene mid-IR plasmon detector at room temperature: one sheet is both the plasmonic medium and the photothermoelectric detector. Two local split gates tune the plasmonic and thermoelectric response, and real-space photocurrent maps resolve propagation, interference, decay and thermal diffusion. Responsivity, NEP and speed: not found in accessible records.
items.source_title: M. B. Lundeberg et al., Thermoelectric detection and imaging of propagating graphene plasmons, Nat. Mater. 16, 204 (2017); PubMed abstract via Europe PMC
items.note: Mid-IR. The accepted manuscript at UPCommons sits behind a bot check and was not accessed. Not the Lundeberg Science 2017 paper that Part I cites as [40].

items.item: Freitag et al. 2013, Nat. Commun. 4, 1951
items.value: Mid-IR graphene nanoribbon arrays with plasmon-SiO2-phonon modes: the in-resonance photocurrent is ~10x that for electron-hole excitation, and the photo-induced temperature rise is up to 4x that of a 2D graphene detector. Polarization-sensitive and gate-tunable.
items.source_title: M. Freitag et al., Photocurrent in graphene harnessed by tunable intrinsic plasmons, Nat. Commun. 4, 1951 (2013)
items.note: Mid-IR. Temperature is not stated in the abstract. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Vicarelli et al. 2012, Nat. Mater. 11, 865: graphene FET THz detectors
items.value: Antenna-coupled graphene FETs at room temperature and 0.3 THz: NEP <30 nW/rtHz. The nonlinear FET (plasma-wave/DS-type) response has thermoelectric and photoconductive contributions.
items.source_title: L. Vicarelli et al., Graphene field-effect transistors as room-temperature terahertz detectors, Nat. Mater. 11, 865 (2012); arXiv:1203.3232
items.note: Overdamped (non-resonant) regime.

items.item: Cai et al. 2014, Nat. Nanotechnol. 9, 814: sensitivity
items.value: Room temperature, 2.52 THz (119 um), PTE with dissimilar-metal contacts: responsivity >10 V/W referenced to incident power (715 V/W absorbed); NEP <1,100 pW/rtHz incident (16 pW/rtHz absorbed, close to the Johnson limit).
items.source_title: X. Cai et al., Sensitive room-temperature terahertz detection via the photothermoelectric effect in graphene, Nat. Nanotechnol. 9, 814 (2014); arXiv:1305.3297
items.note: Effective mobility 1,500 cm2/Vs.

items.item: Cai et al. 2014: speed
items.value: Intrinsic response 10.5 ps (pulse-coincidence/ASOPS, 1.56-um pump, 150 K). Real-time FWHM 30 ps for 800-nm pulses at room temperature (convolved with a 25-ps scope; epitaxial graphene on SiC). Electrical impulse response 110 ps FWHM to ~1-ps, 0-2 THz pulses (160 nJ, 1 kHz) at room temperature on a large-area CVD device, recorded on a 40-GHz sampling scope.
items.source_title: X. Cai et al., Nat. Nanotechnol. 9, 814 (2014); arXiv:1305.3297
items.note: Derived: 110 ps / 14.5 ps = 7.6 Fable slots. This is the fastest real-time electrical response to THz excitation found for graphene.

items.item: Cai et al. 2015, Nano Lett. 15, 4295: plasmon-enhanced THz photodetection
items.value: Room temperature. Epitaxial graphene microribbons (2.3 um wide) on SiC with bimetallic electrodes; PTE photoresponse at 5.3 THz CW. Plasmon Q = wp*tau = 1.2 (mobility 800 cm2/Vs, tau 37 fs, n = 1.6e13 cm-2). Localized, unscreened ribbon plasmon.
items.source_title: X. Cai et al., Plasmon-enhanced terahertz photodetection in graphene, Nano Lett. 15, 4295 (2015); author-hosted PDF
items.note: No responsivity value found in the main text extracted (not found).

items.item: Bandurin et al. 2018, Nat. Commun. 9, 5392: broadband operation and NEP
items.value: Bilayer graphene in hBN (top hBN ~80 nm), L 3-6 um, antenna between gate and source. At 0.13 THz (overdamped, Q 0.2-0.7): R_a max ~240 V/W at 10 K. Dual-gated (D = 0.1 V/nm): >3 kV/W, NEP ~0.2 pW/rtHz (Johnson estimate, cryogenic). Mobility >10 m2/Vs at 10 K and >2 m2/Vs at 300 K. Photovoltage read by lock-in behind a 1-kHz chopper.
items.source_title: D. A. Bandurin et al., Resonant terahertz detection using graphene plasmons, Nat. Commun. 9, 5392 (2018); arXiv:1807.04703
items.note: The text compares the NEP with bolometers 'at the same f and T', i.e. cryogenic (medium confidence on T). Derived at room temperature: tau_tr = 0.036 m_e x 2 m2/Vs / e = 0.41 ps, so Q(1 THz) = 2.6.

items.item: Bandurin et al. 2018: resonant DS detection
items.value: At 2 THz (QCL): gate-tuned plasmonic Fabry-Perot resonances at L = (2k+1)lambda_p/4 (first observed k = 3), clear at 10 K and persisting to 77 K; well developed at 0.46 THz. tau_p 0.3-0.9 ps against tau_tr ~2 ps; Q = 4-11 at 2 THz; lambda0/lambda_p 50-150.
items.source_title: D. A. Bandurin et al., Nat. Commun. 9, 5392 (2018)
items.note: Cryogenic to 77 K. Not cited anywhere in the Fable record.

items.item: Bandurin et al. 2018: boundary conditions and damping
items.value: The source is clamped to the antenna voltage and no AC current flows into the drain, so r_s*r_d ~ -1, the cell's DS boundary pair. The DS rectification model fits the n-side data with an effective antenna impedance Z ~ 74 Ohm. Broadening beyond momentum relaxation is attributed to plasma-wave leakage into the metal contacts and to antenna dissipation, largest at high carrier density and low harmonic number. The authors project that Schottky/tunnel contacts and low-impedance antennas could push resonant detection down to tens of GHz.
items.source_title: D. A. Bandurin et al., Nat. Commun. 9, 5392 (2018)
items.note: Bears on the record's open boundary/contact channel (delta_b, issue #88). The Fable cell runs the fundamental mode at n = 1e12, where this leakage is reported to be largest. No absolute antenna coupling efficiency is reported.

items.item: Alonso-Gonzalez et al. 2017, Nat. Nanotechnol. 12, 31 (Part I [39], Part II [13])
items.value: THz photocurrent near-field nanoscopy: acoustic plasmons launched in the near field under a split metal gate are detected thermoelectrically at the graphene pn junction. lambda_p = lambda0/66 at 2.52 THz, linear dispersion, damping at positive densities dominated by Coulomb impurity scattering. Room temperature.
items.source_title: P. Alonso-Gonzalez et al., Acoustic terahertz graphene plasmons revealed by photocurrent nanoscopy, Nat. Nanotechnol. 12, 31 (2017); arXiv:1601.05753
items.note: Room temperature per the author version (prior session) and Part I Sec. 4. An in-sheet PTE junction does detect the gated acoustic mode at room temperature, but only as imaging: no calibrated responsivity or speed.

items.item: Castilla et al. 2019, Nano Lett. 19, 2765: sensitivity
items.value: Room temperature, 2.52 THz (1.8-4.2 THz measured, antenna-limited). Zero-bias PTE at an antenna-defined pn junction (dipole gap ~100 nm, doubling as split gate), hBN-encapsulated H-shaped channel. Responsivity 14 mA/W (32 V/W) for device A and 25 mA/W (105 V/W) for device B, normalized to a diffraction-limited spot. NEP 80 pW/rtHz (Johnson noise of the 4.2-kOhm device). Linear over >3 decades of power. Hot-carrier cooling length 0.5-1 um at room temperature.
items.source_title: S. Castilla et al., Fast and sensitive terahertz detection using an antenna-integrated graphene pn junction, Nano Lett. 19, 2765 (2019); arXiv:1905.01881
items.note: Antenna-assisted hot-carrier PTE, not plasmon-resonant.

items.item: Castilla et al. 2019: speed
items.value: Measured response <30 ns: exponential fits of 40 and 24 ns, limited by a 3.5-MHz preamplifier (~5 MHz). The RC-limited rise time is calculated, not measured: 56 ps (6 GHz) at 20,000 cm2/Vs and 9 ps (40 GHz) at 100,000 cm2/Vs.
items.source_title: S. Castilla et al., Nano Lett. 19, 2765 (2019); arXiv:1905.01881
items.note: Room temperature.

items.item: Viti et al. 2020, Nano Lett. 20, 3169
items.value: Room temperature. Bow-tie antenna resonant at 3 THz on hBN-encapsulated graphene (>50,000 cm2/Vs), PTE: NEP <=160 pW/rtHz, response time <=3.3 ns, dynamic range of four decades.
items.source_title: L. Viti et al., HBN-encapsulated, graphene-based, room-temperature terahertz receivers, with high speed and low noise, Nano Lett. 20, 3169 (2020); arXiv:2004.10011
items.note: Abstract figures.

items.item: Viti et al. 2021, Nanophotonics 10, 89: sub-ns THz PTE detectors
items.value: Room temperature, 3.4 THz (QCL). Single-gate bow-tie device: Rv max 30 V/W, NEP ~350 pW/rtHz. Split-gate dipole (90-nm gap): NEP ~120 pW/rtHz. Both NEPs are Johnson estimates. Rise times 1.3 +/- 0.4 ns and 890 +/- 150 ps (fall 1.5 and 1.4 ns), i.e. 125 +/- 35 and 180 +/- 30 MHz. The chip has >100-GHz coplanar striplines; readout used a 1.2-GHz preamplifier and a ~200-ps scope.
items.source_title: L. Viti et al., Thermoelectric graphene photodetectors with sub-nanosecond response times at terahertz frequencies, Nanophotonics 10, 89 (2021); arXiv:2006.10622
items.note: The authors attribute the response to PTE, not plasma-wave detection.

items.item: Asgari et al. 2021, ACS Nano 15, 17966
items.value: Scalable CVD graphene (single and polycrystal), room temperature, zero-bias PTE, 0.1-10 THz by antenna choice: NEP <1 nW/rtHz, response ~5 ns.
items.source_title: M. Asgari et al., Chip-scalable, room-temperature, zero-bias, graphene-based terahertz detectors with nanosecond response time, ACS Nano 15, 17966 (2021)
items.note: Abstract via Europe PMC (PMC8613901).

items.item: Gayduchenko et al. 2021, Nat. Commun. 12, 543
items.value: Bilayer-graphene tunnel FET (interband tunnelling rectification) at 0.13 THz and ~10 K: responsivity >4 kV/W (>3 kV/W shown at Vbg 1.5 V), NEP 0.2 pW/rtHz (Johnson estimate). On the p side, responsivity falls >100x at 77 K.
items.source_title: I. Gayduchenko et al., Tunnel field-effect transistors for sensitive terahertz detection, Nat. Commun. 12, 543 (2021)
items.note: Cryogenic.

items.item: Caridad et al. 2024, Nano Lett. 24, 935: room-temperature resonant DS detection
items.value: Monolayer graphene in hBN, L_ch 6 um, top gate 4.8 um, bow-tie antenna between top gate and source. Mobility >70,000 cm2/Vs at 10 K and >60,000 at room temperature; transport tau 0.29 ps (10 K) and 0.23 ps (room temperature). Plasmon tau_p ~0.6 ps from resonance FWHM. Q ~8.6 at 4.7 THz (10 K). lambda_p 0.6-2.1 um at 2.5-4.7 THz (lambda0/lambda_p up to 110). Resonances visible from 10 to 300 K.
items.source_title: J. M. Caridad et al., Room-temperature plasmon-assisted resonant THz detection in single-layer graphene transistors, Nano Lett. 24, 935 (2024)
items.note: Already in the record: notes/CITATIONS.md lists it for the issue #88 benchmark as 'locator-verified', with the instruction to read the article before quoting any Q/tau row. Read in full here: Q 8.6 is a 10-K value; at room temperature tau_tr 0.23 ps gives w*tau ~6.8 at 4.7 THz (derived).

items.item: Caridad et al. 2024: responsivity and bias noise
items.value: Current responsivity (normalized to detector area) ~0.29 A/W at 0.3 THz (overdamped) and ~1.8 mA/W at 4.7 THz. DS mechanism with a pn-junction offset (~0.1 uA/W). The authors note that a source-drain DC voltage or current shifts a device toward the resonant regime but also increases the noise of the rectified signal.
items.source_title: J. M. Caridad et al., Nano Lett. 24, 935 (2024)
items.note: The Fable cell is DC-biased at 0.7 x threshold. The extra noise is not quantified (not found).

items.item: Delgado-Notario et al. 2026, Nanophotonics: resonant DS magnetoplasmons
items.value: Antenna-coupled monolayer and bilayer graphene TeraFETs in hBN, L_ch 6 um, 1.7 K (monolayer) and 15 K (bilayer), 2.5-3.8 THz, fields up to 6 T. Mobility >70,000 cm2/Vs at 1.7 K. Plasmon lifetimes 0.4-1.7 ps from global Lorentzian fits, slightly longer than the transport times. Lock-in at 337 Hz.
items.source_title: J. A. Delgado-Notario et al., Resonant Dyakonov-Shur magnetoplasmons in graphene terahertz photodetectors, Nanophotonics (2026), e70094; arXiv:2512.00180
items.note: Cryogenic. No responsivity, NEP or speed found.

items.item: De Fazio et al. 2026, ACS Photonics 13, 4505 (Part III [43]): detector figures
items.value: CVD graphene without hBN, AlOx-gated dipole-antenna split gates. Acoustic-plasmon Fabry-Perot resonances at 1.83-2.52 THz modulate the PTE photovoltage by up to 40% between 6 and 90 K and vanish by 130 K; peak enhancement is +30% over the maximum conventional PTE response. Max responsivity ~12 V/W at 2.5 THz; NEP 100 pW/rtHz at 6 K (Johnson); lock-in at 267 Hz. The authors write that room-temperature graphene plasmon resonances (Caridad 2024) 'appeared only as weak features' and that such resonances are typically one to two orders of magnitude smaller than the conventional photoresponse.
items.source_title: D. De Fazio et al., Enhanced terahertz photoresponse via acoustic plasmon cavity resonances in scalable graphene, ACS Photonics 13, 4505 (2026); arXiv:2601.16604
items.note: Part III cites it for the CVD Q ~2 and the 130-K cutoff; its detector figures are not used.

items.item: Soundarapandian et al. 2026, Nat. Commun. 17, 2627: bandwidth-responsivity trade
items.value: Room temperature, zero-bias PTE, 0.21-0.23 THz, cavity of antenna plus back mirror. Best device (hBN-encapsulated exfoliated graphene): 0.16 A/W (30 V/W) with a Johnson-limited NEP of 58 pW/rtHz, but only 1-2 GHz bandwidth. A non-resonant device without mirror (device 7) reaches a setup-limited 20-40 GHz at ~10 uA/W. CVD device: 13 mA/W, NEP 416 pW/rtHz.
items.source_title: K. P. Soundarapandian et al., High-speed graphene-based sub-terahertz receivers enabling wireless communications for 6G and beyond, Nat. Commun. 17, 2627 (2026); arXiv:2411.02269
items.note: The 2024 preprint quoted '40 GHz and 0.16 A/W' together; the published version states they come from different devices.

items.item: Soundarapandian et al. 2026: data reception and measured noise
items.value: NRZ OOK at a 0.213-THz carrier: open eye at 1 Gbit/s, narrower at 1.5-2 Gbit/s, closed at 3 Gbit/s (1.2-GHz amplifier). Minimum BER ~2.5e-6 (setup-limited), SNR 4-13 dB, ~3 m link. Electronics noise was two orders of magnitude above Johnson, giving an experimental NEP of 1 nW/rtHz.
items.source_title: K. P. Soundarapandian et al., Nat. Commun. 17, 2627 (2026)
items.note: The only THz-carrier graphene data reception found.

items.item: Yoshioka et al. 2022, Nat. Photon. 16, 718: intrinsic optical-to-electrical speed and gate RC
items.value: Ambient room temperature, hBN/graphene PTE detector with a resistive ZnO top gate, read on-chip by an LT-GaAs photoconductive switch (pump-probe plus lock-in). 3-dB bandwidth 220 GHz at mobility 11,000 cm2/Vs and only 51 GHz at 140,000 cm2/Vs. Photocurrent generation is immediate to >4 ps, depending on Fermi level. The authors state that gate capacitance (RC with the contacts) 'sets the cut-off frequency below 100 GHz'; their devices have contact R 80-530 Ohm and C 32-83 fF.
items.source_title: K. Yoshioka et al., Ultrafast intrinsic optical-to-electrical conversion dynamics in a graphene photodetector, Nat. Photon. 16, 718 (2022); arXiv:2203.05752
items.note: Optical excitation (517/1035 nm), equivalent-time sampling. Directly relevant to the 'gate RC unmodelled' caveat on issue #141.

items.item: Koepfli et al. 2023, Science 380, 1169
items.value: Graphene/metamaterial photodetector with flat response beyond 500 GHz under ambient conditions; centre wavelengths from <1,400 to >4,200 nm, fibre-coupled.
items.source_title: S. M. Koepfli et al., Metamaterial graphene photodetector with bandwidth exceeding 500 gigahertz, Science 380, 1169 (2023)
items.note: Optical carrier. Shows graphene hot-carrier readout can exceed 69 GHz by ~7x.

items.item: Koepfli et al. 2024, Nat. Commun. 15, 7351
items.value: Self-powered PTE graphene photodetector with directional photocurrents from asymmetric metamaterial resonators: frequency response >400 GHz, responsivity ~1.5 V/W.
items.source_title: S. M. Koepfli et al., Controlling photothermoelectric directional photocurrents in graphene with over 400 GHz bandwidth, Nat. Commun. 15, 7351 (2024)
items.note: Infrared optical carrier, room temperature.

items.item: Marconi et al. 2021, Nat. Commun. 12, 806
items.value: CVD graphene PTE detector on a Si waveguide: >65 GHz response; direct detection of 105 Gbit/s NRZ and 120 Gbit/s PAM4 into a 50-Ohm voltage amplifier.
items.source_title: S. Marconi et al., Photo thermal effect graphene detector featuring 105 Gbit/s NRZ and 120 Gbit/s PAM4 direct detection, Nat. Commun. 12, 806 (2021)
items.note: Telecom carrier: graphene PTE plus electronics already exceed 69 Gb/s there.

items.item: Yoshioka et al. 2024, Nat. Electron. 7, 537 (Part I [4], Part II [16]): readout method
items.value: All measurements at 4 K in vacuum. LT-GaAs photoconductive switches on both sides of the graphene; pump-probe with 1035-nm, 280-fs pulses at 16.8 MHz and 20 mW on each switch; 30-V injection bias; chopper at a few hundred Hz with lock-in. Input pulse 1.2 ps FWHM (0-2 THz). Au-gated acoustic plasmon velocity 1.9-3.2e6 m/s over a 12-um gate.
items.source_title: K. Yoshioka et al., On-chip transfer of ultrashort graphene plasmon wavepackets using terahertz electronics, Nat. Electron. 7, 537 (2024); arXiv:2311.02821 v2
items.note: Equivalent-time (stroboscopic) sampling: ps resolution comes from averaging repeated identical waveforms, not single-shot capture.

items.item: Yoshioka et al. 2024: electrical-to-plasmon conversion efficiency per interface
items.value: Energy conversion efficiency per CPW-graphene ohmic interface, assumed equal for in- and out-coupling: eta >= 0.35 for the ZnO-gated unscreened plasmon; eta ~0.03 for the Au-gated acoustic plasmon (propagation length 21 um, attenuation z ~0.56); 6e-5 for optical excitation in earlier work. The authors trace the limit to impedance/velocity mismatch (CPW ~1e8 m/s, acoustic plasmon ~3e6 m/s, unscreened ~1e7 m/s).
items.source_title: K. Yoshioka et al., Nat. Electron. 7, 537 (2024); arXiv:2311.02821 v2, Fig. 5 and text
items.note: At 4 K. Part I Secs. 3.2/9.5 say 'no cited work quantifies the coupling efficiency', yet this is its own ref [4]. The ~3% acoustic value is now confirmed from the primary text; the prior session had it only from secondary sources.

items.item: Kusyak et al. 2025, APL Photonics 10, 076117 (Part I [7]): readout circuit conditions
items.value: Amorphous-Si switches on sapphire, 515-nm 310-fs pulses at 196 kHz (98-kHz AOM modulation), transimpedance amplifier plus lock-in. Data in Figs. 3-4 taken at 7 K. -3 dB at 440 GHz (AC-coupled; 160 GHz DC-coupled), 0.05-1.4 THz range. The 1-THz component is -23 dB (AC) and -39 dB (DC) relative to the strongest component.
items.source_title: K. Kusyak et al., Monolithic optoelectronic circuit design for on-chip terahertz applications, APL Photonics 10, 076117 (2025)
items.note: Read via WebFetch quoting (7 K captions and -23/-39 dB sentence quoted verbatim). Part I Table 2 flags [4]'s 4 K but not [7]'s 7 K; Part I Sec. 9.8 calls every member room-temperature hardware. The -23 dB figure covers generator, line and detector together.

items.item: Muravev et al. 2016, JETP Lett. 103, 792
items.value: Plasmonic (2DEG) THz detector response time <=110 ps, by both time-resolved and heterodyne measurement.
items.source_title: V. M. Muravev et al., On the response time of plasmonic terahertz detectors, JETP Lett. 103, 792 (2016); Mathnet abstract
items.note: Not graphene; temperature not found. Context for the speed of DS-type plasmonic rectifiers.

items.item: Zagrajek et al. 2019, arXiv:1905.08602
items.value: Si junctionless FETs, Si MOSFETs and GaAs HEMTs as THz detectors at 0.6-3.3 THz (pulsed molecular laser): response at least nanosecond (setup-bound), linear over many decades; low-power responsivity falls as R0 ~ f^-3 while saturation power rises as f^3. Room temperature.
items.source_title: P. Zagrajek et al., Time resolution and dynamic range of field effect transistor based terahertz detectors, arXiv:1905.08602
items.note: Not graphene. Non-resonant DS rectification loses responsivity steeply toward 1 THz.

items.item: Derived: thermal decision floor for any detector, 1 THz, BER 6.3e-9
items.value: Homodyne: N = Q^2(2n+1) = 405.8 at 300 K and 477.2 at 353 K, reproducing the record's 406/477. An ideal noiseless square-law detector (PTE, bolometric or DS rectifier), single matched mode, optimal threshold: N = 400 at 300 K and 476 at 353 K.
items.source_title: Derived here; inputs from Part I Sec. 9.5 and Part III Sec. 4.6
items.note: Q = sqrt(2) erfcinv(2 x 6.3e-9) = 5.691; hf = 6.626e-22 J; n = 1/(exp(hf/kT)-1) = 5.764 (300 K), 6.867 (353 K); 5.691^2 x 12.53 = 405.8. Square law: '0' exponential with mean n, '1' non-central chi-square (2 dof, nc = 2N/n); threshold optimized and N solved numerically. Classical-field approximation.

items.item: Derived: per-slot decision energy with demonstrated incoherent graphene THz detectors
items.value:
P = Q x NEP x sqrt(B), B = 1/(2 x 14.5 ps) = 34.5 GHz:
- 16 pW/rtHz (absorbed-referenced, Cai 2014): 16.9 uW, 0.245 fJ per slot, 3.7e5 quanta (910x the 406 floor)
- 58 pW/rtHz: 61 uW, 0.89 fJ, 1.34e6 quanta (3,300x)
- 80 pW/rtHz: 85 uW, 1.23 fJ, 1.85e6 quanta (4,560x)
- 120 pW/rtHz: 127 uW, 1.84 fJ, 2.78e6 quanta (6,840x)
- 160 pW/rtHz: 169 uW, 2.45 fJ, 3.70e6 quanta (9,110x)
- measured 1 nW/rtHz: 1.06 mW, 15.3 fJ, 2.3e7 quanta (57,000x)
Fable reference: 406 quanta = 0.269 aJ = 18.6 nW over 14.5 ps; the cascade's 99-277 quanta = 4.5-12.7 nW; the launch is 2.5 uW.
items.source_title: Derived from the NEPs of Cai 2014, Soundarapandian 2026, Castilla 2019, Viti 2021 and Viti 2020
items.note: sqrt(B) = 1.857e5. Johnson-limited NEPs are kHz figures; most are normalized to a diffraction-limited spot. No device pairs them with >=34.5 GHz. Gaussian approximation, detector noise only.

items.item: Derived: NEP a detector would need to read 406 quanta per 14.5-ps slot
items.value: 17.6 fW/rtHz at 300 K over 34.5 GHz. That is ~910x below Cai's absorbed-referenced 16 pW/rtHz, 3,300x below the best external room-temperature figure (58 pW/rtHz), 57,000x below the measured 1 nW/rtHz, and 1.9x below the 5-K bilayer bolometer (33 fW/rtHz).
items.source_title: Derived here
items.note: 18.55 nW / (5.691 x 1.857e5) = 1.755e-14 W/rtHz. Even an ideal detector stays above the ~400-quanta thermal floor.

items.item: Derived: read-port coupling penalty using Yoshioka 2024's measured eta
items.value:
Plasmon quanta needed = 406/eta at 300 K (477/eta at 353 K).
- eta 0.03 (Au-gated acoustic): 13,533 (15,900 at 353 K); 49-137x the cascade's 99-277 and 18-24x the 576-737 launch budget
- eta 0.35 (ZnO-gated unscreened): 1,160 (1,363 at 353 K); 4.2-11.7x and 1.6-2.0x
- eta 0.35 path plus a -1 to -3 dB acoustic-to-unscreened junction: 1,460-2,310
items.unit: 1-THz quanta at the plasmon side of the port
items.source_title: Derived from Yoshioka et al. 2024 (eta) and Part I Sec. 9.5 (406/477)
items.note: Assumes reciprocity, as the source does, and a loss at temperature T that leaves the thermal occupancy unchanged, so the required signal scales as 1/eta. eta was measured at 4 K on a 26-um ribbon fed by a 485-um CPW, not on a 576-nm cell at 300 K.

items.item: Derived: #141 rectification signal against electronic noise
items.value: Delta U = (0.017-0.021) x e*n/C_g = 8.1-11.2 mV. Here C_g = eps0*eps_z/d = 3.01-3.36 mF/m2 (eps_z 3.4-3.8 from Part I, d = 10 nm) and e*n/C_g = 0.48-0.53 V at n = 1e12 cm-2. Johnson noise of a 50-Ohm node at 300 K: 0.169 mV rms over 34.5 GHz, 0.239 mV over 69 GHz. Electronic SNR 34-66.
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Sec. 6.4 (+1.7-2.1% per '1') and Eq. (1) inputs
items.note: Assumes the drain-plane density shift appears unattenuated within the slot as a drain-to-gate voltage (U = e*n/C_g, quantum capacitance ignored). Excludes DC-bias shot/1-f noise and the field's own thermal noise.

items.item: Derived: optical gate energy for per-slot photoconductive sampling
items.value: Yoshioka 2024 uses 20 mW per switch at 16.8 MHz, i.e. 1.19 nJ per gate pulse. One gate per 14.5-ps slot (68.97 GS/s) then costs 82 W optical per readout line, 1.07 kW per lane (13 lines) and 7.5 kW for 91 lines (7 lanes). The 7-lane fabric itself dissipates 0.47-0.64 W. To fit 10 mW per line the gate must be <=0.145 pJ, 8,200x below the demonstrated pulse.
items.source_title: Derived from Yoshioka et al. 2024 Methods and Part III Sec. 4.6
items.note: An order-of-magnitude scaling only. No single-shot photoconductive sampler at >=69 GS/s was found, nor the minimum gate energy for adequate per-sample SNR.

items.item: Derived: gate and read-node RC
items.value: Yoshioka 2022's contact R and C, if behind a metal gate, would give RC 2.6-44 ps (3.6-62 GHz). One Fable cell: C_g ~3.0-3.4 fF for 1 um2 active, R ~58 Ohm (100 Ohm.um over an assumed 1.74-um width = 1 um2/576 nm), so RC ~0.17-0.19 ps (0.8-0.9 THz). A 50-Ohm read node reaches 34.5 GHz only if its capacitance is <=92 fF.
items.source_title: Derived from Yoshioka 2022 Table S1, Part I (eps_z 3.4-3.8, ~100 Ohm.um contacts) and Part III (1 um2 active)
items.note: 1/(2*pi*50 Ohm*34.5 GHz) = 92 fF. Covers the cell only; wiring and pads to the CMOS perimeter are unmodelled in the record and not found here.

items.item: Derived: measured plasmon lifetimes as Q at 1 THz
items.value:
Q = 2*pi*f*tau:
- Bandurin 0.3-0.9 ps (10-77 K): 1.9-5.7
- Caridad 0.6 ps (room temperature): 3.8
- Delgado-Notario 0.4-1.7 ps (1.7-15 K): 2.5-10.7
Fable design tau = 1 ps gives 6.3; the record's room-temperature baseline 0.4-0.6 ps gives 2.5-3.8.
items.source_title: Derived from Bandurin 2018, Caridad 2024, Delgado-Notario 2026
items.note: Assumes tau_p is frequency-independent between 2-4.7 THz and 1 THz.

items.item: Derived: bit-rate gap of THz-carrier graphene receivers
items.value: 69 Gb/s per readout line against 1-2 Gbit/s demonstrated at a THz carrier: 34-69x. At telecom, graphene PTE already does 105 Gbit/s NRZ.
items.source_title: Derived from Soundarapandian 2026, Marconi 2021, Part III Sec. 4.6

items.item: Derived: cryogenic floor and cold detectors
items.value: At 4 K the 1-THz occupancy is ~6.1e-6, so the homodyne floor is ~32.4 quanta. Over 34.5 GHz the 5-K bilayer bolometer (33 fW/rtHz) would still need ~763 quanta, though its intrinsic speed is only >1 GHz; the 10-K bilayer TFET (0.2 pW/rtHz) needs ~4,620.
items.source_title: Derived from J. Yan 2012 and Gayduchenko 2021

items.item: Derived: per-pulse resolution needed to measure DG4's launch jitter at the in-fabric plane
items.value: A homodyne-limited single-pulse amplitude estimate has relative noise sqrt((2n+1)/(4N)). Resolving sigma_rel = 4.0% needs N >= 1,960 quanta per pulse at the detector at 300 K; 2.3% needs N >= 5,920. That is 2.7-10.3x the 576-737 launch budget, before eta.
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Sec. 9.5 / Part III DG4 (sigma_rel <= 2.3-4.0%)
items.note: 12.53/(4 x 0.04^2) = 1,958; 12.53/(4 x 0.023^2) = 5,921. Variance subtraction over ~1e6 captured pulses could relax this, but it needs per-pulse capture, which lock-in equivalent-time sampling does not give.

mapping.fable_problem: Readout lines: per-slot decision on each of the 13 readout lines per lane (91 at 7 lanes) at 69 Gb/s (Part III Sec. 4.6), using an incoherent plasmon-assisted graphene detector (PTE, bolometric or DS square-law)
mapping.reason: The best room-temperature THz graphene detectors are Johnson-limited at 16 pW/rtHz (absorbed-referenced) or 58-160 pW/rtHz (external), and 1 nW/rtHz once real electronics are included. A 6.3e-9 decision in a 34.5-GHz band then needs 17-169 uW, i.e. 0.25-2.45 fJ or 3.7e5-3.7e6 quanta per 14.5-ps slot. That is 910-9,100x the 406-quanta floor and up to 37,000x the 99-277 quanta a loaded F = 2 cascade delivers; most cases also exceed the 2.5 uW launched per line. Cold detectors (0.2 pW/rtHz at 10 K; 33 fW/rtHz at 5 K, >1 GHz) still do not resolve slots.
mapping.what_must_be_true: NEP <= ~17.6 fW/rtHz at 300 K with >=34.5 GHz real-time bandwidth and eta ~1 from the plasmon. Alternatively >=30-35 dB of near-quantum-limited gain at 1 THz ahead of the detector; the InP HEMT the record cites gives 9 dB, and Part I Sec. 9.5 notes that pre-amplification cannot raise input-referred SNR.
mapping.quantified_effect: No positive effect. Shortfall 910-9,100x the 406-quanta floor (57,000x at the measured 1 nW/rtHz).

mapping.fable_problem: Readout bandwidth: resolving a 14.5-ps slot (>=34.5 GHz Nyquist, real-time, per line)
mapping.reason:
No graphene detector has resolved a single 14.5-ps slot in real time. Real-time responses to THz excitation:
- 110 ps FWHM, about 7.6 slots (Cai 2014, room temperature)
- 0.89-1.3 ns (Viti 2021); <=3.3 ns (Viti 2020); ~5 ns (Asgari 2021); <30 ns, setup-limited (Castilla 2019)
- 20-40 GHz only in a ~10 uA/W device, against 1-2 GHz for the 0.16 A/W devices; 1 Gbit/s open eye (Soundarapandian 2026)
Picosecond resolution exists only in equivalent time: 1.2-ps plasmon packets (4 K, Yoshioka 2024), 220 GHz PTE bandwidth (room temperature, Yoshioka 2022), 10.5 ps intrinsic at 150 K (Cai 2014). Optical-carrier PTE reaches >65 GHz at 105 Gbit/s and >400-500 GHz. For DS rectifiers in graphene, no GHz-class real-time measurement was found: all are read by 0.3-1 kHz lock-in. A GaAs plasmonic detector reached <=110 ps.
mapping.what_must_be_true: One device must combine >=34.5 GHz real-time bandwidth with usable responsivity at a ~1-THz carrier; current devices trade one for the other. The read node also needs sub-ps RC; a resistive ZnO gate lifted PTE bandwidth above 220 GHz.
mapping.quantified_effect: Bit-rate gap 34-69x at a THz carrier (1-2 Gbit/s against 69 Gb/s). Analog bandwidth of 40 GHz (10-90% rise ~8.8 ps, below 14.5 ps) exists only at ~10 uA/W.

mapping.fable_problem: Decision energy: >=406 quanta at 300 K (477 at 353 K) for a homodyne-limited decision at DG1's 6.3e-9 (Part I Sec. 9.5; Part III Sec. 4.6, limitation 12)
mapping.reason: The 1-THz mode's own thermal occupancy (n = 5.76) sets the floor, not the detector. An ideal noiseless square-law detector (any PTE, bolometric or DS mechanism) needs 400 quanta at 300 K and 476 at 353 K, within 1.5% of the record's homodyne 406/477, which are reproduced exactly as Q^2(2n+1). Every demonstrated detector adds noise on top of this.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Lowering the floor needs a colder signal mode (~32 quanta at 4 K) or more signal per decision, not a better detector.
mapping.quantified_effect: None. The record's floor is corroborated by an independent square-law calculation to within 1.5%.

mapping.fable_problem: Read-out port coupling: Part I Secs. 3.3/9.5 say 'no cited work quantifies the coupling efficiency', and which swing reaches the read-out port is open (issue #141)
mapping.reason: Part I's own ref [4] (Part II ref [16]), Yoshioka 2024, quantifies it at 4 K: eta ~0.03 per CPW-graphene interface for the Au-gated acoustic mode and >=0.35 for the ZnO-gated unscreened mode, limited by impedance and velocity mismatch and assumed reciprocal. The record cites the paper but not these numbers. Because a loss at temperature T leaves the thermal occupancy unchanged, a homodyne read through the port needs >=406/eta plasmon quanta.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The record's 406 holds at the port only if eta ~1. The measured values come from a 26-um ribbon on a 485-um CPW at 4 K; room-temperature damping would lower them further.
mapping.quantified_effect: 13,500 quanta needed at eta 0.03 (15,900 at 353 K): 49-137x the 99-277 delivered and 18-24x the 576-737 launch budget. 1,160 at eta 0.35: 4.2-11.7x and 1.6-2.0x.

mapping.fable_problem: Use an unscreened, THz-transparent (ZnO-gated) out-coupling section as the read-out port (the readout counterpart of the prior session's ZnO launch section)
mapping.reason: The same source gives eta >=0.35 for the unscreened mode against ~0.03 for the acoustic mode per interface (4 K). A ZnO-gated read section would cut the plasmon energy needed at the port by ~10.7 dB. A resistive ZnO gate also removed the gate-capacitance RC limit (220 GHz at room temperature, Yoshioka 2022), which suits a dedicated detector segment.
