mapping.what_must_be_true: The acoustic-to-unscreened transition must be low-loss; Part I Sec. 9.4 budgets -1 to -3 dB per junction, owned by the unrun Boltzmann-Maxwell tier. The unscreened section must keep tolerable damping at 300 K, and the cells keep their metal gates.
mapping.quantified_effect: Quanta needed at the port fall from 13,533 to 1,160 at 300 K (x11.7), or to 1,460-2,310 after a -1 to -3 dB junction. Still 4-23x above the 99-277 delivered.

mapping.fable_problem: Part I's photoconductive-sampling read-out chain (Table 2 row 'Launch, read-out, in-situ reference' [7]; Sec. 3.3; Sec. 9.5 'field-resolved and coherent'; Sec. 9.8 'every member ... room-temperature hardware')
mapping.reason:
Both cited demonstrations are cryogenic and equivalent-time:
- Kusyak [7]: data at 7 K, 196-kHz laser plus lock-in, -3 dB at 440 GHz, 1-THz component -23 dB (AC-coupled) / -39 dB (DC-coupled) relative to the strongest component
- Yoshioka [4]: 4 K, 16.8-MHz pump-probe plus lock-in
Part I flags [4]'s 4 K but not [7]'s 7 K, so Sec. 9.8's room-temperature claim is not supported by the cited data. Both resolve picoseconds by averaging repeated waveforms; neither is a single-shot per-slot reader.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A room-temperature, single-shot coherent sampler per readout line at >=69 GS/s, with noise near the thermal floor and sub-pJ gate pulses. Not found.
mapping.quantified_effect: At the demonstrated 1.19 nJ per gate pulse, per-slot sampling costs 82 W optical per readout line, 1.07 kW per lane and 7.5 kW for 91 lines, against the 0.47-0.64 W fabric. A 10 mW per line budget needs <=0.145 pJ per gate (8,200x less).

mapping.fable_problem: Issue #141 electrical read by the cell's own rectification (+1.7-2.1% drain density per '1', 90% in 6.9 ps, 21-35% carried into the next slot; Part I Sec. 6.4, Part III Sec. 4.6, limitation 12)
mapping.reason:
The mechanism exists experimentally in the cell's own boundary geometry: antenna-driven gate-to-source voltage, drain AC-open (r_s*r_d ~ -1), hBN-encapsulated graphene, fitted by DS rectification.
- Bandurin 2018: resonant to 77 K
- Caridad 2024: resonant to 300 K at 4.7 THz, tau_p ~0.6 ps; De Fazio 2026 calls these room-temperature resonances 'weak features'
- Vicarelli 2012: room temperature, overdamped, NEP <30 nW/rtHz
All are read by kHz lock-in. Caridad warns that DC source-drain bias raises rectified-signal noise, and the Fable cell is DC-biased. Derived: +1.7-2.1% of n is 8-11 mV of channel potential against 0.17-0.24 mV rms Johnson noise on a 50-Ohm node, so electronic noise need not bind. The binding limits are the ~400-quanta floor, the read-node RC and DC-bias noise.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The drain shift must reach a matched read node within the slot, in-band shot/1-f noise from the DC bias must stay small, and the reading cell must hold >=~400 quanta at 300 K (more than the 99-277 a loaded cascade sustains).
mapping.quantified_effect: Electronic SNR 34-66 on paper. The input-referred floor of ~400 quanta is unchanged.

mapping.fable_problem: Issue #141: gate and read-node RC unmodelled
mapping.reason: Yoshioka 2022 (room temperature) states that gate capacitance with contact resistance sets graphene PTE cut-off below 100 GHz; a resistive ZnO gate gave 220 GHz, and a 140,000 cm2/Vs sample gave only 51 GHz (photocurrent generation up to >4 ps). Their R and C behind a metal gate would give 2.6-44 ps. A single Fable cell is not RC-limited (C_g ~3.0-3.4 fF, R ~58 Ohm, RC ~0.17-0.19 ps, derived). The unmodelled wiring and pads to the CMOS perimeter will set the read node's speed.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Read-node capacitance <=~92 fF on a 50-Ohm node for 34.5 GHz, i.e. a sense amplifier close to the cell.
mapping.quantified_effect: Not quantifiable from the literature. Bound: <=92 fF per 50-Ohm read node (derived).

mapping.fable_problem: Limitation 12: 'nor a readout's own decision' for the ~800 lines (Part III Sec. 9)
mapping.reason:
The literature bounds the missing term but does not close it:
- an incoherent graphene detector needs ~1e5-1e6 quanta per slot
- a coherent read through a measured CPW-graphene interface needs 1,160-13,500 plasmon quanta
- per-slot photoconductive sampling at demonstrated gate energy costs ~82 W optical per line
- the #141 rectification read is electronically adequate on paper, but its floor is still ~400 quanta
All routes sit above the 99-277 quanta a loaded F = 2 cascade sustains at 300 K, consistent with the record's 'no booking passes warm'.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A last stage that restores the '1' to >=~400-500 quanta at the port (the record puts fan-out-1 at 628-955, outside its velocity domain), eta ~1 coupling, and a single-shot reader.
mapping.quantified_effect: A readout's own decision needs at least ~400 quanta (ideal). At the measured coupling it needs 1,160-13,500, and through an incoherent detector ~3.7e5-3.7e6, at 300 K.

mapping.fable_problem: Bench calibration of tau, s and the sub-threshold linewidth (Part I Sec. 10 calibration sequence; issue #88 linewidth matrix; boundary channel delta_b)
mapping.reason:
notes/CITATIONS.md cites Caridad 2024 for the #88 benchmark with 'read before quoting'. Read here in full:
- Q ~8.6 at 4.7 THz is a 10-K value
- tau_tr is 0.29 ps (10 K) and 0.23 ps (room temperature); tau_p ~0.6 ps
- resonances are visible from 10 to 300 K
Bandurin 2018, not in the record, adds that tau_p (0.3-0.9 ps) < tau_tr (~2 ps), with plasma-wave leakage into contacts and antennas largest at high density and low harmonic number. That is the Fable cell's fundamental mode at n = 1e12, so it is experimental evidence that the contact channel matters. Veksler 2006 (Part I [23]) already covers current-driven resonance narrowing.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The resonant-photovoltage protocol must transfer to a 576-nm cavity at 1 THz with d = 10 nm under DC drift. Contact leakage has to be separated from bulk loss by #88's contact-contrast pairs.
mapping.quantified_effect: Measured tau_p gives Q at 1 THz of 1.9-5.7 (Bandurin, <=77 K), 3.8 (Caridad, room temperature) and 2.5-10.7 (Delgado-Notario, cryogenic), against the design's 6.3 and the record's 2.5-3.8 room-temperature baseline.

mapping.fable_problem: Resonant antenna-coupled gate segment (Part I Sec. 9.5 launch mitigation, least mature) and its reciprocal use as a read port
mapping.reason: The resonant DS detectors use exactly this coupling: an antenna between source and top gate that drives the gate-to-channel voltage at the source (Bandurin's DS fit gives Z ~ 74 Ohm; also Caridad and Delgado-Notario). All are fed from free space through Si lenses. None reports an absolute antenna-to-plasmon energy efficiency.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A stripline-fed (on-chip) antenna-gate segment with its coupling measured at 1 THz.
mapping.quantified_effect: Not found.

mapping.fable_problem: DG4 / Part I Sec. 9.5: measuring launcher pulse-to-pulse jitter sigma_rel <= 2.3-4.0% at the in-fabric, post-coupling launch plane
mapping.reason: The demonstrated in-fabric readers (Yoshioka 2024, Kusyak 2025) are lock-in-averaged equivalent-time samplers. They return the mean waveform, not per-pulse amplitudes, so on their own they cannot measure sigma_rel. Derived: a homodyne-limited single-pulse estimate has relative noise sqrt((2n+1)/(4N)).
mapping.what_must_be_true: Single-shot capture at the slot rate, or variance subtraction over ~1e6 captured pulses with a characterized measurement-noise floor.
mapping.quantified_effect: Per-pulse resolution of 4.0% or 2.3% needs >=1,960 or >=5,920 quanta at the detector, 2.7-10.3x the 576-737 launch budget, before eta.

mapping.fable_problem: Cryogenic readout option (Part II's 4-K rows; Part III limitation 12 'nor a cryostat interface')
mapping.reason: Graphene detectors are far better cold: 33 fW/rtHz at 5 K with >1 GHz (bilayer bolometer, J. Yan 2012), 0.2 pW/rtHz at 10 K (bilayer TFET), and resonant DS detection is clean only <=77 K in bilayer graphene. At 4 K the 1-THz homodyne floor falls to ~32 quanta, but the coherent route actually demonstrated cold is photoconductive sampling at 4-7 K, and the bolometer cannot resolve slots.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The signal mode itself must be cold. Cooling the reader of a warm fabric does not remove the fabric-side occupancy, and the project's premise is room temperature.
mapping.quantified_effect: Floor 406 -> ~32 quanta only for a 4-K signal mode. A 5-K bolometer would still need ~763 quanta per 34.5-GHz slot.

mapping.fable_problem: Detector segment for reads and inverters (Part I Secs. 5/9.8: rectified output of a biased (x8-17 / x9-12 gain) or unbiased (x37-73) detector segment); zero-bias PTE split-gate junction as the unbiased variant
mapping.reason: Zero-bias PTE at a gate-defined pn junction reads plasmons within the same sheet: Lundeberg 2017 (mid-IR, room temperature), Alonso-Gonzalez 2017 (2.52-THz acoustic plasmons, room temperature), Castilla 2019 (80 pW/rtHz), Soundarapandian 2026. With no DC current the noise is Johnson only, avoiding the bias noise Caridad reports. Photocurrent generation takes from ~0 to >4 ps (Yoshioka 2022), comparable to #141's 6.9-ps rise. Fable's gate-defined CNP guard cells make a split-gate junction lithographically compatible.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The 0.5-1 um room-temperature cooling length and the Seebeck contrast must work in a sub-um segment, and the PTE response per plasmon quantum must be computed (not found). The ~400-quanta floor still applies.
mapping.quantified_effect: No change to the floor. Speed class ~0 to >4 ps against the record's 6.9-ps rectification rise.

mapping.fable_problem: Plasmon-enhanced absorption as a sensitivity lever (graphene-plasmon resonators raising detector responsivity)
mapping.reason:
In Fable the plasmon is the signal, so there is no absorption deficit to enhance. The reported gains are for free-space detectors:
- De Fazio 2026: up to 40% modulation and +30% over the conventional PTE maximum at 6-90 K, gone by 130 K
- Freitag 2013: ~10x in resonance (mid-IR)
- Guo 2018: >20x over unpatterned graphene (mid-IR, room temperature, 16 mA/W, 1.3 nW/rtHz)
- Cai 2015: Q 1.2 at 5.3 THz
Room-temperature graphene THz plasmon resonances are typically one to two orders below the conventional photoresponse.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

mapping.fable_problem: The review's own detector examples (refs 175, 181, 183-186) and H. Yan 2012 (ref 180) as I/O components
mapping.reason:
All are metal-plasmonic or photogating detectors from the visible to the mid-IR:
- Liu 2011: x15 EQE
- Yao 2014: 0.4 V/W at 4.45 um
- Ni 2017: 1e9 A/W, gain 1e12
- Chen 2017: 83 A/W, rise <600 ns
- Guo 2020 LSA: 0.4 A/W above 40 GHz at 1.55 um
H. Yan 2012 is a THz filter (8.2 dB) and polarizer (9.5 dB), not a detector. None detects a 1-THz graphene plasmon, and photogating gain is slow. They would matter only for an optical-carrier I/O, which lies outside the record's architecture.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

items.item: What the review itself contains on graphene-plasmon gain
items.value: 5 gain-related refs out of 198: [97] Low/Chen/Basov 2018 (theory: gapped-BLG resonant gain), [193] Apalkov & Stockman (proposal: nanospaser; listed as 2013, published 2014), [192] Zhu 2017 (ZnO-graphene Raman nanolaser), [194] Chakraborty 2016 and [195] Polini 2016 (QCL gain tuned by graphene). No reference to Ryzhii, Otsuji, Rana, Boubanga-Tombet, Li 2012, Gierz, Watanabe, Yadav, Popov/Polischuk or Petrov (checked against the Crossref reference list).
items.source_title: Cui, Wang, Sun, 'Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics', Reviews in Physics 6, 100054 (2021)
items.note: Read from a local PDF text extract plus the Crossref record. The review's text cites the resonant-gain paper as '[98] ... Wang et al.', but [98] is Hasdeo & Song 2017 (domain-wall plasmon lifetime); the gain paper is [97] Low, Chen, Basov, so [97] and [98] are swapped. The review gives no gain number, no THz-at-300-K gain discussion and no Dyakonov-Shur (DS) mechanism.

items.item: Rana & Ahmad: plasmon amplification by interband stimulated emission
items.unit: cm^-1 net plasmon power gain at 1-15 THz
items.source_title: F. Rana, F. R. Ahmad, 'Plasmon Amplification through Stimulated Emission at Terahertz Frequencies in Graphene', arXiv:0704.0607
items.note: Theory (RPA), steady-state inversion with n=p, ungated sheet (eps=4 eps0), tau=0.5 ps. Needs e-h density ~1e9 cm^-2 at 10 K and ~1e11 cm^-2 at 300 K. Intraband loss dominates at the lowest frequencies. The authors conclude that practical oscillators 'might only be realizable' above 1e11 cm^-2 and 5 THz. Plasmons are amplified (in theory); pump is optical or injection. No gain at 1 THz and 300 K.

items.item: Rana: graphene THz plasmon oscillator
items.value: net gain approaches 4e4 cm^-1 at 1-10 THz (77 and 300 K, n=p 1e10-5e11 cm^-2, tau 0.5 ps); below 1 THz intraband loss dominates; a 4-THz, 0.5 x 5 um, 77-K design needs ~1,800 cm^-1 threshold against ~20,000 cm^-1 available; ~2 kW/cm^2 CW 10-um pump (Auger time 10 ps assumed); ~1 uW output
items.source_title: F. Rana, 'Graphene Terahertz Plasmon Oscillators', IEEE Trans. Nanotechnol. 7, 91 (2008), arXiv:0710.3556
items.note: Theory. The author states that image-current losses in surrounding metals and ground planes are not included, which matters for Fable's Au gate 10 nm away. The proposed pumping is optical or forward-biased gated p-n injection. The 300-K curves gain only above ~1 THz.

items.item: Ryzhii, Ryzhii, Otsuji 2007 (Part I ref [3])
items.value: Abstract: population inversion 'can lead to the negative net ac conductivity in the terahertz range' at sufficiently strong pumping. This is a steady-state prediction; the abstract makes no claim about transient duration.
items.source_title: V. Ryzhii, M. Ryzhii, T. Otsuji, 'Negative dynamic conductivity of graphene with optical pumping', J. Appl. Phys. 101, 083114 (2007)
items.note: Only the abstract was read (via OpenAlex). Full text not accessible on 2026-11-03: the Tohoku repository open-access copy (records/47698) has been under maintenance since 2026-10-28, and the AIP copy is paywalled. Later papers by the same group (arXiv 1102.2026; NJP 2013) cite it as a prediction of steady-state negative dynamic conductivity (NDC).

items.item: Ryzhii et al.: CW optical pumping at 300 K, heating and cooling
items.value: Re sigma < 0 from ~2 THz to >=17 THz at I/I0 = 5 in the cooling regime (hbar*Omega0 = 100 meV, Omega0/omega0 = 0.5); S0 = hbar*Omega*I0 ~ 1.39e4 W/cm^2, so ~7e4 W/cm^2 (derived: 5 x 1.39e4). At Omega0/omega0 = 1, NDC only if eta_decay << 1; saturated eps_F ~ 7-17 meV (eta 1-3). Cooling regime gives T_sat 127-200 K and eps_F 33-58 meV.
items.source_title: V. Ryzhii et al., 'Effect of heating and cooling of photogenerated electron-hole plasma in optically pumped graphene on population inversion', JJAP 50, 094001 (2011), arXiv:1102.2026
items.note: Theory, T0 = 300 K, nu0 = 2.5e11-1e12 s^-1 (tau of a few ps at thermal energy). The authors state that accumulated optical phonons 'can prevent' room-temperature inversion. The CW window starts at ~2 THz, so 1 THz is excluded.

items.item: Satou et al.: THz inversion under pulse excitation
items.value: 300 K: THz-range inversion lasts ~10 ps. The lowest NDC frequency is ~0.7 THz (hbar*Omega = 0.1 eV, tau = 10 ps) or ~1.1 THz (0.8 eV, tau = 10 ps). At 1 THz, Re sigma saturates at about -0.4 e^2/4hbar (tau = 10 ps, 0.1 eV). Illustrative fluences: 6e3 / 1e3 / 1e2 nJ/cm^2 at 0.8 / 0.4 / 0.2-0.1 eV.
items.source_title: A. Satou, V. Ryzhii, Y. Kurita, T. Otsuji, J. Appl. Phys. 113, 143108 (2013), arXiv:1210.6704
items.note: Theory. Reaching 1 THz at 300 K requires tau ~10 ps, ten times Fable's tau = 1 ps. The ~10-ps THz inversion lifetime contradicts the 'sub-picosecond' wording in Part I.

items.item: Boubanga-Tombet et al.: room-temperature amplified stimulated THz emission (optical pump)
items.value: threshold ~1e7 W/cm^2 peak (no emission below 5e6), operated at ~3e7 W/cm^2; 1550 nm, 80 fs, 20 MHz, ~4 mW, 40-um spot; THz probe 2 ps and 3.5 ps after the pump; emission band ~1-5 THz (thick crystal) and ~1-6 THz (thin crystal), system-limited at 6 THz
items.source_title: S. Boubanga-Tombet et al., 'Ultrafast carrier dynamics and terahertz emission in optically pumped graphene at room temperature', PRB 85, 035443 (2012); arXiv:1011.2618
items.note: Measured at 300 K on exfoliated monolayer on SiO2/Si. What was amplified is a free-space THz photon echo, not a plasmon. The gain is transient (ps scale) per pump pulse. Magnitude is given only relative to the 2.3% quantum limit (Watanabe 2013, citing this paper: '>10x'). The PRB version itself is paywalled and was not read. The lower band edge is set by Drude absorption, so 1 THz sits at the edge.

items.item: Watanabe et al.: SPP-mediated gain enhancement (optical pump, 300 K)
items.value: pump 3e7 W/cm^2 = 2.4 uJ/cm^2 (0.8 eV, 80 fs, 20 MHz, 120-um beam); probe 3.5 ps after pump; gain band lower cutoff starts ~2 THz and ends ~1.6 THz, independent of pump; upper cutoff 3.5-4.1 THz; peak ~4 THz; enhancement >~50 over the quantum-conductance limit (calculated >~10), attributed to SPP excitation
items.source_title: T. Watanabe et al., New J. Phys. 15, 075003 (2013)
items.note: Plasmon involvement is inferred from TM-localized spatial maps, not measured on a propagating plasmon. tau_m '3.3 ps' is an estimate from the Raman G/D ratio, not from transport. The paper's theory gives SPP gain ~1e4 cm^-1 at 300 K (eps_F 10-60 meV). No gain below ~1.6 THz, so none at Fable's 1 THz.

items.item: Li et al.: femtosecond population inversion (near-IR)
items.value: negative conductivity at 1.16 eV for the first ~200 fs, above ~2,000 uJ/cm^2 (35-fs, 1.55-eV pump)
items.note: Near-IR photons (~280 THz), not THz, not plasmons. Epitaxial graphene on SiC, mu ~0.4 eV, up to 0.5e14 cm^-2 photoexcited. Measurement temperature is not stated in the arXiv text.

items.item: Gierz et al.: direct observation of inversion lifetime (tr-ARPES)
items.value: separate electron and hole Fermi distributions (inversion) merge within ~130 fs after 950-meV, 4.6-mJ/cm^2 excitation; a 300-meV pump (0.8 mJ/cm^2) only heats carriers (Te ~3,000 K)
items.source_title: I. Gierz et al., 'Snapshots of non-equilibrium Dirac carrier distributions in graphene', Nat. Mater. 12, 1119 (2013), arXiv:1304.1389
items.note: Room temperature; gain not measured. This is the sub-picosecond result that applies to inversion at high energy.

items.item: Page, Ballout, Hess, Hamm: spontaneous plasmon emission competes with gain
items.value: 34 fs (exact) vs ~187 fs (Drude approximation) carrier recombination by spontaneous plasmon emission at mu = 0.2 eV, T = 0; 18 fs at 230 K, m = -0.5; gain peak at omega ~2.3e14 s^-1
items.source_title: A. F. Page et al., 'Nonequilibrium plasmons with gain in graphene', PRB 91, 075404 (2015), arXiv:1412.3042
items.note: Theory, free-standing graphene, mid-IR scale. Plasmon gain is possible but drains the inversion in tens of fs.

items.item: Svintsov, Ryzhii, Otsuji: negative 'interband Drude' conductivity
items.value: for uncorrelated disorder, interband-Drude processes cut Drude absorption by at most ~5% (eps_F 50 meV, kappa0 = 5, room temperature); only long-range-correlated disorder (l_c ~100 nm) drives the net Drude conductivity negative, near omega ~ v0/l_c, with amplification above 2.3%
items.source_title: D. Svintsov, V. Ryzhii, T. Otsuji, Appl. Phys. Express 7, 115101 (2014), arXiv:1408.7023
items.note: Theory only. Still requires a population-inverted e-h plasma (CW pump) and engineered correlated disorder. No experiment found.

items.item: Yadav et al.: current-injection THz light-emitting graphene transistor
items.value: amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) over 1-7.6 THz, max ~10 uW (abstract; the group's 2022 review says ~80 uW); single-mode 5.2 THz at ~0.1 uW (Q 170, 30.6 GHz linewidth), both at 100 K; emission threshold temperature 100-150 K
items.source_title: D. Yadav et al., Nanophotonics 7, 741 (2018); T. Otsuji et al., Nanophotonics 11, 1677 (2022)
items.note: Distributed-feedback dual-gate graphene FET on epitaxial graphene. CW, DC-injected THz photons (not plasmons). tau = 1.5-4 ps (300 to 100 K). Not at 300 K. The 10 vs 80 uW discrepancy is between the group's own two papers. De Gruyter served an empty 202 response, so the 2022 review was read via Europe PMC (PMC11502014).

items.item: Otsuji group status 2022-2023: room-temperature current-injection interband gain
items.value: Not reported through 2023. The 2023 chapter describes no experiment newer than 2020 and calls the Coulomb-drag and PT-symmetry mechanisms 'yet to be experimentally verified'. The only room-temperature result is the 9% current-driven plasmonic amplification. Searches on 2026-11-03 found no 2024-2026 experiment.
items.source_title: T. Otsuji et al., Nanophotonics 11, 1677 (2022); T. Otsuji, 'Graphene-Based Plasmonic Terahertz Laser Transistors', IntechOpen (2023)
items.note: The 2022 review text was read directly; the 2023 chapter was read through a summarizing fetch, so quotations from it are medium confidence.

items.item: Boubanga-Tombet et al. 2021: the PRX 2020 room-temperature amplification re-read by its own authors
items.value: 9% gain (= 0.37 dB, derived: 10*log10(1.09)), 4x the quantum limit; EQE ~0.1 (Pout ~2.7 uW, Pin ~32 uW); thresholds 5.4-9.4 kV/cm for L_G 1.5-0.5 um; s ~3e8 cm/s, v0,max 3.85e7 cm/s. Authors: amplified reflection [their ref 17, Dyakonov-Shur 1993] plus transit-time instabilities are 'most likely' the mechanism, increment ~0.87 THz vs decrement ~0.3 THz (linewidth ~0.6 THz). A phenomenological model without instability (break-even v1/s1 = 1/sqrt 3) is kept as the alternative.
items.source_title: S. Boubanga-Tombet et al., 'Paving the Way for Tunable Graphene Plasmonic THz Amplifiers', Front. Phys. 9, 726806 (2021)
items.note: Read from the HAL PDF (hal-04840443). Same experiment as Part I ref [2] (PRX 10, 031004), which had excluded DS because the resonance width did not narrow. The 2022 review says that if an instability is at work, the transit-time type is most probable. This is THz photon amplification mediated by plasmon resonances: CW DC bias, 300 K, ~1-3 THz.

items.item: Koseki et al. (Part I ref [21])
items.value: >4e12 s^-1 total plasmon growth rate at room temperature, from simultaneous Dyakonov-Shur and Ryzhii-Satou-Shur (transit-time) instabilities
items.note: Boltzmann simulation with acoustic-phonon-limited scattering only. Already in the record.

items.item: Petrov et al. (Part I ref [20])
items.value: threshold drift can be tuned below both the plasmon phase velocity and the saturation velocity; increment can exceed the collisional damping of graphene at room temperature
items.source_title: A. S. Petrov, D. Svintsov, V. Ryzhii, M. S. Shur, PRB 95, 045405 (2017), arXiv:1610.07035
items.note: Hydrodynamic transfer-matrix theory. A DS-family mechanism (amplified reflection), already in the record.

items.item: Ryzhii et al.: injection (p-i-n) graphene THz laser at 300 K
items.value: injected e-h plasma cools to T ~0.60 T0 = 180 K at J ~31 mA/cm (20-um i-section, T0 = 300 K); NDC in the THz range at moderate voltage; optical-phonon heating can block room-temperature lasing
items.source_title: V. Ryzhii et al., 'Toward the creation of terahertz graphene injection laser', J. Appl. Phys. 110, 094503 (2011), arXiv:1110.1808
items.note: Theory for intrinsic p-i-n graphene, not an n = 1e12 cm^-2 gated channel.

items.item: Ryzhii et al.: graphene-black phosphorus injection, plasmon amplification
items.value: at 300 K, Re sigma < 0 only for f >= 3.44-6.50 THz (tau0 = 3.6-1.0 ps); plasmon amplification 1.5-2.0e4 cm^-1 in that window; j ~1.6e3-1.6e4 A/cm^2 at 0.1 V
items.note: Theory. Even with injection cooling, the gain window at 300 K starts at >=3.4 THz.

items.item: Popov et al.: plasmonic THz lasing in a graphene nanocavity array, and planar Bragg resonator
items.value: Lasing occurs when plasmon gain balances plasmon radiative damping; amplification at plasmon resonances is 'many orders of magnitude' stronger (abstracts). Numerical conditions: not found.
items.source_title: V. V. Popov et al., PRB 86, 195437 (2012); V. V. Popov et al., J. Opt. 15, 114009 (2013)
items.note: Theory with optical pumping. Abstracts only: the PRB is paywalled, and IOPscience returned a Radware CAPTCHA for the J. Opt. PDF, which was not bypassed.

items.item: Polischuk et al.: plasmonic amplification with carrier injection
items.value: An amplified plasmon mode is excited in the ungated active region of a periodic structure with injecting gated parts; lasing conditions derived (abstract). Numbers: not found.
items.source_title: O. V. Polischuk, D. V. Fateev, T. Otsuji, V. V. Popov, Appl. Phys. Lett. 111, 081110 (2017)
items.note: Theory; abstract only (paywalled).

items.item: Morozov, Popov, Fateev: active graphene directional coupler
items.value: with tau = 1 ps and a 100-meV quasi-Fermi level in the active graphene, plasmon absorption turns negative only above ~5 THz; wave-to-plasmon transformation coefficient >6; unidirectionality up to 80%
items.source_title: M. Yu. Morozov, V. V. Popov, D. V. Fateev, Sci. Rep. 11, 11697 (2021)
items.note: Theory, read via Europe PMC full text (PMC8169778). Gain sets in at 5 THz or above.

items.item: Apalkov & Stockman: graphene nanospaser (in the review)
items.value: mid-IR spaser at hbar*omega_q ~0.15 eV (= 36.3 THz, derived 0.15 eV / h); single InGaAs/AlInAs QC period, hbar*omega12 = 130 meV, d12 = 1.5 e*nm, L ~16 nm, tau12 ~1 ps; Q_min ~0.1; R = 5-nm patch, ~100 MV/m per plasmon; tau_min ~0.02 ps over 0.1-0.3 eV, rising sharply outside that range
items.source_title: V. Apalkov, M. I. Stockman, 'Proposed graphene nanospaser', Light Sci. Appl. 3, e191 (2014), arXiv:1303.0220
items.note: Proposal only; electrically pumped; no temperature analysis. At 1 THz an intersubband transition is 4.14 meV, below kT = 25.9 meV at 300 K. The arXiv text is internally inconsistent between its Eq. (8) and Fig. 3, so no 1-THz threshold is derived from it here.

items.item: Low, Chen, Basov: resonant gain in population-inverted gapped bilayer graphene (review ref [97])
items.value: gain window Delta <~ hbar*omega <~ mu_e - mu_h, with Delta ~0.2 eV (tunable to 300 meV), i.e. mid-IR; calculations at 300 K; the authors put the inverted-state lifetime in monolayer graphene at ~100 fs
items.source_title: T. Low, P.-Y. Chen, D. N. Basov, PRB 98, 041403(R) (2018), arXiv:1712.09924
items.note: Theory. A gap of 4 meV or more blocks any gain at 4 meV, so 1 THz is excluded.

items.item: Chakraborty et al.: graphene plasmons modulating THz QCL gain (review ref [194])
items.value: aperiodic-DFB THz QCL near 2.8 THz, characterized below 10 K; the QCL provides the gain and gated graphene switches mode losses
items.source_title: S. Chakraborty et al., Science 351, 246 (2016)
items.note: Graphene is not the gain medium. Cryogenic.

items.item: Zhu et al.: ZnO-graphene Raman nanolaser (review ref [192])
items.value: thresholdless tunable Raman nanolaser, visible to near-IR, room temperature; Stokes photons 'greatly amplified by the surface plasmon'
items.source_title: H. Zhu et al., Adv. Mater. 29, 1604351 (2017)
items.note: Abstract only. Optical-frequency Raman gain; no THz relevance.

items.item: THz QCL temperature record (context for quantum-well gain at THz)
items.value: Tmax ~261 K, lasing near 4 THz
items.source_title: A. Khalatpour et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 122, 161101 (2023)
items.note: Read from a text extract already in the session scratchpad. No QCL-type gain exists at 1 THz and 300 K.

items.item: Huang et al. 2020 (Part I ref [14]): carrier lifetime in graphene/hBN
items.value: ~30-35 ps at 4 K for photoexcited density <0.1-0.7e9 cm^-2 under CW 117-meV excitation; drops to a few ps (slope -1/Gamma2 ~0.7 ps) once hBN hyperbolic phonon-polariton emission switches on (V_DS* >= 0.07 V or P >= 0.5 mW)
items.source_title: P. Huang et al., Nat. Commun. 11, 863 (2020)
items.note: Read via Europe PMC full text. Cryogenic and at very low density. In Fable's hBN stack, hBN polariton emission is an additional fast recombination channel that works against sustaining an inversion. Part I uses [14] only for residual density.

items.item: Drift-current 'negative Landau damping' (Cherenkov-type) plasmon gain
items.value: graphene on SiC: plasmon amplification at 22.78-27.82 THz with drift v0 of order v_F/2 (theory). Disputed for the 2017 bilayer version (Svintsov & Ryzhii Comment, PRL 123, 219401 (2019)).
items.source_title: T. A. Morgado, M. G. Silveirinha, ACS Photonics 8, 1129 (2021), arXiv:2009.09301
items.note: Requires drift faster than the plasmon phase velocity. Fable's s = 2.33e6 m/s is 2.33 v_F (derived 2.33e6/1e6), so no achievable drift reaches it.

items.item: Zener-Klein transit-time diode (GPIN-TTD), a non-DS THz gain proposal
items.value: at 300 K, transit-time resonances at 0.63 THz (2l = 1 um) and 1.26-2.11 THz (2l = 0.3-0.5 um), negative conductance Gm ~ -0.1; requires low effective permittivity (kappa_eff <~ 1.2-6.2)
items.source_title: V. Ryzhii et al., 'Transit-time resonances enabling amplification and generation of terahertz radiation in periodic graphene p-i-n structures with the Zener-Klein interband tunneling', arXiv:2208.13525 (doi 10.1063/5.0124086)
items.note: Theory only; no experiment found. A room-temperature Coulomb-drag ballistic-injection instability is also predicted (APL 119, 093501 (2021), doi 10.1063/5.0061722), also unverified.

items.item: Graphene Landau-level THz lasers
items.value: Theory only (Wendler & Malic 2015 and follow-ups; requires a magnetic field and cryogenic temperature). Experimental gain or lasing: not found.
items.source_title: F. Wendler, E. Malic, 'Towards a tunable graphene-based Landau level laser in the terahertz regime', Sci. Rep. (2015)
items.note: Not applicable to a room-temperature, field-free fabric.

items.item: Claim of >1 ps room-temperature inversion in epitaxial graphene on SiC
items.value: The 2023 chapter cites Someya et al. 2017 for population inversion 'more than 1 ps'. The primary abstract does not state a duration: not verified.
items.source_title: T. Someya et al., PRB 95, 165303 (2017), as cited in Otsuji (IntechOpen 2023)
items.note: Paywalled; no arXiv copy found.

items.item: Random-grating graphene plasmon amplifier (simulation)
items.value: resonant enhancement up to 175x; a 60 K rise in ambient temperature cuts amplified output 70x
items.source_title: A. G. Ardakani, P. Rafieipour, arXiv:2107.01811
items.note: Simulation only. Shows how steeply photo-inverted gain falls with temperature.

items.item: DERIVED: Fable acoustic-plasmon loss in gain units
items.source_title: Derived from Fable Part I record values (tau = 1 ps, s = 2.33e6 m/s, 27.3/Q dB per wavelength)
items.note: Arithmetic: (1/tau)/s = 1e12/2.33e6 = 4.29e5 m^-1 = 4.29e3 cm^-1. Check: 27.29/6.283 = 4.34 dB per 2.33 um = 1.86e4 dB/cm, /4.343 = 4.29e3 cm^-1. Rana's 1-4e4 cm^-1 is 2.3-9.3x this, but only at f >= ~2-4 THz.

items.item: DERIVED: ceiling on interband (stimulated-emission) gain at the Fable density and 1 THz
items.value: R = gain rate / Drude loss rate <= 0.174 (tau 1 ps), 0.405 (tau 2.33 ps), 0.069 (tau 0.4 ps); R = 1 needs f >= 2.40 / 1.57 / 3.79 THz, or tau >= 5.8 ps at 1 THz
items.source_title: Derived from the graphene conductivity used by Ryzhii et al. 2011 (Eqs. 30-31) and Rana 2008, applied to Fable's E_F = 117 meV
items.note: Damping rate Gamma = 1/tau + Re(sigma_inter)*omega^2/D, from sigma = D/(1/tau - i*omega) + sigma_r and sigma = i*omega*K(q); this holds for any geometry, gated included. sigma_Q = e^2/4hbar = 6.085e-5 S. D = (e^2/(pi*hbar^2))*W with W = 117.6 meV at 300 K, so D = 1.384e10 S/s. omega^2*tau = 3.948e13 at tau = 1 ps, giving R = 6.085e-5 x 3.948e13 / 1.384e10 = 0.174. This assumes perfect inversion (factor 1); any real inversion is lower. The ceiling does not depend on temperature.

items.item: DERIVED: best case for a photo-inverted symmetric e-h plasma at 1 THz
items.value: R_max = 0.142 at mu = 40.9 meV (300 K, tau 1 ps), needing tau >= 7.0 ps for transparency; 0.121 at 353 K (tau >= 8.3 ps); 0.231 with injection-cooled carriers at 180 K (tau >= 4.3 ps); 0.498 at 77 K (tau >= 2.0 ps). At 300 K, R = 1 is reached at 2.74 / 1.76 / 1.47 THz for tau = 1 / 2.33 / 3.3 ps.
items.source_title: Derived (Fermi-Dirac, W = 2kT ln(1+e^{mu/kT}), interband factor tanh((hbar*omega - 2mu)/4kT)); checked against Watanabe 2013, Satou 2013, Ryzhii 2019
items.note: Optimistic: assumes carriers at lattice temperature. Cross-checks: at tau = 3.3 ps the model gives 1.47 THz against Watanabe's measured lower cutoff of 1.6-2 THz (tau_m 3.3 ps estimated). At tau = 10 ps it gives 0.84 THz against Satou's ~1.1 THz (0.8-eV pump). It is consistent with the >=2 THz of Ryzhii 2011 and the >=3.44 THz of Ryzhii 2019.

items.item: DERIVED: hole injection into Fable's gated n = 1e12 channel (two quasi-Fermi levels)
items.value: best R = 0.098 (tau 1 ps) or 0.228 (tau 2.33 ps) at 300 K with p ~2.5e11 cm^-2 (mu_c 121.8 meV, mu_v -38.8 meV, inversion factor 0.80, W 166 meV); 0.091 / 0.213 at 353 K with p ~3.2e11 cm^-2. This upper bound gives M_th 0.125 -> 0.113 and per-gate loss 2.17 -> 1.96 dB (300 K) or 2.56 -> 2.33 dB (353 K).
items.source_title: Derived (same model, n - p = 1e12 cm^-2 fixed by the gate)
items.note: Penalties: s rises x1.19 (sqrt(166/117.6)), detuning the 576-nm cell. Counter-drifting holes (W_h = 44 of 166 meV) cut the Drude-weighted drift that drives DS to (122 - 44)/166 = 0.47 of v0 (rough single-fluid estimate; e-h friction ignored). n_sp = 1.0024, so there is no noise penalty.

items.item: DERIVED: added energy per MAC for each pumping route (lane of 8,169-8,455 cells, 2.207 TMAC/s)
items.value: CW optical at 6.95e4 W/cm^2 (Ryzhii 2011): 0.695 mW per 1-um^2 active area, 68-89x the cell's 7.78-10.22 uW, giving 2.57-2.66 pJ/MAC (66-92x of 29-39 fJ/MAC). Pulsed, one pump per 14.5-ps slot: 2.4 uJ/cm^2 gives 24 fJ/cell/slot and 6.1-6.3 pJ/MAC; 0.8 uJ/cm^2 gives 2.0-2.1 pJ/MAC; Satou's 0.1 uJ/cm^2 (0.1-eV pump, needs tau = 10 ps) gives 0.26 pJ/MAC; Li's 2 mJ/cm^2 gives 5.1-5.3 nJ/MAC. Electrical hole injection to p = 2.5e11: 2.15-64.6 uW per cell (tau_r = 30-1 ps), +8-247 fJ/MAC.
items.source_title: Derived from Ryzhii 2011, Watanabe 2013, Satou 2013, Li 2012, and Fable Part III lane figures
items.note: Arithmetic: E/MAC = P_cell x N_cells / 2.207e12, or E_slot x N_cells / 32. Hole injection: P/A = (p/tau_r) x 0.1606 eV. The DS Joule saving from R = 0.098 is 1 - 0.902^2 = 18.6% of 7.78-10.22 uW, i.e. 1.45-1.90 uW, so energy breaks even only if tau_r >= 34-45 ps. No measured tau_r exists for this configuration; Huang 2020 measured 30-35 ps only at 4 K and very low density.

items.item: DERIVED: interband gain alone against G1
items.value: Even at the perfect-inversion ceiling, the cell keeps a net loss of >=1.79 dB per gate at 300 K (2.17 x (1 - 0.174)) and >=2.12 dB at 353 K (2.56 x (1 - 0.173)), against the G1 requirement of +2.6 dB net gain: a shortfall of >=4.4-4.7 dB.
items.source_title: Derived (ceiling above, applied to Part I per-gate loss and the G1 pass threshold)
items.note: Excludes interband gain as a fallback for G1 at 1 THz, at 300 or 353 K, for any pump.

mapping.fable_problem: G1 fallback: single-cell net gain >= +2.6 dB at <= 80 C at 1 THz without Dyakonov-Shur gain, using interband population-inversion gain (optical, current-injection or quantum-well/spaser)
mapping.reason: At 1 THz the Drude loss always wins. At Fable's density, even perfect inversion cancels at most 17.4% of the damping (tau 1 ps; 40.5% at 2.33 ps), and an optimized photo-inverted plasma at 300/353 K reaches only 14.2/12.1%. Every primary source puts room-temperature net gain at >=1.5-6.5 THz: Watanabe measured a 1.6-2 THz lower cutoff; Ryzhii 2011 >=2 THz; Ryzhii 2019 >=3.44 THz; Morozov >5 THz. 1 THz is reached only with tau ~10 ps (Satou 2013). Intersubband gain at 4.14 meV cannot be inverted at kT = 25.9 meV; the best THz QCL reaches ~261 K at ~4 THz. Every experiment amplified photons: transient room-temperature gain at >=1.6 THz, or CW gain at 100 K.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Merely reaching transparency at 1 THz needs one of: tau >= 5.8 ps (perfect-inversion ceiling) to 7.0-8.3 ps (e-h plasma optimum at 300-353 K), against the record's 1 ps, the measured 0.4-0.6 ps and a ceiling of ~1.2-2.33 ps; or a carrier at >= 2.4-2.7 THz (tau 1 ps), which Part I §1's 1-THz compromise rules out; or carriers at <= ~77 K with tau >= 2 ps, which breaks the cryo-free, <= 80 C charter.
mapping.quantified_effect: The interband-only cell stays at a net loss of >=1.79 dB per gate (300 K) or >=2.12 dB (353 K), against the +2.6 dB G1 threshold: a shortfall of >=4.4-4.7 dB (derived).

mapping.fable_problem: Loss budget / gain margin of the DS cell (Part I Eq. 3: M_th = 0.125; per-gate loss 2.17 dB at 300 K, 2.56 dB at 353 K) using interband gain as an add-on (hole injection into the n = 1e12 channel)
mapping.reason: The ideal bound on the improvement is small: the damping rate falls 9.8% (tau 1 ps) to 22.8% (tau 2.33 ps) at the best hole density p ~2.5-3.2e11 cm^-2. Three costs pull the other way and are probably larger: (1) counter-drifting holes cut the Drude-weighted drift that drives DS to ~0.47 of v0; (2) s rises x1.19 and detunes the 576-nm cell; (3) sustaining p costs 2.15-64.6 uW per cell electrically (or 0.47-14 mW optically), against a DS Joule saving of <=1.45-1.90 uW. On top of that, hole drift, electron-hole drag damping, and how a p-contact interacts with the DS source and drain clamps are all unmodelled. No primary work tests interband gain inside a drift-biased cell.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Holes sustained in steady state at p ~2.5e11 cm^-2 (mu_v ~ -39 meV) with carrier temperature at the lattice temperature; recombination time tau_r >= 34-45 ps at 300 K in n-doped, hBN-encapsulated graphene (none measured; Huang 2020 found 30-35 ps only at 4 K and ~1e9 cm^-2, collapsing to a few ps once hBN polariton emission switches on); DS drive not diluted by the hole fluid; the cell re-trimmed for s x1.19.
mapping.quantified_effect: Upper bound, derived: M_th 0.125 -> 0.113 (-9.8%) and per-gate loss 2.17 -> 1.96 dB at 300 K, 2.56 -> 2.33 dB at 353 K (tau 1 ps); up to -22.8% at tau 2.33 ps. Probably cancelled by the ~0.47x drift dilution and by +8-247 fJ/MAC of injection power.

mapping.fable_problem: Energy per MAC (29-39 fJ/MAC at 300 K; 7.78-10.22 uW per cell)
mapping.reason: Every non-DS gain route adds energy, and none removes the DS bias.
mapping.what_must_be_true: An electrically injected inversion with recombination time >= 34-45 ps at 300 K, which has not been observed. Even then the gain fraction is limited by the ceiling above.
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived. CW optical pumping (Ryzhii 2011, 6.95e4 W/cm^2 on 1 um^2): +2.57-2.66 pJ/MAC (66-92x). Pulsed pump per 14.5-ps slot: +2.0-6.3 pJ/MAC (0.26 pJ/MAC with Satou's 0.1-eV pump, which needs tau = 10 ps); Li-type near-IR inversion: +5.1-5.3 nJ/MAC. Electrical hole injection: +8-247 fJ/MAC. Heat: the cell already dissipates 1.267 kW/cm^2 over its 1-um^2 active area at 353 K; CW optical pumping at 6.95e4 W/cm^2 is ~55x that.

mapping.fable_problem: Part I Table 1 alternatives (room-temperature-relevant logic or gain technologies)
mapping.reason: None of these is a room-temperature, restoring THz logic family, and none provides gain at 1 THz and 300 K. Graphene current-injection emitters work only at 100 K (threshold 100-150 K; 1-7.6 THz ASE at <=10-80 uW; 5.2 THz single-mode at 0.1 uW). Optically pumped graphene gain is transient (ps), at room temperature and >=1.6-2 THz, and amplifies photons. THz QCLs reach <=261 K at ~4 THz. The spaser is a mid-IR (~36 THz) proposal. Gapped-BLG gain is mid-IR theory. The one room-temperature graphene THz amplifier (9% = 0.37 dB, current-driven) is already in the record as ref [2].
mapping.what_must_be_true: A room-temperature 1-THz interband or QW gain medium, which the bound above excludes. If Table 1 were extended with gain media rather than logic, a 'graphene interband THz laser' row would read: cryogenic CW (<=150 K) or room-temperature ps-transient at >=1.6 THz.
mapping.quantified_effect: None: no Table 1 entry changes.

mapping.fable_problem: Part I §1 (p. 3): 'Optically pumped gain ... cannot be sustained beyond a sub-picosecond transient [3]'
mapping.reason: Part I already rejects optical pumping, but the stated reason and the citation do not match the primary sources. Ref [3]'s abstract predicts steady-state NDC under strong pumping and makes no transient claim. THz-range gain at room temperature was observed 2-3.5 ps after the pump (Boubanga-Tombet 2012; Watanabe 2013) and is predicted to last ~10 ps (Satou 2013). The sub-picosecond figures belong to near-IR and mid-IR inversion: ~200 fs (Li 2012), ~130 fs (Gierz 2013), '~100 fs' (Low 2018). The conclusion survives on a firmer basis: at 1 THz interband gain cannot exceed 17.4% of the Drude loss at tau 1 ps, and the room-temperature gain band starts at >=1.6 THz.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Qualify, don't contest: re-cite the sub-ps statement to Li 2012 / Gierz 2013 and state the 1-THz Drude ceiling. This would be an ERRATA row of the I-41...I-43 type (text attributes something to cited work); no promoted note exists yet, so flag the convention. The full text of [3] could not be read (Tohoku repository under maintenance since 2026-10-28), so check it before filing.
mapping.quantified_effect: No released number moves. Cited duration: 'sub-ps' becomes ps to ~10 ps for THz-range inversion. Supporting bound: R <= 0.174 at 1 THz.

mapping.fable_problem: Part I §1-2 and Table 2: the gain mechanism of ref [2] (PRX 2020), described as attributed by its authors 'to dissipative phase shift, not DS'
mapping.reason: That description is correct for the PRX paper. The same authors' 2021 follow-up on the same devices (Front. Phys. 9, 726806) says amplified reflection at the cavity boundaries (citing Dyakonov-Shur 1993) plus transit-time instabilities are 'most likely' the mechanism (increment ~0.87 THz vs decrement ~0.3 THz), while keeping the non-instability model as the alternative. The group's 2022 review calls a transit-time instability the most probable if an instability is involved. This makes a DS-type contribution to the room-temperature data more plausible, but it remains an interpretation, not a demonstration.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Qualify the record sentence with the 2021 reading. G1 and G4 stay unrun, and the record's 'experimentally unconfirmed' status for DS-cavity gain stands.
mapping.quantified_effect: None on released numbers. Evidence: 9% (0.37 dB) gain, room temperature, thresholds 5.4-9.4 kV/cm, s/v0 >= 7.8.

mapping.fable_problem: Drift-driven Cherenkov / 'negative Landau damping' as a non-DS gain for the acoustic plasmon
mapping.reason: It needs drift faster than the plasmon phase velocity. Fable's s = 2.33 v_F, while drift is below v_F, so it is kinematically excluded. Part I §7.5 (p. 31) already states that Im Pi_intra vanishes above v_F q for any electron distribution, drifted or not. The Morgado-Silveirinha gain is at 22.8-27.8 THz on SiC and disputed (PRL 123, 219401).
mapping.what_must_be_true: A mode slower than the drift (phase velocity below ~5e5 m/s at 1 THz), which a gated graphene plasmon never is (s > v_F).
mapping.quantified_effect: None (excluded: s/v_F = 2.33).

mapping.fable_problem: Current-driven gain mechanisms other than DS (transit-time, Zener-Klein transit-time diode, Coulomb-drag ballistic injection) as a G1 fallback or as gain at junctions
mapping.reason: These are the only non-DS mechanisms predicted to give gain near 1 THz at 300 K. The Zener-Klein transit-time diode gives negative conductance at 0.63-2.11 THz (Gm ~ -0.1). Koseki 2016's combined DS + transit-time growth exceeds 4e12 s^-1 (already in the record). All are theory except the 9% room-temperature amplification, whose mechanism is disputed. A transit-time contribution could arise in Fable's ungated junction sliver (Part I §9.4), which belongs to the unrun Boltzmann-Maxwell tier.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Any experimental demonstration (none found as of 2026-11-03). For the Zener-Klein diode: an ungated or low-permittivity i-region of 0.3-1 um (kappa_eff <~ 1.2-6.2), which conflicts with the Au-gated 10-nm-hBN cell; growth exceeding damping in the BM-tier model of the junction.
mapping.quantified_effect: None on a Fable number yet. Predicted: 0.63-2.11 THz resonances at 300 K; growth >4e12 s^-1 (simulation).

mapping.fable_problem: Compatibility with the 69-GHz (14.5-ps) slot at 300 K
mapping.reason: Pulsed optical gain lasts ps and would fit a 14.5-ps slot, but its room-temperature band starts at >=1.6-2 THz, and pumping every slot costs +2.0-6.3 pJ/MAC (average intensity 5.5e4-1.7e5 W/cm^2). CW current injection is fast enough but needs <=100-150 K. CW optical NDC (theory) starts at >=2 THz and costs +2.6 pJ/MAC. Near-IR inversion (130-200 fs) is the wrong frequency.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A 1-THz gain window at 300 K, excluded by the ceiling above unless tau >= 7 ps.
mapping.quantified_effect: None compatible at 1 THz and 300 K.

mapping.fable_problem: Launch coupling, readout and I/O (UTC-PD -> stripline -> acoustic mode; photoconductive or electrical readout)
mapping.reason: None of the gain works addresses the transducer into the gate-screened mode. Watanabe's SPP-mediated 'gain enhancement' concerns free-space TM coupling to ungated SPPs on SiO2/Si at 2-4 THz under 2.4-uJ/cm^2 pulses. The room-temperature graphene amplifier's 9% (0.37 dB) gain is too small to relax the 27.9-32.7 dB launch-quietness requirement or the launch-power budget.
mapping.what_must_be_true: n/a
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

mapping.fable_problem: Decision quanta and noise (Part II: a homodyne decision at 6.3e-9 needs >=406 quanta at 300 K vs 99-277 delivered; G3 noise figure <= 6 dB)
mapping.reason: An interband stage would be quiet: n_sp ~1.0024 at the best hole density (derived from exp((4.14 - 160.6)/25.85)), the same ~3-dB class as the DS cell. But it cannot reach transparency at 1 THz, so it cannot add quanta. Spontaneous plasmon emission also drains any inversion in 18-34 fs (Page 2015; mid-IR scale).
mapping.what_must_be_true: Net interband gain at 1 THz (tau >= 5.8-8.3 ps at 300-353 K).
mapping.quantified_effect: None; the delivered 99-277 quanta are unchanged.

items.item: How the review uses the topic papers
items.value: Vakil & Engheta [74] is cited only for the Kubo conductivity map (its Fig. 5A,B). Fei 2015 [90] and Forati 2013 [91] appear only inside the range [86–94]. Nikitin 2011 [182] appears only inside the photodetector range [181–186]. Ke/Huang/Liu/Wang [139]–[145] are described together with Qin [137] as 'supermode' simulations. Christensen 2012 (ACS Nano 6, 431) is not among the 198 references.
items.source_title: Cui, Wang, Sun, 'Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics', Rev. Phys. 6, 100054 (user-supplied PDF text; Crossref reference list)
items.note: Checked 2026-11-03 against the Crossref record (198 refs) and a grep of the PDF reference list. The review gives no device numbers for any of these works.

items.item: Vakil & Engheta: regime
items.value: Simulation (CST) of free-standing graphene at 30 THz (λ0 = 10 µm), T = 3 K, Γ = 0.43 meV. Conductivity patterns are made by split gates, an uneven ground plane or inhomogeneous spacer permittivity.
items.source_title: Vakil & Engheta, One-atom-thick IR metamaterials and transformation optics using graphene (arXiv 1101.3585; Science 332, 1291)
items.note: Mid-IR, cryogenic, ungated (unscreened) mode.

items.item: Vakil & Engheta: guided SPP figures
items.value: λ_SPP = 144.22 nm (λ0/69.34); propagation length 2.25 µm = 15.6 λ_SPP; Re β/Im β = 97.7
items.source_title: Vakil & Engheta (arXiv 1101.3585)
items.note: Derived: 4π/97.7 × 4.343 = 0.56 dB per λ_SPP. Fable's mode loses 27.3/Q = 4.33 dB per λp at Q 6.3.

items.item: Vakil & Engheta: gate-defined components
items.value: Guide at μc = 0.15 eV next to cladding at μc = 0.065 eV with Im σ < 0 (σ2 = 0.0039 − i0.0324 mS) gives near-total reflection at an 'invisible' boundary. Also shown: an edge wave with λ ≈ 61.5 nm; 200-nm and 30-nm ribbon guides, a bend and a splitter (field maps only); a flat Luneburg lens 1.5 µm across (0.15 λ0).
items.source_title: Vakil & Engheta (arXiv 1101.3585)
items.note: Bend, splitter and junction insertion loss in dB: not found (no numbers given). Modulation speed: not addressed.

items.item: Vakil–Engheta confinement mechanism at Fable's operating point
items.value: Not available at 1 THz and 300 K: graphene is inductive (σ'' > 0) everywhere, including at the charge-neutrality point (CNP)
items.source_title: Derived, using Forati & Hanson J. Opt. 15, 114006 temperature data
items.note: ħω = 4.14 meV, while the thermal intraband weight at the CNP is 2kT ln2 = 35.8 meV, so intraband conduction dominates. Even at 45 THz Forati & Hanson's numbers flip from net Im σ = −41 + 62 = +21 µS at 3 K (no TM SPP) to −42 + 39 = −3 µS at 300 K (TM SPP supported).

items.item: Forati & Hanson APL: soft-boundary (gate-defined) ribbon
items.value: Simulation (EFIE) of a ridged ground plane at 25–75 THz, T = 3 K, Γ = 1e13 1/s. Ridge W = 25 nm, a = 25 nm, b = 1 µm, V0 = 20 V, channel μc ≈ 0.239 eV. No cutoff: W_eff/W = 21.13, 8.97, 5.4, 3.3 at 25, 40, 55, 75 THz. Edge modes are slower and lower-loss. A voltage-controlled switch and demultiplexer are proposed.
items.source_title: Forati & Hanson, Appl. Phys. Lett. 103, 133104 (arXiv 1306.3143)
items.note: Switch speed and modulation depth: not found. Note that confinement weakens as frequency falls.

items.item: Forati & Hanson J. Opt.: loss of a soft versus hard boundary
items.value: At 30 THz: β/k0 = 43.8 − j12.3 for the soft boundary versus 60.7 − j2.8 for a hard-edged 50-nm ribbon with the same channel conductivity. The authors attribute the extra loss to current flowing in the lower-conductivity boundary.
items.source_title: Forati & Hanson, J. Opt. 15, 114006 (arXiv 1306.3138)
items.note: Derived: power loss per wavelength = 4π·Im/Re × 4.343 = 15.3 dB (soft) vs 2.5 dB (hard), a factor 6.1. Simulation, mid-IR, 3 K.

items.item: Nikitin et al.: THz micro-ribbons
items.value: Simulation (COMSOL) of 5- and 20-µm ribbons at 1–12 THz, T = 300 K, μ = 0.2 eV, E_τ = 0.1 meV (τ ≈ 41 ps, 1.87e6 cm²/Vs). The fundamental mode is the even hybridized edge mode with propagation length L ≈ 10 GSP wavelengths. A second mode appears above 3.8 THz (5 µm) or 1.8 THz (20 µm).
items.source_title: Nikitin, Guinea, García-Vidal, Martín-Moreno, Phys. Rev. B 84, 161407(R) (arXiv 1107.5787)
items.note: Ungated mode; τ is about 40× Fable's 1 ps. The authors state that results for gate-defined ribbons are unchanged only if the graphene outside the ribbon supports no plasmons, which CNP graphene at 300 K does.

items.item: Christensen et al. 2012: nanoribbon waveguiding
items.value: Abstract only: plasmon propagation on individual and paired ribbons, hybridization, and a universal scaling law. Frequency band, propagation length and loss: not found.
items.source_title: Christensen et al., ACS Nano 6, 431 (abstract via OpenAlex)
items.note: Paywalled and not on arXiv. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Fei et al. 2015: measured ribbon plasmons
items.value: s-SNOM measurement at 850–1450 cm⁻¹ (25.5–43.5 THz) on etched CVD-graphene ribbons 155–480 nm wide on Al2O3, E_F ≈ 2700 cm⁻¹. Damping γp = Im q/Re q ≈ 0.12 above 1100 cm⁻¹ (CW), > 0.2 below 1000 cm⁻¹, > 0.4 near the 830 cm⁻¹ phonon.
items.source_title: Fei et al., Edge and surface plasmons in graphene nanoribbons, Nano Lett. 15, 8271 (arXiv 1512.06910)
items.note: Measured, mid-IR, ambient. Derived: γp 0.12 → 4π·0.12·4.343 = 6.5 dB per λp.

items.item: Fei et al. 2015: edge plasmons
items.value: λ_ep = 0.906 λp (theory) versus 0.81–0.82 measured at 1065–1160 cm⁻¹. Lithographic edge defects reflect and localize edge plasmons. Zero-field edge plasmons are not expected to propagate much farther than sheet plasmons.
items.source_title: Fei et al. 2015 (arXiv 1512.06910)
items.note: This is the cost side of etched (hard-edged) rows.

items.item: Zhu et al. 2013: bends
items.value: Free-standing ribbons 20–30 nm wide, E_F = 0.3 eV, τ ≈ 0.3 ps, λ0 = 10–100 µm. A sharp 90° bend transmits > 99 % for λ0 > 14 µm (30 nm) or > 12 µm (20 nm).
items.source_title: Zhu, Yan, Mortensen, Xiao, Bends and splitters in graphene nanoribbon waveguides, Opt. Express 21, 3486 (arXiv 1212.4259)
items.note: Simulation, mid/far-IR, etched ribbons. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Zhu et al. 2013: T-splitter
items.value: Equal-width T: 42 % per branch (84 % total); transmission-line theory predicts 88.9 %. Reflection is near zero when d_in/d_out = 2.25 (λ0 = 12 µm).
items.source_title: Zhu et al., Opt. Express 21, 3486 (arXiv 1212.4259)
items.note: Derived: 84 % → −0.76 dB excess loss; transmission-line |r|² = 1/9 → −0.51 dB excess.

items.item: He et al. 2013: nano-ribbon guides
items.value: 30 THz, T = 3 K, ribbons 20–40 nm. λ_spp = 21.4 nm, propagation length 338 nm, figure of merit up to 145 with a SiO2 buffer on Si.
items.source_title: He, Zhang, He, Opt. Express 21, 30664 (arXiv 1305.6500)
items.note: Simulation, mid-IR. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Zheng et al. 2015: MMI 3-dB splitter
items.value: Footprint 0.56 × 1.2 µm (0.014 λ²), tunable over 7–9 µm with E_F 0.5–1 eV, τ ≈ 0.5 ps, 300 K. Per-port transmittance is given only in a figure (not found in text).
items.source_title: Zheng, Gao, Dong (arXiv 1507.05238)
items.note: Simulation, mid-IR.

items.item: Lu et al. 2024: self-imaging 1×2 splitter
items.value: 3-µm-wide graphene MMI at E_F = 0.5 eV: transmission efficiency η rises from 5 % to 40 % as λ goes from 7 to 12 µm
items.source_title: Lu et al., Nanomaterials 14, 1538 (PMC11435397)
items.note: Simulation, mid-IR. Passive MMI splitters lose most of the power.

items.item: Ke et al. 2015 (review ref 139)
items.value: Cross-shaped graphene array absorber in the far-IR/THz; simulation. Absorption and loss values: not found.
items.source_title: Ke et al., Opt. Express 23, 8888 (abstract via OpenAlex/PubMed 25968726)
items.note: Optica full text showed a 'please wait' interstitial and was not bypassed. Localized absorber, not a waveguide component.

items.item: Ke et al. 2016 (review ref 140)
items.value: Exceptional points in a pair of graphene sheets with different losses; λ0 = 10 µm, μ1 = 0.15 eV, τ1 = 0.5 ps, τ2 = 1 ps; simulation. No insertion-loss or speed numbers.
items.source_title: Ke et al., J. Lightwave Technol. 34, 5258 (arXiv 1608.00204)
items.note: Mid-IR, vertically stacked sheets.

items.item: Ke et al. 2017 (review ref 141)
items.value: Topological edge modes in non-Hermitian graphene-pair arrays with alternating gain and loss; lateral width ~λ/70; simulation. Wavelength and loss: not found.
items.source_title: Ke et al., Opt. Express 25, 11132 (abstract; PubMed 28788795)
items.note: Assumes a gain medium. Full text behind the Optica interstitial.

items.item: Huang et al. 2017 (review ref 142)
items.value: Rippled-graphene absorber with absorption > 50 %; simulation. Wavelength: not found.
items.source_title: Huang et al., J. Lightwave Technol. 35, 320 (abstract via OpenAlex)
items.note: Absorber, not relevant to Fable.

items.item: Liu Q. et al. 2017 (review ref 143)
items.value: Exceptional points in a Fano-resonant graphene multilayer metamaterial; unidirectional invisibility; simulation. Numbers: not found.
items.source_title: Liu et al., Opt. Express 25, 7203 (abstract)
items.note: Free-space metamaterial.

items.item: Liu W. et al. 2016 (review ref 144): THz tapers
items.value: Nanofocusing in tapered graphene multilayers: field amplitude enhanced 620× at λ = 50 µm (6 THz); group velocity ≈ c/2815; simulation
items.source_title: Liu et al., Opt. Express 24, 14765 (abstract)
items.note: This is a field enhancement, not a power-transfer efficiency; efficiency not found. Ungated multilayers at 6 THz.

items.item: Wang F. et al. 2015 (review ref 145)
items.value: Bloch-mode (Rabi) conversion in graphene-pair arrays by periodic permittivity modulation; simulation. Numbers: not found.
items.source_title: Wang et al., Opt. Express 23, 31136 (abstract)
items.note: Mode converter in stacked sheets.

items.item: Qin et al. 2014 (review ref 137): multilayer supermodes
items.value: The lowest-loss supermode's loss falls with layer number and saturates at about 5 layers; simulation
items.source_title: Qin et al., Opt. Express 22, 25324 (abstract)
items.note: The prior session (R3) showed loss per wavelength stays set by Q = ωτ and heat scales as N².

items.item: Tu et al. 2018 (NTT): density-defined THz ribbons
items.value: Measured at room temperature by FTIR (1.3–20 THz). CVD graphene with SAM-doped 1.7-µm ribbons at 8-µm period plus a Si back gate. Modes at 2.8 and 4.3 THz. Plasmons stay in one ribbon array when the other is set near the CNP. Transmissivity across the boundaries is finite (reflectivity < 1).
items.source_title: Tu et al., Plasmon confinement by carrier density modulation in graphene, Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 57, 110307 (arXiv 1812.01266)
items.note: Measured, THz, 300 K, unscreened mode. Not in the review or the Fable record.

items.item: Tu et al. 2020 (NTT): gate-defined THz boundaries at room temperature
items.value: Measured at room temperature by FTIR. Patterned ZnO gate (20 nm, ~1 S/m), stripes 2 µm wide at 6-µm period, plus a Si back gate, 21-nm Al2O3, CVD graphene. Cavity peaks at 2.3 THz (4-µm regions, with the ZnO region at the CNP) and 4.7 THz (2-µm regions). The reflection measure A_r peaks at 0.54 with the ZnO region at the CNP; the authors attribute the non-perfect reflection 'mostly' to finite temperature.
items.source_title: Tu, Yoshioka, Sasaki, Takamura, Muraki, Kumada, Active spatial control of terahertz plasmons in graphene, Commun. Mater. 1, 7 (arXiv 1911.08672)
items.note: Numbers are from the arXiv v1 preprint. The same work's simulation needs gate conductivity < 1e3 S/m to avoid acoustic-plasmon reflections at gate boundaries. Not in the review or the Fable record.

items.item: Alonso-González et al. 2017 (Part I ref [39]): measured gate gap
items.value: Measured at room temperature, 2.52 THz (λ0 = 118.8 µm). Acoustic plasmons with λp ≈ λ0/66 over 15-nm AuPd gates separated by a 50-nm gap (42-nm hBN). No plasmon reflection was detected at the gap/pn junction (it 'essentially damps or transmits'). Plasmons were seen at the CNP (λp ≈ 650 nm at 3.11 THz), attributed to thermally excited carriers. v_g ≈ 0.014 c.
items.source_title: Alonso-González et al., Acoustic terahertz graphene plasmons revealed by photocurrent nanoscopy, Nat. Nanotechnol. 12, 31
items.note: Already cited by Part I [39], but only for lifetimes. Room temperature is taken from the paper's own text (thermally excited carriers at room temperature; finite-temperature conductivity at room temperature).

items.item: Svintsov & Alymov 2023: Fresnel laws for 2D plasmons
items.value: Exact Wiener–Hopf reflection and transmission at a 2D conductivity step for any incidence angle. For gated plasmons with qd ≪ 1 the dielectric function becomes local. Gated reflection vanishes at the angle where σ_L·q_x = σ_R·q'_x. Ungated plasmons get non-trivial reflection phases.
items.source_title: Svintsov & Alymov, Refraction laws for two-dimensional plasmons, Phys. Rev. B 108, L121410 (arXiv 2305.14266)
items.note: Theory. Justifies the local transmission-line treatment of Fable's gated junctions and lateral boundaries.

items.item: Moiseenko et al. 2026 PRL: gate-edge reflection and slot cavities
items.value: Reflection at a gate edge has phase −π/4 and |r| close to 1 at small gate–2DES separation; non-retarded r = exp(−iπ/4 − iφ_g)(1 − q_u/q_g)/(1 + q_u/q_g). A slot between gates is a cavity with L = λ/8 + nλ/2. Slot modes decay into the gated region at a rate ∝ (q_u d)^1/2. Absorption cross-section 0.1–0.3 λ0.
items.source_title: Moiseenko, Devizorova, Polischuk, Muravev, Svintsov, Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 166901 (arXiv 2511.03829)
items.note: Theory plus CST simulation.

items.item: Moiseenko & Svintsov 2026: exact gated/ungated scattering
items.value: Exact r and t for plasmons incident on a gated/ungated boundary from either side. In the non-retarded, small-separation limit radiative losses are negligible and |r_ii| → 1 as d → 0. Radiation from a gated plasmon peaks at q_u·d ≈ η''.
items.source_title: Moiseenko & Svintsov, Exact theory of plasmon reflection and transmission in partially gated 2D system (arXiv 2605.05504)
items.note: Preprint. Treats a single semi-infinite gate edge; the narrow two-edge slot (Fable's sliver) is not computed there.

items.item: Khisameeva et al. 2025: measured slot plasmons
items.value: Slot plasmons observed in an AlGaN/GaN plasmonic crystal with q_u = (N + 1/4)π/l_u; excitation requires q_u·h ≪ 1; they persist up to room temperature
items.source_title: Khisameeva et al., Discovery of slot plasma excitations in a AlGaN/GaN plasmonic crystal (arXiv 2511.03450, abstract)
items.note: Measured, THz, not graphene. Abstract only.

items.item: Moiseenko, Nikulin, Svintsov 2025: gate edge as launcher
items.value: A gate edge launches gated and ungated plasmons in both directions; both amplitudes peak when the 2DES reactance is of order Z0·λ0/d
items.source_title: Electromagnetic diffraction and bidirectional plasmon launching in partially gated 2d systems, Phys. Rev. Appl. 24, 014059 (arXiv 2505.04356)
items.note: Theory, abstract read. Relevant to launch, and to stray-mode generation at gate edges.

items.item: Zabolotnykh & Volkov 2019: strip-gated 2DES
items.value: Modes propagate along a strip gate with N nodes across it. The N = 0 'near-gate plasmon' has ω0 = sqrt(8πe²nd|q_y|/(mκL_x)) for |q_y|·L_x ≪ 1, with currents mainly outside the gate.
items.source_title: Zabolotnykh & Volkov, Phys. Rev. B 99, 165304 (arXiv 1812.10693)
items.note: Theory. For Fable q_y·L_x ≈ 2.7 µm⁻¹ × 1.74 µm = 4.7 ≫ 1, so this limit does not apply.

items.item: Mishchenko et al. 2010: plasmons guided by p–n junctions
items.value: Plasmons are guided along density-minimum lines with ω_n² = α_n (e²v/ħ)·sqrt(q|ρ'0|/e), α0 ≈ 3.39 (dispersion ∝ q^1/4)
items.source_title: Mishchenko, Shytov, Silvestrov, Phys. Rev. Lett. 104, 156806 (arXiv 1001.0011)
items.note: Hydrodynamic theory at T = 0. Low-density lines are the high-index side for plasmons.

items.item: Menabde et al. 2021: measured acoustic plasmons over gapped Au
items.value: Measured at room temperature, 1150 cm⁻¹, CVD graphene on 8/18-nm Al2O3 over Au. q_AGP = 39.06 + 2.92i (t = 18 nm); figure of merit L_p/λ_p = 2.12. Over Au nanoribbons with 30-nm gaps (period 230–270 nm) no bandgap was visible.
items.source_title: Menabde et al., Nat. Commun. 12, 938 (PMC7895983)
items.note: Mid-IR. Weakly consistent with gate gaps being weak scatterers.

items.item: Xiong et al. 2019 (review ref 191): gate-defined plasmonic crystal
items.value: Measured at T = 60 K, 904 cm⁻¹. hBN-encapsulated graphene on SiO2 pillars (period 80 nm) plus a back gate gives a complete, gate-switchable plasmonic bandgap near n ≈ 5.4–5.5e12 cm⁻². An artificial domain wall supports a 1D mode.
items.source_title: Xiong et al., Photonic crystal for graphene plasmons, Nat. Commun. 10, 4780
items.note: Cryogenic, mid-IR.

items.item: Room-temperature CNP sheet resistance of hBN/graphene/hBN
items.value: ρ at the CNP ≈ 1.05 kΩ at 290 K
items.source_title: Purdie et al., Cleaning interfaces in layered materials heterostructures, Nat. Commun. 9, 5387 (Fig. 7a)
items.note: Read from the figure. Used as R_CNP in the lateral-leak model.

items.item: Fable record: junction budget (Part I §9.4)
items.value: −1 to −3 dB per gate-defined junction. An ideal 2× density step costs < 0.1 dB. The budget is attributed to gate-gap scattering, ungated-sliver mode mismatch and radiation, owned by the unrun Boltzmann–Maxwell tier. The cascade closes through −6 dB junctions; no multi-cell cascade has been run.
items.source_title: Furui, The Fable Computer Part I (repository copy, papers/Fable-Computer-Part-I.pdf)
items.note: The CNP guards are said to 'define both the signal paths and the gain' (§6.1); the drain is terminated 'into a depleted (CNP) region' (§9.1). No lateral loss is booked.

items.item: Fable record: F = 2 requirement and headroom (Part III)
items.value: F = 2 requirement 6.515 dB = 3.01 dB split + 0.95 dB kinetic correction + per-gate loss, with no junction term. Existence headroom +0.98 dB at 71 GHz and +1.21 dB at 67 GHz. Booking A2 (split) passes below 144 K; A3 (plus a −1 dB junction) below 114 K.
items.source_title: Furui, The Fable Computer Part III (repository copy)
items.note: The 69-GHz frontier is computed at the 0-dB junction class.

items.item: Fable record: area (Part III)
items.value: 27.4 µm² charged per cell (11 lattice sites), of which 1 µm² active (3.6 % fill). Areas exclude wires, guards, clock taps and line fan-in (limitation 3).
items.source_title: Furui, The Fable Computer Part III (repository copy)

items.item: Active row width (derived)
items.value: W ≈ 1.74 µm, which exceeds λp/2 = 1.165 µm, so a hard-walled row of this width would also carry the first odd lateral mode
items.source_title: Derived from Part I (~1e-8 cm² per cell, L = 576 nm) and Part III (1 µm² active)
items.note: 1 µm² / 0.576 µm = 1.736 µm. Consistent with Part I's 12.67 µW / 7.3 µW per µm = 1.74 µm.

items.item: CNP thermal Drude weight relative to the channel (derived)
items.value: 0.305 at 300 K, 0.357 at 353 K. The gated speed in CNP guards is ≈ 0.55 s (0.60 s at 353 K), so the guards are the slow, high-index side.
items.source_title: Derived (finite-T intraband Drude weight 2kT·ln[2cosh(μ/2kT)])
items.note: 2kT ln2 = 35.8 meV versus 117.6 meV at E_F = 117 meV and 300 K. Measured support: plasmons at the CNP at room temperature (Alonso-González 2017) and partial CNP reflection blamed on finite temperature (Tu 2020).

items.item: Single gate edge for Fable's stack (derived)
items.value: q_u/q_g = 0.097–0.126 (λ_u = 18.6–23.9 µm vs λ_g = 2.33 µm), giving |r| = 0.78–0.82 (power 0.60–0.68) for a gated→ungated edge. Fundamental slot length λ_u/8 = 2.3–3.0 µm.
items.source_title: Derived with the Moiseenko et al. 2026 non-retarded formula
items.note: Ungated q_u = 2ε̄ε0ω²/D with D = e²E_F/(πħ²) and ε̄ = 5.2–6.7 (sapphire 9.4 below; top 1–4); q_g = 2π/2.33 µm = 2.70e6 m⁻¹; q_u·d = 0.0026–0.0034.

items.item: Ungated-sliver mismatch bound (derived)
items.value: |r| ≤ q_g·g/2, giving −0.003, −0.020, −0.080 and −0.33 dB for slivers g = 20, 50, 100 and 200 nm
items.source_title: Derived local transmission-line bound (sliver as missing gate capacitance), consistent with Svintsov & Alymov's local gated limit
items.note: For a missing shunt jωC'g: r ≈ jωC'g/(2Y0) = j·q_g·g/2, with q_g = 2.697 µm⁻¹. Fringing makes this an upper bound. Assumes ideal, AC-common (grounded) gates and no depletion of the sliver. Measured RT support: no reflection seen at a 50-nm gap (Alonso-González 2017).

items.item: Slot resonance for Fable slivers (derived)
items.value: First slot resonance ≈ 5–8 THz for g = 100–50 nm, far above the 1-THz carrier, so the sliver is non-resonant
items.source_title: Derived from L = λ_u/8 (Moiseenko et al. 2026) with the ungated ω ∝ √q dispersion
items.note: f/1 THz = sqrt((π/4g)/q_u(1 THz)) = 7.7 (50 nm) and 5.5 (100 nm) at ε̄ = 5.2; 6.8 and 4.8 at ε̄ = 6.7. Here q·d ≈ 0.16, so validity is marginal.

items.item: Radiation per gate edge (derived)
items.value: ≈ 0.16 % of the power (≈ −0.007 dB) per edge
items.source_title: Derived from the Moiseenko et al. 2026 radiative factor ε_u,rad ≈ 1 − η''²/4
items.note: η'' = σ''Z0/2 = 0.415; with the substrate replacement η/ε̄ = 0.0798, η''²/4 = 0.0016.

items.item: Ideal 2× density step (derived)
items.value: |r|² = 0.0073, i.e. −0.032 dB, consistent with the record's '< 0.1 dB'
items.source_title: Derived from the local gated Fresnel law r = (√σ1 − √σ2)/(√σ1 + √σ2) (Svintsov & Alymov 2023, qd ≪ 1)
items.note: σ ∝ E_F ∝ √n.

items.item: Doped→CNP step at 300 K (derived)
items.value: |r| = 0.289 lossless (power 0.083). With CNP loss, |r| = 0.35, 0.39, 0.48 and 0.64 for R_CNP = 0.5, 1.05, 2 and 5.2 kΩ. At 353 K (lossless) |r| = 0.25.
items.source_title: Derived (local gated transmission line; characteristic impedances sqrt(Z_s/jωC) including quantum capacitance)
items.note: Bears on the CNP guards (§6.1) and on the CNP-terminated DS drain (§9.1): such a boundary is far from an AC open.

items.item: Lateral leak of an active row into contiguous CNP guards (derived)
items.value: 8.5–8.8 dB per λp versus 4.30 dB for a hard edge, i.e. +2.1 to +2.3 dB per λp/2 gate, for R_CNP = 0.5–2 kΩ (Q 6.3, W = 1.74 µm, 300 K)
items.source_title: Derived: exact transverse eigen-solution of the local gated telegrapher equations (doped strip with semi-infinite gated CNP sheets on both sides)
items.note: CNP sheet impedance Z_s = R_CNP + jω/D_CNP with D_CNP thermal; C reduced by the CNP quantum capacitance; β/q = 0.995 − 0.160j versus about 1 − 0.079j for a hard edge. Guard field decays 1/e over 0.67 µm with a lateral wavelength of 1.63 µm (leaky anti-guide). Not modelled in the record. Qualitatively matches Forati & Hanson's ×6 soft-boundary loss.

items.item: Lateral-leak sensitivity (derived)
items.source_title: Derived (same solver)
items.note: High-quality RT graphene sits near 1 kΩ at the CNP (Purdie 2018), so the leak stays near +2.2 dB per gate.

items.item: Lateral leak expressed as an effective lifetime (derived, heuristic)
items.value: Per-gate loss 2.17 → 4.41 dB, i.e. Q_eff ≈ 3.1 and τ_eff ≈ 0.49 ps; Part I Eq.(3) then gives M_th ≈ 0.25 instead of 0.125
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Eq.(3) M_th = 1/(8f0τ) and the 13.65/Q per-gate loss
items.note: Q_eff = 13.65/4.41 = 3.10. This places the cell inside the measured RT baseline band (Q 2.5–3.8) even with τ = 1 ps material.

items.item: High-density ('bright') guards as an index guide (derived)
items.value: Guards at 2n–4n give a bound mode losing 4.65–5.06 dB per λp (+0.17 to +0.38 dB per gate); guard 1/e tail 1.06–0.75 µm; λp lengthens 8–14 %
items.source_title: Derived (same solver; guard τ = 1 ps)
items.note: Requires the guards to carry no drift current; the heat is otherwise unquantified.

items.item: Total internal reflection at a gate edge into an ungated margin (derived)
items.value: Critical angle arcsin(q_u/q_g) = 5.6–7.2° from the normal, so a mode travelling along the row is totally reflected. Stray ungated plasmons lose 0.36–0.47 dB per µm versus 1.86 dB per µm for the gated mode.
items.source_title: Derived from Svintsov & Alymov 2023 (Snell/TIR for 2D plasmons) and Moiseenko et al. 2026
items.note: Ungated: 54.6/Q dB per λ_u (19–24 µm) at Q 6.3. Gated: 4.33 dB per 2.33 µm.

items.item: Unmatched F = 2 split (derived)
items.value: An equal-width T adds 0.51 dB (transmission-line, |r|² = 1/9) to 0.76 dB (Zhu simulation) per branch. That would consume 0.51–0.76 dB of Part III's +0.98–1.21 dB F = 2 existence headroom. A 2:1 input:output width ratio removes it.
items.source_title: Derived from Zhu et al. 2013 and Part III
items.note: Fable rows are 0.75 λp wide, so the transmission-line picture is only approximate.

items.item: Wider passive fan-out instead of buffer trees (derived)
items.value: F = 3 and F = 4 need 8.30 and 9.55 dB per stage against a deliverable 7.49–7.72 dB, short by 0.58–0.81 and 1.82–2.05 dB
items.source_title: Derived from Part III (6.515 dB F = 2 requirement + 0.98–1.21 dB headroom; 0.95 dB kinetic; 2.575 dB per gate at 353 K)
items.note: 10·log10(F) + 0.95 + 13.65/5.3. A passive MMI section one λp long would add 4.33 dB at Q 6.3.

items.item: Floating gate segments (derived, rough)
items.value: Two floating λp/4 gate segments act as a series capacitance C_g·L/2 ≈ 7.7e-10 F/m per width, whose reactance is ≈ 1.26× the gated line impedance per width (1.65e-4 Ω·m). That gives |r| ≈ 0.39 (−0.7 dB) per junction plus a resonance shift.
items.source_title: Derived lumped estimate (C_g = 2.66e-3 F/m², L_k = 7.27e-11 H/sq)
items.note: Every junction theory cited assumes ideal common-potential gates. Fable's segments are DC-addressed (§9.3) and AC-tied to each cell's source (§9.1); their AC termination at 1 THz is unspecified.

mapping.fable_problem: Junction loss −1 to −3 dB per gate-defined junction (Part I §9.4): ungated-sliver mode mismatch, gate-gap scattering, radiation
mapping.reason: None of the review's waveguide papers (Vakil–Engheta, Forati–Hanson, Nikitin, Christensen, Fei, Ke/Huang/Liu/Wang) treats a gated-to-gated junction at THz. Newer primary work gives an analytic route to these terms, which the record leaves to the unrun Boltzmann–Maxwell tier: exact Wiener–Hopf gate-edge and step coefficients (Svintsov & Alymov 2023; Moiseenko et al. PRL 2026; Moiseenko & Svintsov 2026), which show radiation is negligible at q_u·d ≪ 1. The record's own ref [39] saw no reflection at a 50-nm gap between two AuPd gates at room temperature and 2.52 THz. A local transmission-line bound then makes the sliver term small. This bounds a budget item; it does not improve the 69-GHz frontier, which already uses the 0-dB junction class.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Gate segments act as perfectly conducting, AC-common (grounded) equipotentials at 1 THz; the theories assume this and the record does not specify it. The sliver keeps the cell density (no depletion). The sliver is ≲ 100 nm and far below the slot resonance (λ_u/8 = 2.3–3.0 µm). The junction is uniform across the row (no lateral mode conversion). Disorder and kinetic Knudsen-layer losses are handled separately.
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived: sliver mismatch ≤ −0.003, −0.020, −0.080 and −0.33 dB for g = 20, 50, 100 and 200 nm; radiation ≈ 0.16 % per edge. If these terms were the whole junction loss, booking A3 (−1 dB junction, passes below 114 K) would move toward A2 (below 144 K). The 69-GHz frontier and the 300-K DG1 verdict (≥ 406 quanta needed versus 99–277 delivered) do not change.

mapping.fable_problem: Ideal density step at a junction (Part I §9.4: '< 0.1 dB for a 2× step')
mapping.reason: The record's estimate is reproduced by the local (qd ≪ 1) limit of the exact gated-plasmon Fresnel law (Svintsov & Alymov 2023), r = (√σ1 − √σ2)/(√σ1 + √σ2).
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived: |r|² = 0.0073 for a 2× step, i.e. −0.032 dB, inside the record's < 0.1 dB

mapping.fable_problem: Lateral confinement of active rows by CNP guard rows (Part I §3.1, §6.1 'gate pattern defines the signal paths', §9.7 dark guard rows)
mapping.reason: The waveguide literature confines plasmons by making the cladding non-plasmonic (Vakil–Engheta's Im σ < 0) or by sharp hard boundaries (Nikitin: results hold only if the outside supports no plasmon). Forati–Hanson found gate-defined soft boundaries raise loss about 6× because current spreads into the boundary. At 1 THz and 300 K, CNP graphene is still plasmonic: the thermal Drude weight is 0.30 of the channel's, Alonso-González 2017 measured plasmons at the CNP at room temperature, and Tu 2020 measured only partial reflection at room-temperature CNP boundaries, attributed to finite temperature. For the gated mode the CNP side is the slower, higher-index side, so a doped row in a CNP background is a leaky anti-guide. The record books no lateral loss.
mapping.what_must_be_true: For the record's assumption to hold, the guards must not support a 1-THz plasmon (R_CNP well above 10 kΩ, whereas high-quality graphene at 300 K gives ≈ 1 kΩ), or the rows need hard or totally-reflecting boundaries. A 2D EM or Boltzmann–Maxwell solve of a row, or a bench comparison of etched against gate-defined rows, would confirm or refute the derived leak.
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived (local transverse eigen-solve, W = 1.74 µm, Q 6.3): +2.1 to +2.3 dB per λp/2 gate for R_CNP = 0.5–2 kΩ (+1.4 dB at 5.2 kΩ, +2.4 dB at 353 K, +3.7 dB at W = 1 µm). Per-gate loss rises from 2.17 to about 4.4 dB (Q_eff ≈ 3.1, τ_eff ≈ 0.49 ps; heuristically M_th ≈ 0.25 instead of 0.125).

mapping.fable_problem: Alternative lateral confinement for the gate-map fabric (etched rows; metal-free ungated doped margins; high-density 'bright' guards)
mapping.reason: The literature shows three ways to confine laterally: hard-edged ribbons (Nikitin 2011, Zhu 2013, Christensen 2012, Fei 2015); index contrast between two plasmon-supporting regions (Vakil–Engheta's fiber-like case; Forati–Hanson's sharp boundary); and gate edges, which reflect strongly at small gate distance (Moiseenko 2026; Zabolotnykh–Volkov strip-gate modes). Each restores a bound mode but costs programmability, DC heat or edge parasitics.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Etched rows: routing is fixed by lithography, and edge damage and lithographic edge defects (which localize edge plasmons, Fei 2015) add no loss; edge plasmons (λ_ep ≈ 0.81–0.91 λp) stay off the cell resonance. Ungated margins: they carry no drift current, and stray ungated plasmons launched at gate edges (λ_u ≈ 19–24 µm) do not cause cross-talk. Bright guards: they carry no drift current, since the thermal budget is already at its edge.
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived: a hard edge removes the +1.4 to +2.4 dB per gate leak (4.30 dB per λp). Bright guards at 2n–4n cost +0.17 to +0.38 dB per gate, with a 0.75–1.06 µm tail and λp 8–14 % longer (cells must be retuned). A gate edge into an ungated margin totally reflects beyond 5.6–7.2° (|r| = 0.78–0.82 at normal incidence).

mapping.fable_problem: Realizing the F = 2 split ('−3 dB split' in Part I §6.3/Table 5; Part III F = 2 requirement 6.515 dB, headroom +0.98–1.21 dB at 71/67 GHz)
mapping.reason: The record charges an ideal 3.01-dB split. An equal-width T of transmission-line-like guides presents a 2:1 load: Zhu et al. 2013 simulated 84 % total transmission and removed the reflection by widening the input (d_in/d_out = 2.25). This is the design rule needed to make the record's assumption true, not an improvement over it.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The transmission-line picture must hold at the split (Fable rows are 0.75 λp wide, so only approximately). The buffer cell's drain boundary must tolerate the matched branch load, and a 2W input cell must not excite higher lateral modes.
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived: an unmatched T adds 0.51–0.76 dB per branch, eating that much of the +0.98–1.21 dB F = 2 existence headroom; a 2:1 width ratio restores it

mapping.fable_problem: Activation buffer trees 256·(2L−2) cells and weight fan-out 384 cells per lane (Part III §4.2, §4.6)
mapping.reason: Passive splitters (Y/T junctions, MMI self-imaging, multiport junctions) cannot replace regenerating F = 2 nodes. The cell's deliverable gain only just covers a 2-way split, MMI sections need lengths of several plasmon wavelengths, and simulated graphene MMIs transmit 5–40 % even in the mid-IR (Lu 2024). The record's own 'only F = 2 closes' (disorder ceiling F ≤ 2.56) stands.
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived: F = 3 and F = 4 need 8.30 and 9.55 dB per stage against 7.49–7.72 dB deliverable, short by 0.58–0.81 and 1.82–2.05 dB. A 1-λp passive section costs 4.33 dB at Q 6.3. No reduction of 256·(2L−2).

mapping.fable_problem: Area per cell 27.4 µm² (1 µm² active, 3.6 % fill; Part III limitation 3)
mapping.reason: The literature's tight lateral confinement (≈ 50-nm ribbon fringes, λ/70 topological edge modes, 25–50-nm soft-boundary ribbons) is mid-IR, ungated and mostly simulated. Fable's acoustic mode is already at λ0/129, and its area is an 11-site booking rather than a layout.
