Absorbing the derived lateral leak would need guards of about 1–2 µm (1/e 0.67 µm, lateral wavelength 1.63 µm). Area is not binding: heat at 3.6 % fill is no constraint and the I/O lines are the harder number, while shrinking guards raises fill and heat.
mapping.quantified_effect: None: no defensible area reduction

mapping.fable_problem: Per-gate loss and gain margin through multilayer supermodes, PT/exceptional-point and topological arrays (review §2.6 refs [137], [139]–[145])
mapping.reason: All are mid/far-IR simulations of stacked or arrayed ungated sheets: absorbers, exceptional-point switches, gain/loss arrays, Rabi mode converters and 6-THz multilayer tapers. None treats a single gated sheet at 1 THz and 300 K. Supermode loss per wavelength is still set by Q = ωτ, and stacking raises heat as N² (prior session R3).
mapping.quantified_effect: None

mapping.fable_problem: Launch coupling by tapered-gate impedance transformers (Part I §9.5 mitigations)
mapping.reason: Liu W. et al. 2016 (review [144]) simulate 620× field enhancement in multilayer graphene tapers at 6 THz. That is a field-enhancement figure, not a power-transfer efficiency, for unscreened multilayers. The full text sits behind an Optica interstitial, which was not bypassed, and no efficiency was found. Moiseenko et al. 2025 show a gate edge launches gated and ungated plasmons (theory). This belongs to the launch topic.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A measured or computed power efficiency into the gated acoustic mode at 1 THz and 300 K
mapping.quantified_effect: Not found

mapping.fable_problem: DS current-clamped drain realized as a gate-segment boundary into a depleted CNP region (Part I §9.1)
mapping.reason: The same junction physics applies: at 300 K a doped→CNP step is far from the AC open the DS boundary assumes. A gate edge into ungated graphene reflects more (Moiseenko 2026), and an etched edge most. This lies outside the junction/tree/area targets and is flagged for the boundary-kinetics topic.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The open (j = 0) drain condition at 1 THz needs a hard edge or a much larger impedance step than a CNP region gives at 300 K; to be checked by the Boltzmann–Maxwell tier or bench gate G1
mapping.quantified_effect: Derived: doped→CNP |r| = 0.29 lossless and 0.35–0.64 with R_CNP = 0.5–5.2 kΩ (0.39 at 1.05 kΩ); gated→ungated edge |r| = 0.78–0.82

mapping.fable_problem: AC termination of the per-segment gate lattice at 1 THz (Part I §9.3 static kHz–MHz map; §9.1 gate AC-shorted to the source)
mapping.reason: Every junction and edge theory used here assumes perfectly conducting gates at a common AC potential. If segments float at THz, or are tied to each cell's own source, the gap becomes a series element in the image-current path instead of a missing capacitance, and the sliver bound no longer applies.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Each segment needs an AC return at 1 THz with impedance well below about 60 Ω (the segment capacitance is about 2.7 fF), or a model of floating segments
mapping.quantified_effect: Rough derived estimate: two floating λp/4 segments give a reactance about 1.26× the line impedance, so |r| ≈ 0.39 (−0.7 dB) per junction plus a cell-resonance shift; low confidence

mapping.fable_problem: Clock rate, energy per MAC, readout and I/O line count (Part III §4.6, limitation 12)
mapping.reason: No waveguide-component work in the review or since supplies a 1-THz, 300-K, gated-mode element that changes the 69-GHz slot, the 29–64 fJ per MAC, the readout, or the 384–704 launch lines. The switches and demultiplexers (Forati–Hanson, Ke 2016, Liu Q. 2017) are static-bias mid-IR concepts with no reported speed or modulation depth.
mapping.quantified_effect: None

items.item: Review coverage of this topic (checked against the user-supplied PDF text extract; the ScienceDirect bot check was not touched)
items.value: Cited by the review: [34] Levitov–Falkovich; [38] Low & Avouris ACS Nano 8, 1086 (a review, not a bilayer paper); [93] Poumirol 2013; [96] Jiang 2016; [97] Low/Chen/Basov 2018; [98] Hasdeo–Song 2017; [99]–[110] double-layer/BLG theory; [122]–[125] twisted bilayer incl. [123] Hu 2017; [127]–[137], [144] trilayer/multilayer; [180] Yan 2012 stacks; [187] Yan 2012 magnetoplasmons; [189]/[190] topological plasmons; [195] Polini 2016. NOT cited: Stauber–Low–Gómez-Santos 2018, Bandurin 2016, Crossno 2016, Fei 2015 bilayer (the review's Fei 2015 is [90], the nanoribbon edge-plasmon paper), Fizeau 2021 (published after the review)
items.source_title: L. Cui, J. Wang, M. Sun, 'Graphene plasmon for optoelectronics', Rev. Phys. 6, 100054 (2021); reference list read from the local text extract
items.note: The task text mislabels five items. (1) 'Polini & Geim Science 351, 229': that page is Polini's single-author perspective on a THz QCL. The hydrodynamics piece is Polini & Geim, Physics Today 73(6) 28 (2020). (2) 'Low 2014 ACS Nano bilayer' is the Low & Avouris review. (3) Hu 2017 is listed as chiral, but its plasmons are reciprocal. (4) 'M_th = L/(2sτ) rises with s' is wrong (see the DS item). (5) 'Physics World' should read Physics Today.

items.item: Fizeau drag: largest plasmon-wavelength difference, co-drift vs counter-drift (Zhao et al.)
items.value: 3.6 % between +4 mA and −4 mA (±0.8 mA/µm); 2.2 % at ±3 mA, where the drift velocity changes by 1.04e5 m/s (≈2.4 % of v_p)
items.source_title: W. Zhao et al., 'Efficient Fizeau drag from Dirac electrons in monolayer graphene', Nature 594, 517 (2021); arXiv:2106.02021
items.note: Cryogenic: 25 K base temperature. Mid-IR: 10.6 µm laser, f = 28.3 THz. |n| = 7.2e12 cm^-2. Channel is 5 µm wide, hBN-encapsulated with ~2 nm top hBN, on SiO2/Si with no metal gate over it, so this is the unscreened mode, not Fable's 1-THz gated acoustic mode at 300 K. Derived: v_p = 1.04e5/0.024 ≈ 4.3e6 m/s, giving λp ≈ 150 nm.

items.item: Fizeau shift for plasmons running against the current (Dong et al.)
items.value: −2.5 % at J = 0.7 mA/µm against the current; the co-propagating shift is vanishingly small
items.source_title: Y. Dong et al., 'Fizeau drag in graphene plasmonics', Nature 594, 513 (2021); arXiv:2103.10831
items.note: Cryogenic: T = 170 K (same trends at 60 K). Mid-IR: ω = 890 cm^-1 = 26.7 THz. n = 2.9e12 cm^-2, 2-µm channel, currents up to ±0.8 mA/µm. Derived drift velocity at 0.7 mA/µm: u = J/(ne) = 700 A/m ÷ (1.602e-19 C × 2.9e16 m^-2) = 1.5e5 m/s ≈ 0.15 v_F. Already cited in Part I as ref [24]; Zhao is [25].

items.item: Drag coefficient η in Δλ/λ = η·u/v_g − …
items.value: Theory: η = 1/4 in the collisionless limit (Γee < ω), 1/2 in the hydrodynamic limit; a Galilean 2DEG gives η = 1. The 26.7-THz data agree with η = 1/4.
items.source_title: Dong et al. 2021 (arXiv:2103.10831), Eq. (1) and Fig. 3
items.note: The authors write that 'Galilean invariance is broken in graphene'. Part I §5 already drops the Galilean law: drag is ½ in energy-conserving Dirac hydrodynamics and 0.35–0.69 in its kinetic and isothermal closures. The record's upper value 0.69 is above Dong's T→0 bound of ½; it is a finite-temperature in-model figure that no measurement supports or contradicts. No measurement of η at 1 THz / 300 K was found.

items.item: Current-driven asymmetric (Cherenkov-phonon) plasmon damping
items.value: The plasmon Q drops more for counter-propagating plasmons at current densities above ~1e3 A/m (~1 mA/µm); the paper gives no percentage
items.source_title: Y. Dong et al., 'Current-driven nonequilibrium electrodynamics in graphene revealed by nano-infrared imaging', Nat. Commun. 16, 3861 (2025), Europe PMC full text
items.note: 170 K, 890 cm^-1 (mid-IR), carrier densities 2.3–4.4e12 cm^-2. Mechanism: Cherenkov emission of acoustic phonons once v_d exceeds the phonon speed (~1e4 m/s). Already Part I ref [44] (§2).

items.item: Fable operating current density (DERIVED)
items.value: 0.33 mA/µm at the Galilean tracked bias; 0.57 mA/µm if the bias tracks the ×1.74 Dirac-drift-law threshold
items.source_title: Derived from Part I v6.1 §5 / Table 3 (n = 1e12 cm^-2, M/M_th = 0.7, M_th(300 K) = 0.125, s = 2.33e6 m/s)
items.note: J = n·e·v0 = 1.602e-3 C/m² × 2.04e5 m/s = 327 A/m; × 1.74 gives 568 A/m. Part I quotes 0.43–0.50 mA/µm at 353 K. This is 1/3–1/2 of the ~1 mA/µm at which Dong 2025 saw asymmetric damping (170 K, mid-IR).

items.item: Per-cell drift routing contrast after correcting for graphene's drag coefficient (DERIVED)
items.value: ≈0.065 dB (η = 1/4, Galilean bias); 0.09–0.18 dB (the record's η band 0.35–0.69); ≈0.23 dB (η = 1/2 with the bias raised ×1.74)
items.unit: dB per cell transit at 300 K
items.source_title: Derived from Part I §6.1 Eq. (6) (≈0.26 dB per cell at 300 K on the Galilean law) and Dong 2021's η
items.note: To first order Δκ ∝ η·v0, so 0.26 × 0.25 = 0.065, 0.26 × (0.35–0.69) = 0.09–0.18, and 0.26 × 0.5 × 1.74 = 0.23. Assumes the temporal damping 1/(2τ) does not depend on direction (Dong 2025 suggests otherwise at ≥1 mA/µm, 170 K). Every case is far below an isolator-class ~20 dB.

items.item: Expected Fizeau-type phase-velocity asymmetry in the Fable cell (DERIVED)
items.value: Δλ/λ ≈ η·v0/s = 2.2 % (η = 1/4) to 4.4 % (η = 1/2) at v0/s = 0.0875; the Galilean law would give 8.75 %
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Table 3 and the Dong 2021 first-order term
items.note: Assumes v_g ≈ s for the linear gated mode. Not measured.

items.item: Magnetically biased graphene THz isolator at room temperature
items.value: ≈20 dB isolation (18.5–18.8 dB at its two working points) with 7.5 dB insertion loss at 2.9 THz; the direction reverses near 7.5 THz
items.source_title: M. Tamagnone et al., 'Near optimal graphene terahertz non-reciprocal isolator', Nat. Commun. 7, 11216 (2016), Europe PMC full text
items.note: B = 7 T, measured at 290 K. A free-space reflection device: 3 CVD monolayers separated by ~60 nm PMMA on a back-metallized 9.15-µm Si Fabry–Perot layer. Fitted E_F = 0.53 eV, τ = 35 fs. Not on-chip and not plasmon-guided. The PMC page showed a reCAPTCHA; it was not bypassed, and the Europe PMC REST full text was used instead.

items.item: Cyclotron scale for Fable's carriers (DERIVED)
items.value: f_c = 1.36 THz per tesla. ω_c equals ω at 1 THz for B = 0.735 T. ω_c·τ = 1 at B = 0.117 T (τ = 1 ps). The Hall angle reaches tan θ = 6.3 at 0.735 T.
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Table 3 (E_F = 117 meV, τ = 1 ps)
items.note: m* = E_F/v_F² = 1.874e-32 kg (0.0206 m_e), so ω_c = eB/m* = 8.55e12·B rad/s. Tamagnone's carriers reach only ω_cτ ≈ 0.46 at 7 T (m* = 0.093 m_e, τ = 35 fs). At these fields the DS drift becomes Hall flow and the bulk mode is pushed toward ω_c; no DS-cell analysis in a field was found.

items.item: Dirac THz magnetoplasmons in graphene disks
items.value: Fields up to 17.5 T; T = 4.5 K; 3-µm disks (4.5-µm lattice) on SiO2/Si. Dipole plasmon ≈130 cm^-1 (≈3.9 THz). Edge (ω−) mode lifetime rises from 79 fs to 132 fs at 17.5 T; bulk (ω+) mode 47 fs.
items.source_title: H. Yan et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3766 (2012); arXiv:1204.4398
items.note: E_F = −0.54 eV; fitted ω0 = 134 cm^-1, m_c = 0.096 m0, Γ = 76 cm^-1. Predicted edge lifetime 250 fs at E_F = −0.34 eV. Cryogenic, 17.5 T, localized (non-propagating) modes. Review ref [187].

items.item: Magnetoplasmons (upper-hybrid mode) in quasi-neutral epitaxial graphene nanoribbon arrays
items.value: T = 4.2 K; 50–200-nm ribbons. Upper-hybrid mode at 300–610 cm^-1 (≈9.0–18.3 THz) for 100-nm ribbons; visible down to 0.2 T for 200-nm ribbons; 4 T is quoted. Maximum field: not found in the accessible text.
items.source_title: J.-M. Poumirol et al., PRL 110, 246803 (2013); arXiv:1305.4823
items.note: C-face multilayer epitaxial graphene whose top layers stay quasi-neutral (E_F ≤ 17 meV, μ ≫ 50,000 cm²/Vs, v_F = 1.02e6 m/s). This also shows that the far layers of a decoupled stack do not dope like the near ones. Review ref [93].

items.item: Chiral edge magnetoplasmons detected electrically with time resolution
items.value: 1.5 K; |B| up to ≈11–12 T. EMP velocity tunable over ≈1e4–2.5e6 m/s by field and gate screening. Propagation over 1.1 mm; time of flight ~1 ns ungated, ~10 ns gated. The sign of B sets the chirality.
items.source_title: N. Kumada et al., 'Plasmon transport in graphene investigated by time-resolved electrical measurements', Nat. Commun. 4, 1363 (2013); arXiv:1204.5034
items.note: Epitaxial graphene on SiC, cryogenic, quantizing field. Low & Avouris 2014 cite a ~50 ps EMP lifetime at ν = 2, about 10³ times the Drude time.

items.item: Chiral response of twisted bilayer graphene (theory)
items.value: The chirality is reciprocal (no time-reversal breaking). Twist angles 3° and 6°; THz and ω→0 limit. Longitudinal plasmons carry a longitudinal magnetic moment.
items.source_title: T. Stauber, T. Low, G. Gómez-Santos, PRL 120, 046801 (2018), CHORUS accepted manuscript
items.note: The response 'complies with reciprocity for time reversal'. Optical activity without time-reversal breaking cannot provide Miller input–output isolation. Not cited by the review.

items.item: Chiral plasmons observed in twisted bilayer graphene (newer work)
items.value: Chiral plasmons arise from uncompensated Berry flux under optical pumping; a slow plasmon near 0.4 eV
items.source_title: T. Huang et al., 'Observation of chiral and slow plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene', Nature 605, 63 (2022)
items.note: Taken only from search-result abstract summaries; OpenAlex has no abstract and the full text was not accessed. Mid-IR and optically pumped. Temperature not found.

items.item: Chiral Berry plasmons without magnetic field (theory)
items.value: Predicted counter-propagation splittings up to 'tens of THz' in gapped Dirac systems; needs anomalous-Hall metals or optically pumped (valley-polarized) materials; the modes sit at boundaries
items.source_title: J. C. W. Song, M. S. Rudner, PNAS 113, 4658 (2016)
items.note: Fable's graphene is gapless and unpolarized, so this offers no passive 300 K route.

items.item: Current-driven plasmon nonreciprocity from band hybridization (theory)
items.value: Strong only for interaction strength α ≫ 1 in narrow, strongly hybridized (moiré) bands
items.source_title: M. Papaj, C. Lewandowski, PRL 125, 066801 (2020); arXiv:2008.02804
items.note: No room-temperature or 1-THz case is given.

items.item: Proposed drift-current graphene THz isolator
items.value: >20 dB isolation, <3 dB insertion loss; the >20-dB bandwidth widens about 5× to 1.7 THz with density tuning
items.source_title: C.-R. Xu, W. Fan, Y. Tang, D. Wang, 'Electrically tunable graphene terahertz isolator assisted by nonreciprocal plasmon', Chin. Phys. Lett. 42, 014201 (2025)
items.note: The abstract says 'we propose'. Free-space reflection geometry with an air gap. Assumed drift velocity, mobility and temperature were not found. Not a measured on-chip plasmon isolator.

items.item: Magnet-free THz isolators by spatiotemporal gate modulation (theory)
items.value: Graphene parallel-plate waveguides with double-gated electrodes; the isolation figure for this letter was not found
items.source_title: D. Correas-Serrano et al., 'Nonreciprocal graphene devices and antennas based on spatiotemporal modulation', IEEE AWPL 15, 1529 (2016)
items.note: Needs a traveling-wave modulation of the gate. Not in the record. Modulation frequency and depth requirements not found.

items.item: Topological one-way edge plasmons in patterned graphene (review refs [189], [190], theory)
items.value: Need a static magnetic field (Pan et al. quote 2 T); band gaps at 'tens of THz' (Jin et al.)
items.source_title: D. Jin et al., PRL 118, 245301 (2017); D. Pan et al., Nat. Commun. 8, 1243 (2017)
items.note: Infrared, magnet-biased, theory.

items.item: Drift-induced negative Landau damping in double-layer graphene: contested
items.value: Current cannot push graphene plasmons into negative Landau damping; the square-root singularity keeps v_ph > v_F
items.source_title: D. Svintsov, V. Ryzhii, Comment, PRL 123, 219401 (2019); arXiv:1812.03764 (comment on Morgado & Silveirinha, PRL 119, 133901, 2017)
items.note: Consistent with Part I §7.5's 'Landau damping kinematically excluded'. A reply is PRL 123, 219402. Not in the record.

items.item: Drude weight vs layer number in graphene/insulator stacks
items.value: Drude weight grows ∝ N (linear fit); the scattering width stays at 50–60 cm^-1 (τ ≈ 0.1 ps)
items.source_title: H. Yan et al., 'Tunable infrared plasmonic devices using graphene/insulator stacks', Nat. Nanotechnol. 7, 330 (2012); arXiv:1202.5235
items.note: Room temperature, N2 ambient. CVD layers separated by ~20-nm polymer. Every layer chemically doped (8–9e12 cm^-2, ~2.5e13 after HNO3), not gated. Review ref [180].

items.item: Plasmon resonance-frequency scaling in stacks
items.value: Frequency ∝ n_total^1/2 by stacking (∝ N^1/2 at fixed per-layer density), against ∝ n^1/4 by doping a single layer. Single-layer disks: 114 cm^-1 (3.4 THz), width 65 cm^-1.
items.source_title: Yan et al. 2012 (arXiv:1202.5235)
items.note: Disks 4.4 µm on a 9-µm lattice. Derived resonance Q ≈ 114/65 ≈ 1.8. Five-layer devices: 97.5 % extinction below 1.2 THz, 8.2 dB notch filter, 9.5 dB polarizer at 40 cm^-1. All free-space parts with τ ≈ 0.1 ps (derived Q ≈ 0.63 at 1 THz).

items.item: Modes of N Coulomb-coupled graphene layers (theory)
items.value: One in-phase (optical) mode whose energy scales ∝ √N and weight ∝ N, plus N−1 out-of-phase (acoustic) branches with linear dispersion
items.source_title: J.-J. Zhu, S. M. Badalyan, F. M. Peeters, PRB 87, 085401 (2013)
items.note: Review ref [135]; double-layer theory also in review refs [99], [104], [106]. Derived concern: the N−1 slower modes become mode-conversion channels wherever contacts or launchers drive the layers unequally.

items.item: Multilayer supermode loss (simulation)
items.value: Loss of the lowest-loss supermode falls as N grows and levels off near 5 layers
items.source_title: C. Qin et al., 'Low-loss plasmonic supermodes in graphene multilayers', Opt. Express 22, 25324 (2014)
items.note: Review ref [137]. Derived: this is loss per length, which falls because the wavelength grows; loss per wavelength stays set by Q.

items.item: THz nanofocusing in tapered graphene multilayers (simulation)
items.value: Field amplitude ×620 at λ0 = 50 µm (6 THz); group velocity c/2815
items.source_title: W. Liu et al., Opt. Express 24, 14765 (2016)
items.note: Review ref [144]. Simulation of an unscreened taper fed from free space. It reports field enhancement, not coupling efficiency into a gated mode.

items.item: Twisted-bilayer plasmon wavelength and damping vs twist angle
items.value: Monolayer: λp 279 nm, γp 0.20. Twisted bilayer at θ ≈ 27°: 393 nm, 0.10; θ ≈ 12°: 387 nm, 0.11; θ ≈ 5°: 340 nm, 0.16; θ ≈ 3°: 278 nm, 0.28.
items.note: Ambient, mid-IR (CO2 laser 0.11 eV = 26.6 THz), CVD on SiO2, n ≈ 1.2e13 cm^-2. Derived: 393/279 = 1.41 ≈ √2, i.e. two decoupled layers sharing a fixed total density (Drude weight ×√2). The damping halving is mid-IR physics and does not carry over to 1 THz. Review ref [123]; reciprocal, despite the task listing it as chiral.

items.item: Plasmon wavelength: Bernal bilayer vs monolayer vs double layer
items.value: λp = 150 nm (Bernal bilayer), 188 nm (monolayer), 243 nm (randomly stacked double layer). Double-layer/monolayer ratio 1.3–1.4, inside the predicted 1–2.
items.source_title: Z. Fei et al., 'Tunneling plasmonics in bilayer graphene', Nano Lett. 15, 4973 (2015); arXiv:1508.07883
items.note: Ambient, mid-IR 883 cm^-1 (109 meV, 26.5 THz), exfoliated on SiO2. Fitted bilayer gaps at charge neutrality ~24 and ~100 meV give a gate-switchable plasmon-off region.

items.item: Bilayer mid-IR plasmonics (review and theory)
items.value: The bilayer Γ-phonon becomes IR-active near 0.2 eV, with ≥5× plasmonic enhancement of its extinction (Fano lineshape, transparency window)
items.source_title: T. Low, P. Avouris, ACS Nano 8, 1086 (2014), arXiv:1403.2799; T. Low et al., PRL 112, 116801 (2014), arXiv:1310.4693
items.note: Mid-IR only; no bearing at 1 THz. Low & Avouris also restate Drude weight ∝ N and frequency ∝ N^1/2 for stacks.

items.item: Population-inverted bilayer gain (theory)
items.value: Resonant optical gain near the bilayer asymmetry gap (above the optical-phonon energy) under population inversion
items.source_title: T. Low, P.-Y. Chen, D. N. Basov, PRB 98, 041403 (2018)
items.note: Mid-IR, optically pumped; review ref [97].

items.item: Domain-wall plasmons in gapped bilayer graphene (theory)
items.value: Room-temperature lifetimes up to a few ps predicted; propagation direction depends on valley; the modes exist at zero bulk density
items.source_title: E. H. Hasdeo, J. C. W. Song, Nano Lett. 17, 7252 (2017)
items.note: Frequencies extend into the mid-IR; 1-THz velocity and coupling not given. Both valleys are present, so the system is reciprocal overall. Review ref [98].

items.item: Plasmon reflection at bilayer domain walls (experiment)
items.value: Reflection depends on soliton type (tensile or shear) and on gating; the abstract gives no numbers
items.source_title: L. Jiang et al., Nat. Mater. 15, 840 (2016), PubMed abstract
items.note: Mid-IR near-field on exfoliated bilayers; review ref [96]. The Nature page redirected to a sign-in flow, which was not followed.

items.item: THz plasmons in graphite thin films (the multilayer limit)
items.value: THz plasmons in ~15–30-nm graphite films, tunable by temperature and bias, measured at 5 K and at room temperature; Q not found
items.note: A two-component semimetal (massive electrons plus Dirac holes), not decoupled graphene layers.

items.item: Electrical plasmon generation by inelastic tunneling in twisted double layers (theory)
items.value: Generation efficiency drops ~20 % at 4° twist vs aligned stacking; per-electron efficiency not found
items.source_title: S. de Vega, F. J. García de Abajo, PRB 99, 115438 (2019)
items.note: Review ref [125]. A photomixer-free launch concept, not quantified.

items.item: N decoupled layers at equal per-layer density: kinetic inductance, reactance and resistance (DERIVED)
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Table 3 plus Yan 2012 (Drude weights add)
items.note: Check: L_k = πħ²/(e²E_F) = 7.27e-11 H at E_F = 117 meV. Q = ωτ, and so the loss per λp (27.3/Q dB), does not change.

items.item: N layers at equal per-layer density: speed, wavelength and cell length (DERIVED)
items.source_title: Derived from s² = 1/(L_k·C_g) with C_g unchanged (Part I Table 3)
items.note: Quantum capacitance per layer is C_Q(1e12) = 2.75 µF/cm² against C_g(10 nm hBN) = 0.30–0.34 µF/cm². Including it trims the N = 2 speed gain by ≈2.6 % (s ≈ 0.974·√N·s1).

items.item: N layers: DS threshold and required drift (DERIVED)
items.value: M_th = 1/(8f0τ) = 0.125 at 300 K, unchanged at f0 = 1 THz. Drift needed at 0.7·M_th: v0 = 2.04e5·√N → 2.88e5, 3.53e5, 4.08e5 m/s. Total current density 0.33·N^1.5 → 0.92, 1.70, 2.61 mA/µm.
items.source_title: Derived from Part I Eq. (3) and Table 3
items.note: The task premise 'M_th = L/(2sτ) rises with s' is wrong. At fixed f0 (L ∝ s), M_th does not change. At fixed L, M_th ∝ 1/s while v0 = L/(2τ) = 2.88e5 m/s stays the same, but f0 rises ∝ √N, off the 1-THz carrier.

items.item: N layers at equal per-layer density: heat, power and energy per MAC (DERIVED)
items.value: Joule density ×N² (4, 9, 16). Per-cell power ×N^2.5 (5.66, 15.6, 32): 7.78–10.22 µW becomes 44–58 µW at N=2 and 249–327 µW at N=4. Energy per MAC at 300 K: 29–39 fJ becomes 164–221 fJ (N=2) and 928–1,248 fJ (N=4).
items.source_title: Derived from Part III §4.5 / §2.2 cell dissipation and Part I §4 Joule form (n·m*·v0²/τ per layer)
items.note: p = J²R with J ∝ N^1.5 and R ∝ 1/N; cell area ∝ L ∝ √N at fixed width. Thermal effect: Part I's 42 K rise at 1/3 fill becomes 168 K at N=2, against a 55 K budget. Part III's lane rise of 2.8–3.7 K at 3.6 % fill becomes 11–15 K (×N²) or 16–21 K (×N^2.5) at N=2, against DG5 ≤ 10 K.

items.item: N layers sharing a fixed total density of 1e12 cm^-2 (DERIVED)
items.value: Per-layer E_F = 117/√N (82.7 meV at N=2). L_k = 7.28e-11/√N (5.15e-11 H/sq at N=2: 324 Ω/sq reactance, 51.5 Ω/sq at τ = 1 ps). s ∝ N^1/4 (2.77e6 m/s, cell 685 nm at N=2). Joule density unchanged; per-cell power ×N^1/4 (×1.19, i.e. 34–46 fJ/MAC at N=2).
items.source_title: Derived; the √N Drude-weight sharing is confirmed (unscreened, mid-IR) by Hu 2017 (λ ratio 1.41) and Fei 2015 (1.3–1.4)
items.note: Lower per-layer density moves toward the disorder-limited side that Part I §4 uses to select n = 1e12.

items.item: Doping a two-layer stack from a single gate (DERIVED)
items.value: q2/q1 = C_a/(C_a + C_Q): ≈0.52 for a 1-nm hBN spacer (C_a = 3.0 µF/cm²) and ≈0.27 for a 3-nm spacer (1.0 µF/cm²), with C_Q(1e12) = 2.75 µF/cm²
items.source_title: Derived lumped electrostatics; consistent with Poumirol 2013 (quasi-neutral upper layers) and Yan 2012 (chemical doping used to dope all layers)
items.note: A single gate cannot dope a stack uniformly, so Fable's gate-written density map, including the CNP guard cells, would differ from layer to layer.

items.item: Characteristic impedance of a gated plasmon strip (DERIVED)
items.value: Z_p·W = L_k·s = 170 Ω·µm at N=1, falling ∝ N^-1/2 to 120 (N=2) and 85 (N=4) Ω·µm. At the cell width W ≈ 1.74 µm: 97.5 Ω (N=1), 69 Ω (N=2), 49 Ω (N=4). At N=1, 50 Ω needs W ≈ 3.4 µm and 100 Ω needs W ≈ 1.7 µm.
items.source_title: Derived transmission-line model Z = sqrt(L'/C') = L_k·s/W; W from Part I §8.1 (12.67 µW per cell ÷ 7.3 µW per µm = 1.74 µm = 1 µm² / 0.576 µm)
items.note: Kinetic inductance dominates. Width alone sets the scalar impedance; stacking only rescales it.

items.item: Velocity mismatch to a stripline on sapphire, and loss per length (DERIVED)
items.value: Stripline c/√ε_eff ≈ 1.32e8 m/s (ε_eff ≈ (9.4+1)/2) against s gives ratios of 56× (N=1), 40× (N=2), 28× (N=4). Loss is 4.3 dB per λp at every N; per mm it falls from 1,846 (N=1) to 1,305 (N=2) and 923 (N=4) dB/mm.
items.source_title: Derived from Part I §3.1 (sapphire ε_r ≈ 9.4) and Table 3
items.note: Quasi-TEM estimate; Kusyak's actual stripline geometry was not used. Metal THz guides lose 1–10 dB/mm (prior-session finding).

items.item: Part I record: hydrodynamic tier
items.value: τ_ee ≈ 115 fs at 300 K (83 fs at 353 K) from 1/τ_ee ≈ (k_BT)²/(ħE_F); ωτ_ee ≈ 0.7 at 1 THz; ν0 = v_F²τ_ee/4; νq² ≈ 20 % of 1/τ before the 1/(1+(ωτ_ee)²) factor; closure ν(ω) = ν0/(1 − iωτ_ee); kinetic correction −1.27 dB [−1.6, −0.5] at 300 K with the threshold ×1.16; A band 0.5–3; ℓ_ee/L ≈ 0.2
items.source_title: R. Furui, The Fable Computer Part I v6.1, §7.5 and §5 (refs [10] Barcons Ruiz 2023, [15] Lucas & Fong 2018, [19] Crabb 2021)
items.note: Hydrodynamics is already in Part I's model for the bulk. The cavity model is 1D (§10: 'the 1D gated cavity with its quasistatic Poisson kernel'). Knudsen layers at the source and drain contacts are carried as a ±1 dB allowance; lateral sidewalls are not modelled.

items.item: Electron viscosity of graphene's Fermi liquid
items.value: ν ≈ 0.1 m²/s at n ~1e12 cm^-2, for monolayer and bilayer (honey: 0.002–0.005 m²/s)
items.source_title: D. A. Bandurin et al., 'Negative local resistance caused by viscous electron backflow in graphene', Science 351, 1055 (2016); arXiv:1509.04165
items.note: Not a 300 K value: Polini & Geim (2020) place it at liquid-nitrogen temperatures, and the vicinity resistance turns positive near room temperature. Many-body calculation gives ℓee 0.1–0.3 µm at T ≥ 150 K. D_ν ≈ 0.4 µm for ν = 0.1, τ = 1.5 ps. μ > 5 m²/Vs up to room temperature. Metal gates 70–80 nm away change ℓee by <5 %.

items.item: Viscosity at 100 K, n = 1e12 cm^-2 (point-contact geometry)
items.value: ν ≈ 0.16 m²/s
items.source_title: R. Krishna Kumar et al., 'Superballistic flow of viscous electron fluid through graphene constrictions', Nat. Phys. 13, 1182 (2017); arXiv:1703.06672
items.note: ℓee = 4ν/v_F. The measured T-dependence departs from 1/T² at 50–100 K. Room-temperature mobility ~5 m²/Vs at ~1e12.

items.item: τ_ee at 300 K from measured viscosities (DERIVED)
items.value: ≈70–135 fs, giving ωτ_ee(1 THz) ≈ 0.45–0.84 and Part I's A multiplier ≈ 0.86–1.6
items.source_title: Derived from Krishna Kumar 2017 and Kim 2020
items.note: Kumar: ℓee(100 K) = 4 × 0.16/1e6 = 0.64 µm, so τ = 0.64 ps against the formula's 1.04 ps (A = 1.6); scaling as T⁻² gives 71 fs at 300 K. Kim: ℓee(200 K) ≈ 0.3 µm, so 0.30 ps against 0.259 ps (A = 0.86); T⁻² gives 133 fs. Both sit inside Part I's 0.5–3 band and bracket its 115 fs. Uses the ¼ viscosity convention (Principi, Kumar, Part I); Levitov–Falkovich write ν ≈ ½v_F²/γee, which would double A.

items.item: Gate-proximity screening of electron–electron scattering
items.value: Matters only for gate dielectrics of a few nm or less; crossover d* ≈ 1/(2q_TF) ≈ 1.1 nm (hBN ε ≈ 3.5, n ~1e12). At 200 K, ℓee ≈ 0.3 µm with a 300-nm gate vs 0.8 µm with a 1.7-nm gate.
items.source_title: M. Kim et al., 'Control of electron-electron interaction in graphene by proximity screening', Nat. Commun. 11, 2339 (2020); arXiv:1911.10128
items.note: Fable's 10-nm hBN is ≈9× d* (derived), so the gate does not screen e–e scattering and gives no τ_ee lever. The density for the 0.3/0.8 µm values is not stated in the extracted text. OpenAlex responses during this search carried a notice asking for an email-registered API key; it was ignored and no personal data was sent anywhere.

items.item: Room-temperature momentum mean free path at n = 1e12 cm^-2
items.value: ℓ ≈ 0.7–1.1 µm across device quality. Derived: τ = ℓ/v_F ≈ 0.7–1.1 ps and μ ≈ 6.0–9.4 m²/Vs.
items.source_title: Kim et al. 2020, Supplementary Fig. 1b (arXiv:1911.10128); Polini & Geim, Physics Today 73(6), 28 (2020), arXiv:1909.10615 ('longer than a micron even at room T')
items.note: Supports Part I's τ = 1 ps (86,000 cm²/Vs) as the upper end of what is demonstrated.

items.item: Electron viscosity and vortices (Levitov & Falkovich, theory)
items.value: ν ≈ ½v_F²γee⁻¹ with γee ~ (k_BT)²/E_F away from neutrality. Near charge neutrality γee⁻¹ ≈ 80 fs at 100 K (A ≈ 1); momentum relaxation ~0.5 ps there.
items.source_title: L. Levitov, G. Falkovich, Nat. Phys. 12, 672 (2016); arXiv:1508.00836
items.note: The only hydrodynamics paper the review cites ([34]). Theory of negative nonlocal resistance.

items.item: Dirac fluid and Wiedemann–Franz violation
items.value: Lorenz ratio up to 22× L0 near charge neutrality; the Dirac fluid exists between T_dis ≈ 40 K and T_el-ph ≈ 80 K; n_min 5–10e9 cm^-2
items.source_title: J. Crossno et al., Science 351, 1058 (2016); arXiv:1509.04713
items.note: Charge-neutral regime at 40–80 K. Fable's cells run at E_F/k_BT ≈ 4.5 at 300 K (Fermi liquid), so this does not apply.

items.item: Hydrodynamic plasmons and energy waves near charge neutrality
items.value: A bipolar hydrodynamic plasmon plus an energy wave; the energy-wave speed is v_F/2 in the Kavli-hosted abstract and v_F/√2 in an LBL summary (the sources disagree)
items.source_title: W. Zhao et al., Nature 614, 688 (2023) (abstract page)
items.note: On-chip THz spectroscopy of a near-neutral microribbon. Temperatures not found. Charge-neutral regime.

items.item: Science 351, 229 (2016), which the task cites as the hydrodynamics perspective
items.value: It is M. Polini, 'Tuning terahertz lasers via graphene plasmons', a perspective on Chakraborty et al., Science 351, 246 (graphene-plasmon gain modulation of a THz quantum-cascade laser)
items.source_title: Crossref records doi:10.1126/science.aad7995 and doi:10.1126/science.aad2930
items.note: Review ref [195]. It concerns gain and lasers, not hydrodynamics.

items.item: Upper bound on the bulk viscous supplement (DERIVED)
items.value: Re ν(ω)·q² ≤ v_F²q²/(8ω) = 1.45e11 s⁻¹, i.e. 14.5 % of 1/τ (τ = 1 ps, q = 2π/2.33 µm), reached at ωτee = 1
items.source_title: Derived from Part I §7.5's closure
items.note: Quantifies the record's 'bounded interior maximum at ωτ_ee = 1'.

items.item: Sidewall viscous boundary layer of the finite-width cell, not in the 1D model (DERIVED)
items.value: Stokes thickness δ = sqrt(2ν0/ω) ≈ 75–103 nm (≈ ℓee). No-slip upper bound on the extra momentum-relaxation rate: 2ν0/(δW) = sqrt(2ν0ω)/W ≈ 0.27–0.37 × 1/τ at W = 1.74 µm (ν0 = 0.018–0.033 m²/s). Zero for slip (specular) edges.
items.source_title: Derived; no-slip viscous-flow framework from Bandurin 2016 and Levitov–Falkovich 2016; cell geometry from Parts I and III
items.note: Because δ ≈ ℓee this is really a Knudsen layer, so the hydrodynamic number is only a scale. The ballistic diffuse-edge analogue is of order v_F/W = 5.7e11 s⁻¹ times an O(1) factor. Gurzhi length D_ν = sqrt(ν0τ) = 133–182 nm against W = 1.74 µm. Whether gate-defined sidewalls next to CNP guard cells reflect specularly is unknown.

items.item: Input–output isolation as a logic criterion (bibliographic record only)
items.value: Miller lists input–output isolation among the requirements for cascadable optical logic
items.source_title: D. A. B. Miller, 'Are optical transistors the logical next step?', Nat. Photonics 4, 3 (2010)
items.note: Only the bibliographic record was checked here, via Crossref.

mapping.fable_problem: Input–output isolation (Miller criterion) at 300 K without magnets
mapping.reason: Part I §2 and §6.1 (Eq. 6, refs [24]–[27]) already book the only magnet-free mechanism in this topic: drift nonreciprocity, at ≈0.26 dB per cell, with no isolator claimed. The primary works are cryogenic and mid-IR: 25 K at 28.3 THz (≤3.6 %) and 170 K at 26.7 THz (−2.5 %). They also show graphene's drag coefficient is η ≈ 1/4, not the Galilean 1 that the 0.26 dB assumes. The other routes need something Fable lacks: twisted-bilayer chirality (Stauber 2018) is reciprocal; Berry- and valley-chiral plasmons (Song–Rudner 2016; Huang 2022; Hasdeo–Song 2017) need optical pumping or valley polarization; moiré current nonreciprocity needs α ≫ 1 narrow bands.
mapping.what_must_be_true: The wave running against the drift would need an extra, direction-dependent damping comparable to the whole loss budget, shown at 1 THz and 300 K and booked against gain. Cherenkov-phonon damping (Dong 2025) has so far been seen only at ≳1 mA/µm, 170 K, mid-IR.
mapping.quantified_effect: Eq. (6) corrected for drag gives ≈0.065 dB per cell (η = 1/4, Galilean bias), 0.09–0.18 dB (the record's η band 0.35–0.69), or ≈0.23 dB (η = ½ with the bias raised ×1.74). A discrete isolator gives ~20 dB. No Fable number improves.

mapping.fable_problem: Isolation by magnetoplasmons (Faraday or edge-magnetoplasmon nonreciprocity)
mapping.reason: Graphene isolation that truly breaks time reversal has only been shown with magnets: a 290 K free-space reflection isolator at 2.9 THz (≈20 dB, 7.5 dB insertion loss) needs 7 T (Tamagnone 2016); on-chip chiral edge magnetoplasmons were seen at 1.5–4.5 K and 4–17.5 T (Kumada 2013, Yan 2012, Poumirol 2013); topological one-way plasmons need ~2 T (Pan 2017, theory). Fable's light, clean carriers need much less field (derived ω_c = ω at 0.735 T; ω_cτ = 1 at 0.117 T). But such a field also turns the DS drift into Hall flow (tan θ = 6.3 at 0.735 T) and pushes the bulk plasmon toward ω_c. The record has no magnetic-field analysis.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A redesigned isolator section or cell that keeps DS gain at ω_cτ ~1–6; a die-scale 0.1–0.7 T magnet; and a measured isolation and insertion loss on gated graphene at 1 THz and 300 K.
mapping.quantified_effect: No effect on a named Fable number until modelled. The field needed is 0.12–0.74 T (derived).

mapping.fable_problem: Routing sign at 300 K (Part I §6.1: signals co-propagate with the electron drift)
mapping.reason: The sign Part I uses (the co-drift wave is less damped and longer in wavelength) is what Dong 2021 and Zhao 2021 measured, and Part I cites both. Both measurements were at 25–170 K and 26.7–28.3 THz, on the unscreened mode in 2–5 µm channels. No 300 K, 1-THz or gated measurement was found.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A bench measurement of co- and counter-propagating phase and attenuation on the gated 1-THz cell at the operating 0.33–0.57 mA/µm.
mapping.quantified_effect: Expected phase-velocity asymmetry ≈2.2–4.4 % (η = 1/4 to 1/2 at v0/s = 0.0875) vs 8.75 % on the Galilean law (derived).

mapping.fable_problem: Launch impedance match (Part I §9.5, tapered-gate transformers): multilayer stacks
mapping.reason: Scalar impedance is not what limits the launch. A gated strip's characteristic impedance is set by its width: Z_p = 170 Ω·µm / W (derived), i.e. 97.5 Ω at the cell width of 1.74 µm and 50 Ω at 3.4 µm, all with one layer. Stacking N layers only rescales Z_p ∝ N^-1/2 (69 Ω at N=2). The measured coupling, η ≈ 0.03 at 4 K (Yoshioka 2024, already in the record), cannot be explained by scalar Z in a lumped-junction model. A single gate also dopes a stack unevenly (q2/q1 ≈ 0.27–0.52), which would make the gate-written program differ by layer.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A measured transducer whose coupling is limited by scalar impedance, which no source shows, and per-layer doping that does not rely on the single gate.
mapping.quantified_effect: None on the ~10 aJ/slot launch budget. Z_p at W = 1.74 µm: 97.5 Ω (N=1), 69 Ω (N=2), 49 Ω (N=4).

mapping.fable_problem: Launch velocity and mode-size mismatch (stripline ~1.3e8 m/s vs acoustic plasmon 2.33e6 m/s)
mapping.reason: Stacking raises s by √N at equal per-layer density (N^1/4 if the density is shared), cutting the velocity ratio from 56× to 40× (N=2) and 28× (N=4) and stretching λp to 3.3–4.7 µm (derived). No primary work measures coupling efficiency against N. The only multilayer THz coupler in the review is a simulation (Liu 2016: ×620 field at 6 THz, unscreened, fed from free space) that reports field enhancement rather than power transfer. Tunneling-based electrical launch (de Vega 2019) is theory with no efficiency given.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A measured η(N) on gated stacks at 1 THz whose gain outweighs the energy and area penalties listed below.
mapping.quantified_effect: Unknown; the only derivable change is the velocity ratio falling as 1/√N.

mapping.fable_problem: G1: single-cell per-pulse net gain ≥ +2.6 dB at ≤ 80 °C (M_th = 1/(8f0τ))
mapping.reason: At fixed f0, stacking leaves M_th and Q = ωτ unchanged, because Eq. (3) does not depend on s; M_th does not rise with s as the task assumed. The drift required grows ∝ √N (2.04e5 → 2.88e5 → 4.08e5 m/s) and the total current density ∝ N^1.5 (0.33 → 0.92 → 2.61 mA/µm). That crosses the ~1 mA/µm where current-driven asymmetric damping was seen, and Joule density rises ×N². The N−1 out-of-phase modes (Zhu 2013) and uneven layer doping add detuning and mode-conversion risk.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Nothing in this topic offers a gain lever. A stack would also need per-layer doping and a duty cycle below roughly 1/N² to stay inside the 80 °C cap.
mapping.quantified_effect: M_th stays 0.125 at 300 K. Part I's 1/3-fill temperature rise goes from 42 K to 168 K at N=2, against a 55 K budget. This is a penalty, not an improvement.

mapping.fable_problem: Energy per MAC (Part III: 29–39 fJ/MAC and 7.78–10.22 µW per cell at 300 K) and lane heating (DG5 ≤ 10 K)
mapping.reason: Stacking raises per-cell power ×N^2.5 at equal per-layer density (×N² Joule density times a √N longer cell), or ×N^1/4 when layers share a fixed total density (√N Drude-weight sharing, as Hu 2017 and Fei 2015 measured in the mid-IR).
mapping.what_must_be_true: No route to lower energy per MAC appears in this topic.
mapping.quantified_effect: At N=2: 164–221 fJ/MAC with equal per-layer density, or 34–46 fJ/MAC with shared density. The lane rises 11–21 K at 3.6 % fill, against DG5 ≤ 10 K (derived).

mapping.fable_problem: Cell area and pitch (576-nm cell; 27.4 µm² per cell with 1 µm² active; ~500-nm lithography pitch)
mapping.reason: λp and the quarter-wave cell grow ∝ √N (815 nm at N=2, 1152 nm at N=4). That is the same direction as lowering f0, which Part I §1 rejects because the cell outgrows the ~500-nm pitch.
mapping.quantified_effect: Active area grows ×√N (1.41 µm² at N=2).

mapping.fable_problem: Passive loss (27.3/Q dB per λp; 4.3 dB per λp at 300 K; ≈1,850 dB/mm)
mapping.reason: Loss per wavelength depends only on Q, which stacking does not change. Loss per mm falls ∝ 1/√N only because λp grows: 1,846 → 1,305 → 923 dB/mm (derived). That is still at least 90× worse than metal THz guides (1–10 dB/mm). Cell budgets are counted per gate (per λp). The 'low-loss supermodes' of Qin 2014 are the same per-length effect, in simulation.
mapping.quantified_effect: The per-gate loss of 2.17 dB at 300 K is unchanged.

mapping.fable_problem: Channel material: Bernal or twisted bilayer instead of monolayer (Q at 1 THz)
mapping.reason: Every bilayer plasmon dataset here is mid-IR at ambient temperature or theory. Fei 2015 (26.5 THz): Bernal bilayer is more confined (λp 150 vs 188 nm) and has a gate-gapped plasmon-off region. Hu 2017 (26.6 THz): large-angle twisted bilayer acts as two decoupled layers, with λp ×1.41 and γp halved. The rest are theory (Low 2014, Low 2018, Hasdeo–Song 2017). The mid-IR damping physics (phonons, impurities, Fermi-velocity renormalization) is absent at 1 THz, where damping equals the DC transport rate.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A 1-THz, 300-K measurement showing a longer momentum τ in a bilayer channel at the operating density.
mapping.quantified_effect: None derivable.

mapping.fable_problem: G1 kinetic/hydrodynamic correction (Part I §7.5: τee ≈ 115 fs, ωτee ≈ 0.7, −1.27 dB [−1.6, −0.5] at 300 K, A band 0.5–3)
mapping.reason: Hydrodynamics is already in Part I's model: Navier–Stokes with ν0 = v_F²τee/4 inside a Maxwell/Mermin viscoelastic closure (refs [10], [15], [19]). The measured viscosities bracket the record: Kumar 2017 (ν ≈ 0.16 m²/s at 100 K) and Kim 2020 (ℓee ≈ 0.3 µm at 200 K) give τee(300 K) ≈ 70–135 fs and A ≈ 0.86–1.6 (derived), inside the 0.5–3 band. Bandurin's ν ≈ 0.1 m²/s is a ~77–150 K value, not a 300 K one. The bulk viscous supplement is capped at 14.5 % of 1/τ for any τee (derived).
mapping.quantified_effect: G1 numbers unchanged. ωτee ≈ 0.45–0.84 vs the record's 0.7.

mapping.fable_problem: τee lever through gate proximity
mapping.reason: Kim 2020 finds that gate screening of e–e scattering needs gate distances of a few nm or less (crossover ≈1.1 nm at 1e12). Fable's 10-nm hBN is about 9× that, and Bandurin's supplement finds 70–80-nm gates change ℓee by under 5 %.
mapping.what_must_be_true: d ≲ 1–2 nm, at the tunneling floor, plus a reason to want a longer τee. The record's correction peaks at ωτee = 1, so raising τee does not help.
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

mapping.fable_problem: Sidewall boundary layers of the finite-width cell (absent from the record's 1D cavity model)
mapping.reason: The cell is ≈1.74 µm wide (derived from 12.67 µW per cell ÷ 7.3 µW/µm). That is close to the room-temperature momentum mean free path (0.7–1.1 µm, Kim 2020) and about 10× the Gurzhi length (133–182 nm). Part I books Knudsen layers only at the source and drain contacts. If the sidewalls are no-slip, the AC Stokes layer (δ ≈ 75–103 nm ≈ ℓee) adds up to 27–37 % of 1/τ. If they reflect specularly, the addition is about zero.
mapping.what_must_be_true: Gate-defined CNP-guard edges must reflect nearly specularly for this to vanish. A bench test: excess sub-threshold linewidth that scales as 1/W across a width sweep, a fourth signature alongside Part I's three linewidth discriminants.
mapping.quantified_effect: A risk, not a gain: Q 6.3 → 4.6–5.0 at worst under the no-slip upper bound (derived); 0 if specular.

mapping.fable_problem: Non-Galilean DS drift law (Part I §5: drag ½, closures 0.35–0.69, threshold ×1.67–1.74)
mapping.reason: Dong 2021's measured Fizeau drag (η ≈ 1/4 at 26.7 THz and 170 K, theory range 1/4–1/2, Galilean 1) is the experimental basis for the record's non-Galilean drift law. At 1 THz and 300 K the cell sits in the crossover (derived ωτee 0.45–0.84), so η between 1/4 and 1/2 is expected. The record's in-model upper value of 0.69 lies above Dong's T→0 bound and has no data either way.
mapping.quantified_effect: No improvement; the data support the record's caveat.

mapping.fable_problem: Current-induced Cherenkov-phonon damping (Dong 2025, record ref [44])
mapping.reason: Asymmetric extra damping of counter-propagating mid-IR plasmons appears at ≳1 mA/µm at 170 K. Fable runs at 0.33–0.57 mA/µm (derived) with v0 ≈ 2e5 m/s, far above acoustic-phonon speeds (~1e4 m/s), so the Cherenkov condition is met. Its size at 1 THz and 300 K is unknown. It would add routing contrast but also damp the backward cavity leg.
mapping.what_must_be_true: A measurement on the gated 1-THz cell. A stack at equal per-layer density would reach 0.92 mA/µm already at N=2.
mapping.quantified_effect: Unknown.

mapping.fable_problem: Drift-gain claims beyond DS (negative Landau damping in double layers; drift-biased 'active plasmonics'; population-inverted bilayer gain)
mapping.reason: All theory. The double-layer negative-Landau-damping claim is contested (Svintsov & Ryzhii 2019), consistent with Part I's own result that Landau damping is kinematically excluded. Population-inverted bilayer gain is mid-IR and optically pumped. Science 351, 229 (Polini 2016) is a THz-QCL perspective.
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

mapping.fable_problem: Charge-neutral hydrodynamics (Crossno 2016; Zhao 2023) and the CNP guard cells
mapping.reason: Fable's active cells are Fermi liquids (E_F/k_BT ≈ 4.5 at 300 K), while the Dirac-fluid Wiedemann–Franz violation (up to 22× L0) was seen at 40–80 K near charge neutrality. Only the CNP guard cells sit near neutrality, and what the design uses there is their THz absorptivity, not their viscosity. Zhao 2023's temperatures were not found.
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

mapping.fable_problem: Electrical plasmon readout (Part III #141)
mapping.reason: The only electrical, time-resolved plasmon detection in this topic (Kumada 2013: chiral edge magnetoplasmons over 1.1 mm with ns time of flight) was done at 1.5 K and up to ~12 T.
mapping.quantified_effect: None.

outline.content_summary:
AUTHORS AND DATES: L. Cui and J. Wang (equal contribution; USTB and Liaoning Shihua Univ.); M. Sun (corresponding author, USTB). Reviews in Physics 6, 100054. Received 2020-05-03, revised 2021-01-19, accepted 2021-02-06, online 2021-02-09; issue June 2021. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

STRUCTURE: 20 pages in four sections — 1.1–1.4 introduction, 2.1–2.7 graphene plasmons by structure, 3.1–3.4 applications, 4 outlook. There are 11 numbered equations and 15 figures, all reproduced from cited works. The review has no new data, no comparison table and no quantitative benchmark.

REFERENCES: 198 references from 1999–2020, none later. Derived from the Crossref reference years: 1 from 1995–99, 2 from 2000–04, 43 from 2005–09, 72 from 2010–14, 75 from 2015–19, 4 from 2020; 22 are from 2018–20. Eleven are self-citations of the Sun/J. Wang group (5.6 %, derived).

SCOPE GAPS: the abstract names five application areas. The body has sections for metamaterials, photodetectors, photonic crystals and lasers. Waveguides appear only inside §2.6, and no section covers optical information transmission. outline.section: §1.3 Electrical and optical properties of graphene (pp. 3–4)
outline.content_summary:
ELECTRICAL CONTENT [17–36]:
- Ambipolar field effect; minimum conductivity of order 4e²/h.
- Room-temperature mobility up to 2.0×10⁵ cm²/Vs at 10¹² cm⁻², described as phonon-limited and cited to Novoselov 2005 [18]; that paper concerns the cyclotron mass (Fig. 3b).
- Mean free path about 1 µm; transport approaching ballistic (Du 2008 [19]).
- Room-temperature quantum Hall effect.
- Klein tunnelling [22–24], quantum billiards [25], shot noise [27], Landau levels [28, 29], quantum Hall effect [21, 30, 31].
- Giant intrinsic mobilities (Morozov 2008 [32]); epitaxial graphene [33].
- Electron viscosity (Levitov & Falkovich 2016 [34]) — the review's only hydrodynamics reference, never discussed.
- Two self-reviews [35, 36].

OPTICAL CONTENT [37–51]:
- 2.3 % absorption, said to hold over 300–2500 nm, which the review calls UV to far-IR.
- Saturable absorption.
- Below 2E_F, Pauli blocking leaves only the intraband (Drude) response from the mid-IR to the THz.
- Graphene-oxide and graphene-quantum-dot photoluminescence [40–50], unrelated to plasmons.
- Self-review [51].

PRIMARY CHECKS:
- The 2×10⁵ figure is from Chen et al. 2008, which the review does not cite. That paper gives the acoustic-phonon-limited mobility at 10¹², a mean free path above 2 µm, about 30 Ω intrinsic resistivity, and a room-temperature cap of about 4×10⁴ on SiO₂.
- The review's own [32] (Morozov 2008) says mobilities above 200,000 are achievable once extrinsic disorder is removed.
- Nair 2008 measured πα = 2.3 % for white light. 2500 nm is near-IR, not far-IR.
- Du 2008 reports suspended graphene with mobility above 100,000 near the Dirac point.

DERIVED FOR FABLE: τ = μE_F/(e v_F²) = 20 m²/Vs × 0.1167 V / 10¹² m²/s² = 2.33 ps, giving Q = 14.7 at 1 THz.

BEARING: this is the only number in the review that maps onto a Fable row. It is already_in_record — see the lifetime/Q row in the mapping.

outline.section: §2.1 Basic parameters — Kubo conductivity, TE/TM modes, λsp (Eqs. 3–7; pp. 4–6)
outline.content_summary:
CONTENT:
- Kubo intraband + interband conductivity (Eq. 3). The Drude τ is 'set as 10⁻¹³', with units printed as s⁻¹.
- Carrier density–chemical potential relation (Eqs. 4–5).
- Intraband response dominates from the THz to the far-IR; interband dominates in the visible/NIR.
- TE modes are tied to interband and TM modes to intraband conductivity (Hanson 2008a [66]); Eq. 6 gives both dispersions.
- Eq. 7: λsp = λ0·e²/(πε0ħc)·μc/(εr1+εr2)·1/(ħ(ω+i/τ)), i.e. 4α·E_F/((εr1+εr2)ħω) — the unscreened √q branch.
- The review says graphene is like noble metals but with relatively small losses, citing [76–85].

FIGURE SOURCES: Fig. 5a,b are conductivity maps over 10–50 THz from Vakil & Engheta [74]. Fig. 5d is HREELS on SiC graphene at n ~2×10¹³ (Liu 2008 [77]). Fig. 5e shows the RPA dispersion and the Landau-damping regions (Hwang & Das Sarma 2007 [78]).

OTHER WORKS IN THE RANGE:
- Hanson 2008b [69]: quasi-TEM modes of a graphene parallel-plate waveguide, with attenuation similar to metal guides.
- Tan 2007 [68].
- Gao 2012 [70] = [85]: a duplicated FDTD grating-coupler paper.
- Chen & Alù cloak [75].
- Jablan 2009 [76]: low loss below ħω_Oph ≈ 0.2 eV, using the DC relaxation time as input.
- Reviews [79], [82], [83]; sensing [80]; emitter–ribbon coupling [84].
- Thermo-optic LRSPP modulator at telecom (Kim 2013 [81]): 30 dB with 12 mW.

DERIVED:
- τ = 10⁻¹³ s gives Q = 0.63 at 1 THz — overdamped.
- Eq. 7 at Fable's point (E_F 116.7 meV, ħω 4.136 meV, air + sapphire ε 1 + 9.4) gives λsp = 23.7 µm. That is ×10.2 the acoustic 2.33 µm, and a quarter-wave cell of ≈5.9 µm instead of 576 nm.

BEARING:
- The unscreened mode is not_applicable; it makes a worse bit (prior session: 54.6/Q dB per λ, DS threshold at τ ≈ 6–15 ps).
- Already in record: DC τ below the optical-phonon onset, interband blocking and the Landau-damping boundaries (Part I §1 lines 97–100, §5 lines 568–574, §7.5 line 1355 — interband absorption below 0.001 dB).
- Hanson [69] is the classical parallel-plate precursor of the gated quasi-TEM picture that Part I Eq. (1) refines. It is in the record in substance but not cited.

outline.section: §2.3 Bilayer graphene — domain walls, gapped bilayer, gain (pp. 7–8)
outline.content_summary:
DOMAIN-WALL REFLECTION — Jiang 2016 [96]: near-field IR imaging with a 10.6 µm laser (28.3 THz, derived). Plasmons reflect at stacking domain walls, and the reflection depends on the soliton type (tensile vs shear) and on the gate.

DOMAIN-WALL PLASMONS — Hasdeo & Song 2017 (list [98]; the review cites it as [97]). Theory:
- Domain-wall plasmons in dual-gated gapped bilayer live orders of magnitude longer than the bulk transport time.
- At room temperature the lifetime reaches up to a few ps; the modes exist even at zero bulk density and extend up to the mid-IR.
- The reproduced Fig. 7d is at ħω = 60 meV = 14.5 THz (derived). No 1-THz value was found.

RESONANT GAIN — Low, Chen & Basov 2018 (list [97]; the review cites it as [98] and calls it 'Wang et al.'). Theory:
- An AB bilayer with a gap larger than the optical-phonon energy acts as an active medium.
- It gives resonant optical gain near the asymmetry gap, amplified plasmons with negative group velocity, superluminal effects and leaky modes.
- The population must be inverted (Fig. 7f: Δ = 0.2 eV, μe = −μh = 0.3 eV), so gain sits at ≥ ~48 THz (derived from 0.2 eV).

REST OF THE RANGE [99–110]:
- Double-layer graphene in-phase and out-of-phase (acoustic) modes: Stauber & Gómez-Santos 2012 [99]; Hwang & Das Sarma 2009 [106]; Profumo 2012 [104] (acoustic modes); Badalyan 2012 [109]; de la Cruz 2015, metallic substrate [110] (DOI 10.1016/j.ssc.2015.03.021; abstract not found); Bagheri 2014, acoustic mode in double-layer ribbons [105].
- Dual-gated bilayer at 300 K and THz (Farzaneh & Rakheja 2017 [100], theory): an energy gap lengthens TM propagation.
- Also: AA stacking or B field [101, 103], bilayer screening [102], nanodisks [107], cylinders [108].

BEARING:
- The double-layer acoustic modes are the review's closest content to Fable's gate-screened mode, but they are only listed, never discussed. Their physics is already_in_record in substance through Part I Eq. (1).
- Gain by population inversion: not_applicable at 1 THz.
- Domain-wall plasmons: alternative_route, theory only.
- Caridad 2024 states that bilayer graphene's intrinsic room-temperature mobility is ~15,000 cm²/Vs, against >60,000 measured in its monolayer device.

outline.content_summary:

At liquid-nitrogen temperature the intrinsic propagation length exceeds 10 µm, or 50 λp, which implies λp ≈ 0.2 µm (derived). The review adds a lifetime up to 1.6 ps (paywalled body, not verified) and confinement below one-sixth of λ0 (not found; conflicts with λp ≈ 0.2 µm at a mid-IR λ0).

CITED WORKS:
- Liu 2011 [181]: metal-plasmon-enhanced multicolour graphene photodetectors; external quantum efficiency enhanced by up to 1,500 %.
- Nikitin 2011 [182], THz theory placed in this range without discussion: in ribbons, the even-parity hybridized edge mode is the fundamental, lowest-loss mode, and loss has a frequency minimum.
- Yu 2016 [183]: Si quantum dot/graphene Schottky photodetectors.
- Ni 2017 [184]: B-doped Si quantum dot/graphene phototransistor; up to ~10⁹ A/W, gain ~10¹², ~10¹³ Jones. The review adds 45 A/W and 10⁵ Jones in the mid-IR over 375 nm–4 µm (body not verified).

2021–2026 SUPERSEDERS:

CITED WORKS:
- Shi 2016 (list [188]; the review cites it as [187], which is Yan 2012's magneto-plasmon paper). Simulated band-stop filter from a periodically modulated chemical potential: centre tunable over 37–53 THz with −26 dB depth and 3.1 THz bandwidth held fixed; length ~750 nm ≈ λ0/9.

- Pan 2017 [190], theory: topologically protected plasmons at 2 T.
- Xiong 2019 [191], experiment: continuous graphene over a back gate with a nano-patterned SiO₂ gate insulator (80-nm lattice). The gate opens and closes a plasmonic bandgap, the LDOS varies up to 16×, and an artificial domain wall carries 1D modes. Measured at 60 K and 904 cm⁻¹ (27.1 THz, derived), λp = 160 nm; Q ≈ 100 at low temperature and ≈25 at room temperature, which the authors themselves judge unsatisfactory at ambient.

BEARING:
- These show that gate-defined periodic density maps can make plasmonic bandgaps, reflectors and guided domain-wall channels — the principle behind Part I §3.1/§9.4. Already_in_record in concept, not cited.
- But they are cryogenic, mid-IR and unscreened, and give no junction transmission for a gated 1-THz mode: unknown.

THz SUPERSEDER (not in the review): Tu et al. 2019/2020 — a ZnO dual gate continuously controls THz plasmon reflection at density boundaries and makes programmable cavities. It appears only in ERRATA I-41.

Graphene is a tunable loss/feedback element, not the gain medium. The review's description (GaAs 'quantum dots', a 'cantilever beam') does not match the abstract. review_claims.claim:
The abstract says graphene SPPs combine “high carrier mobility, strong localization, low consumption and high tunability” (Cui, Wang & Sun 2021, abstract). It lists applications in optical information transmission (the abstract's word is 'knowledge', sic), photodetectors, SPP waveguides, metamaterials and nanolasers.
CHECK: none of the five is developed at 1 THz and 300 K. 'Low consumption' is never quantified: there is no energy-per-bit, loss-per-length or power figure anywhere in the review.

The review puts room-temperature, phonon-limited mobility as high as 2.0×10⁵ cm²/Vs at 10¹² cm⁻², citing Novoselov 2005 [18].
CHECK: the figure is Chen et al. 2008's acoustic-phonon intrinsic limit (arXiv:0711.3646, posted 2007-11-23): 2×10⁵ at 10¹², mean free path >2 µm, ~30 Ω intrinsic resistivity, while SiO₂ caps room-temperature mobility near 4×10⁴. The review does not cite it. Its own [32], Morozov 2008 (arXiv:0710.5304), says >200,000 is reachable once extrinsic disorder is removed.
DERIVED: τ = μE_F/(e v_F²) = 2.33 ps, so Q = 14.7 at 1 THz.

The review gives a mean free path of up to about 1 µm and near-ballistic transport, citing Du 2008 [19].
CHECK: Du 2008 (arXiv:0802.2933, 2008-02-20) reports suspended graphene with mobility above 100,000 cm²/Vs near the Dirac point. Chen 2008 gives an acoustic-phonon mean free path above 2 µm at 10¹². The review's 1 µm has no source in the cited abstracts.

The review says graphene absorbs 2.3 % of normal-incidence light from 300 to 2500 nm, which it calls UV to far-IR. It adds that saturable absorption implies a strong nonlinearity, and that below 2E_F Pauli blocking leaves only intraband response from the mid-IR to the THz.
CHECK: Nair 2008 (arXiv:0803.3718, 2008-03-26) gives πα = 2.3 % of white light. 2500 nm is near-IR, not far-IR. The Pauli-blocking point agrees with Part I §7.5, where interband absorption at ħω ≪ 2E_F adds under 0.001 dB.

The review reports that graphene plasmons were imaged in real space with wavelength ~200 nm, travel several wavelengths, and have gate-tunable wavelength and amplitude (Fei 2012 [52]).
CHECK: this matches Fei 2012 (arXiv:1202.4993, 2012-02-22): mid-IR, graphene/SiO₂/Si, λp of order 200 nm. But the review says the measurement used inelastic electron scattering and inelastic STM; Fei used infrared nano-imaging. The Fig. 4 data are at 892 cm⁻¹ = 26.7 THz (derived).

The review sets the Kubo/Drude relaxation time to 10⁻¹³, printing the units as s⁻¹ (meaning 100 fs).
DERIVED: at 1 THz this gives Q = ωτ = 0.63, an overdamped plasmon. Fable's best-case row is τ = 1 ps, Q = 6.3.

The review says graphene behaves like a noble metal but with relatively small propagation losses ([76]–[85]), a point it repeats for IR/THz graphene SPPs in §2.6.
CHECK: no normalization is given. At 1 THz Fable's acoustic plasmon loses 27.3/Q = 4.3 dB per 2.33 µm, about 1,860 dB/mm, against 1–10 dB/mm for metal THz guides (prior SPP session, deck\spp_assessment.md). Per unit length at THz the statement is false. Fei 2012 claims superiority only on confinement-normalized figures of merit in the mid-IR.

Eq. (7) gives λsp = λ0·e²/(πε0ħc)·μc/(εr1+εr2)·1/(ħ(ω+i/τ)), i.e. λsp/λ0 = 4α·E_F/((εr1+εr2)ħω). This is the unscreened √q branch, consistent with Koppens 2011 (arXiv:1104.2068).
DERIVED at Fable's point (E_F 116.7 meV, 1 THz, air/sapphire with ε = 1 + 9.4 from Part I §3.1): λsp = 23.7 µm, ×10.2 the gated 2.33 µm, for a quarter-wave cell of ≈5.9 µm instead of 576 nm. The gate-screened branch that Fable uses never appears in the review.
review_claims.where: §2.1, p.6 (Eq. 7, checked on the page image)

review_claims.claim:
The review says ribbon resonances follow an edge-phase Fabry–Pérot formula (Eq. 8) and that coupling between ribbons matters below about 500 nm separation (Du 2014 [86]).
CHECK: Du 2014 is mid-IR full-wave simulation (OpenAlex abstract, 2014-09-11): near-total edge reflection with a ~0.27π phase jump.

The review calls Ju 2011 [87] the first experimental graphene-plasmon metamaterial, with THz resonances tuned by ribbon width and gating, and attributes it to 'Wang et al.'.
CHECK: Europe PMC PMID 21892164 (2011-09-04) confirms broad THz tuning by width and electrostatic doping, with prominent room-temperature absorption. The reproduced Fig. 6e,f peaks near 100–200 cm⁻¹ (3–6 THz, derived) at 1.5×10¹³ cm⁻². The caption's '4 mm' should be 4 µm, and Fig. 12f mislabels these THz data as mid-IR.

The review says graphene plasmon-induced-transparency structures have lower loss and stronger confinement than noble-metal ones (Zhao 2016 [88]).
CHECK: Zhao 2016 is a numerical THz design (OpenAlex abstract) and gives no loss comparison.

The review cites [97] for domain-wall plasmons in gapped bilayer graphene that propagate along topological domain walls and live picoseconds even at room temperature.
CHECK: the work is Hasdeo & Song 2017, which is the list's [98] (arXiv:1706.00790, 2017-06-02). It is theory: lifetimes orders of magnitude above the bulk transport time, up to a few ps at room temperature, even at zero bulk density, up to the mid-IR. The reproduced Fig. 7d is at ħω = 60 meV = 14.5 THz (derived). No 1-THz value was found.

The review credits 'Wang et al.' [98] with predicting resonant optical gain near the gap of gapped bilayer graphene, giving amplified plasmons with negative group velocity and superluminal effects.
CHECK: the work is Low, Chen & Basov 2018, which is the list's [97] (arXiv:1712.09924, 2017-12-28; PRB 98, 041403). It is theory and needs a population-inverted AB bilayer with a gap above the optical-phonon energy; Fig. 7f uses Δ = 0.2 eV and μe = −μh = 0.3 eV. The gain therefore sits at ≥ ~48 THz (derived). It is neither a 1-THz nor a drift mechanism, and the author attribution is wrong.

The review says the twisted-bilayer plasmon wavelength rises and damping falls with twist angle (Hu 2017 [124]), and that the twist angle sets plasmon-generation efficiency, which falls to 20 % of its maximum ([126]).
CHECK:
- Hu 2017 (arXiv:2301.11646, for PRL 119, 247402): mid-IR near-field imaging; at larger angles λp is longer with apparently lower damping, attributed to Fermi-velocity renormalization.
- de Vega & García de Abajo 2019 (arXiv:1812.10109, 2018-12-25): theory; efficiency ~20 % at 4°, and metal|insulator|graphene tunnelling generation several orders of magnitude weaker than double-layer graphene.

The review says ABA trilayer graphene has optical (√q) and acoustical (linear-in-q, ∝ √d) plasmons (Eq. 11, [128]). It reports that bilayer ribbons resonate most strongly and trilayer no more (Emani 2015 [129]), that multilayers matter most, and that experiments are more useful than simulations.
CHECK: Emani 2015 (OpenAlex, 2015-10-26) confirms double layer > single layer and triple layer not above double layer, from IR microscopy. Eq. 11's acoustical branch is the same √d acoustic-plasmon physics as Fable's Eq. (1) (Part I line 1870). The in-text [127] is really Krstajić 2013, which is [128].

The review says the inverse-coupled multilayer supermode has the lowest loss and shortest wavelength, that loss falls with layer number, spacing and μc, that multilayers suit low-loss waveguides and deep-subwavelength imaging, and that supermode fields help modulation and photocatalysis.
CHECK: Qin 2014 (OpenAlex, 2014-10-09) is simulation; loss falls with layer number N and saturates near 5 layers. The modulation and photocatalysis remarks have no support in the cited abstracts.
DERIVED for a gated cell: N decoupled sheets raise s and λp by √N (576 → 815 nm at N = 2), leave per-gate loss unchanged and raise Joule density ×N².

The review says, without citation, that graphene plasmons compress light to a third of its wavelength.
CHECK: unsupported. The review's own §4 says λ0/40, Chen 2012 says more than 40× shorter, and Fable's gated mode is λ0/129.

For hBN-encapsulated graphene at low temperature (Ni 2018 [146]), the review reports fringes several µm long, a lifetime up to 1.6 ps, confinement below one-sixth of λ0, and loss set by the encapsulant rather than electron scattering.
CHECK: the Europe PMC abstract (PMID 29795255, 2018-05-23) confirms cryogenic imaging, encapsulant dielectric loss as the dominant channel, and >10 µm = 50 λp at liquid-nitrogen temperature, so λp ≈ 0.2 µm (derived). The 1.6 ps sits in the paywalled body and was not verified. The one-sixth figure is not found and conflicts with λp ≈ 0.2 µm. This paper is already Part I [42].

The review says plasmon–phonon (SP3) modes barely suffer ohmic loss and propagate farther than plain graphene plasmons (SP2), citing Dai 2015 [148] and Kumar 2015 [149].
CHECK: Dai 2015 (2015-06-22) finds graphene/hBN hyperbolic plasmon–phonon modes propagate 1.5–2.0× farther than hBN's own phonon polaritons. The comparison is with phonon polaritons, not with SP2. This is mid-IR Reststrahlen physics, which Part I §1 places outside 1 THz.
The review's own verdict: graphene-plasmon metamaterial research is still mostly theory and simulation, because micro/nano fabrication is immature.

The review cites Ni 2017 [184] for ~10⁹ A/W and ~10¹³ Jones from UV to NIR, 45 A/W and 10⁵ Jones in the mid-IR, over 375 nm–4 µm. It cites Chen 2017 [185] for Au nanoparticles raising short-wave-IR absorption about tenfold, with high responsivity and super-fast response.
CHECK:
- Ni 2017 (2017-09-22) confirms up to ~10⁹ A/W, gain ~10¹² and ~10¹³ Jones; the mid-IR figures are in the body and were not verified.
- Chen 2017 (2017-01-12) gives 83 A/W at 1.55 µm with a rise time under 600 ns — not fast on a 14.5-ps slot scale.

The review cites Guo 2020 [186] for Si–graphene hybrid plasmonic waveguide photodetectors: >20 GHz and ~70 mA/W at 2 µm; >40 GHz and ~0.4 A/W at 1.55 µm.
CHECK: PMC7048841 (2020-02-28) confirms both, with the bandwidths limited by the test setup and −0.3 V bias at 1.55 µm. The mechanism is bolometric/photoconductive.

The review cites Shi et al. as [187] for a gate-modulated graphene filter tunable over 37–53 THz, with ~26 dB depth and 3.1 THz bandwidth held fixed.
CHECK: the work is Shi 2016 Sci. Rep., which is the list's [188] (PMC4882757, 2016-05-27). It is a transfer-matrix/numerical design (−26 dB, 3.1 THz, ~750 nm ≈ λ0/9). The list's [187] is Yan 2012's magneto-plasmon paper.

The review describes B-field topological one-way edge plasmons (Jin 2017 [189]) and a gate-tunable plasmonic photonic crystal with LDOS varying up to 16× and an engineered domain wall carrying 1D modes (Xiong 2019 [191]).
CHECK:
- Jin 2017 (OpenAlex, 2017-06-16) is theory, with mid-gap frequencies up to tens of THz under a static B field.
- Xiong 2019 (PMC6803641, 2019-10-21) measured at 60 K and 904 cm⁻¹ (27.1 THz, derived), with an 80-nm lattice and λp = 160 nm. Q is ≈100 at low temperature and ≈25 at room temperature; the authors call ambient performance not fully satisfactory.

The review describes a ZnO–graphene superlattice giving a thresholdless, room-temperature, tunable Raman nanolaser from visible to NIR (Zhu 2017 [192]).
CHECK: the abstract (Adv. Mater., online 2016-11-09) confirms room-temperature operation from visible to near-IR.

The review states that Apalkov & Stockman's quantum-cascade graphene nanospaser [193] will be the world's first electrically excited graphene-plasmon laser.
CHECK: the source (LSA 3, e191, 2014-07-18; OpenAlex) is a mid-IR proposal and claims the first-ever status only if the device is experimentally realized. The review drops that condition.

The review describes a laser tuned by gating graphene that replaces gold, built from GaAs quantum dots, a gold waveguide, polymer electrolyte and a 'cantilever beam' (Chakraborty 2016 [194]; Polini 2016 [195]).
CHECK: the abstract (PMID 26816373) describes graphene plasmons in an aperiodic-lattice THz quantum cascade laser, where E_F is tied to round-trip gain through the photon lifetime. Graphene is a tunable loss/feedback element, not the gain medium. Quantum dots and a cantilever do not appear. The operating temperature was not found in the accessible text.

The outlook claims extreme confinement, λGP ≈ λ0/40 (Chen 2012 [53]), gate tunability and low mid-IR loss, with excitation by nearby dipoles, near-field tips or charges at hybrid boundaries.
CHECK: Chen 2012 (arXiv:1202.4996, 2012-02-22) gives a plasmon wavelength more than 40× shorter, but for mid-IR, unscreened modes launched by a tip. Fable's gated mode is already λ0/129, ×3.2 tighter (derived).

The outlook predicts better devices from combining graphene with other low-dimensional materials, metamaterials, metal particles or 2D materials, citing [196]–[198].
CHECK: [196] is a carbon-quantum-dot bioimaging synthesis (self-citation), [197] an interfacial charge-transfer exciton study (self-citation), and [198] a photosystem-I/Au-nanoparticle graphene-FET photosensor. None is a graphene-plasmon device result, and the outlook sets no quantitative target.

WHAT THE REVIEW NEVER COVERS:
- The gate-screened (acoustic) mode — Alcaraz Iranzo 2018 [151] sits only inside a citation range, and double-layer acoustic modes are only listed ([99]–[110]).
- Drift, DC current, Dyakonov–Shur or hydrodynamic plasmons; only [34] on viscosity, never discussed.
- Propagating THz plasmons at 300 K.
- On-chip electrical launch or readout of plasmons.
- Loss per length, energy per operation, speed of a plasmonic element, logic or information processing.
Verified by term search of the body: 'drift' 0, 'Dyakonov' 0, 'information' 0, 'logic' only inside 'topological'/'biological', 'acoustical' once (Eq. 11).
